The aircraft weathervaned into the wind, exited the runway, and sustained substantial right wing damage after striking a ditch and a two-foot deep rut.

synopsis: A private pilot operating a Grumman G-164A Agcat (RA-1398G) suffered minor injuries after a forced landing near Volgodonsk, Russia, caused by a loss of engine power. The aircraft was substantially damaged during this local flight.
summary: A private pilot operating a Grumman G-164A Agcat (RA-1398G) suffered minor injuries after a forced landing near Volgodonsk, Russia, caused by a loss of engine power. The aircraft was substantially damaged during this local flight.

synopsis: The student pilot's inadequate directional control during the landing roll.
summary: A student pilot performing a touch-and-go landing experienced a left drift, applied right rudder, and nosed over, damaging the vertical stabilizer and rudder. Examination indicated excessive side loading caused the steering rod separation, with no pre-impact mechanical anomalies found.

synopsis: The airplane's inability to establish a climb for undetermined reasons, which resulted in a collision with trees.
summary: The pilot and two passengers departed a private airstrip when the aircraft descended into trees shortly after takeoff. Although the pilot suspected engine power loss or windshear, physical evidence indicated the engine was producing power, and the cause of the descent was undetermined.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control as result of the gusting wind.
summary: A cargo pilot delayed taxiing due to strong winds but was struck by a gust before shutting down, causing the aircraft's nose to swing left and the right wing to lift. The resulting ground impact bent the right wing and damaged the propeller during 36-knot winds gusting to 48 knots.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
summary: During a fourth practice three-point landing in a tailwheel airplane, the pilot lost directional control and exited the runway. Despite applying full right rudder and power, the aircraft pivoted, causing the left main gear to collapse and the left wing to strike the ground, resulting in substantial damage with no reported mechanical failure.

synopsis: The pilot's controlled flight into terrain while conducting a flight at low altitude in instrument meteorological conditions.
summary: During a cross-country flight in rain and thunderstorms, a pilot flew at low altitude in reduced visibility and impacted a lake. The aircraft was not recovered, but fragmented wreckage and illegal narcotics were found, consistent with controlled flight into terrain.

synopsis: A loss of electrical and engine power for undetermined reasons.
summary: The pilot experienced electrical system failures and engine power loss during initial climb, forcing a lake landing. Post-recovery examinations found no anomalies in the electrical system or a cause for the engine power loss.

synopsis: The pilot of an Embraer EMB-202 (PT-UPW) experienced a loss of power during cruise while flying from Joacaba to Ponta Grossa. The aircraft landed in a soybean field near Guarau with no injuries to the pilot and no damage to the airplane.
summary: The pilot of an Embraer EMB-202 (PT-UPW) experienced a loss of power during cruise while flying from Joacaba to Ponta Grossa. The aircraft landed in a soybean field near Guarau with no injuries to the pilot and no damage to the airplane.

synopsis: The pilot did not maintain control of the airplane during initial climb, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's lack of recent flight experience.
summary: The pilot of an experimental amateur-built aircraft lost control during the initial climb of its first flight, resulting in a ground impact 800 feet from the runway. Post-accident examination found no mechanical failures, while records showed the builder-pilot had only 3 hours of flight time in the preceding six months.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control while landing with a crosswind, which resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: While approaching the destination airport, the pilot landed on runway 28 behind another aircraft practicing crosswind landings. During the landing roll, she relaxed crosswind correction inputs, causing the airplane to veer off the left side of the runway, collapse the nosegear, and sustain firewall damage.

synopsis: Fatigue failure of the right flap extend cable during the landing approach.
summary: During the downwind leg, a pilot experienced a right flap cable failure causing asymmetric deployment and an 80-degree roll, requiring constant left aileron input to land safely. Post-incident inspection revealed fatigue fractures in 36-year-old cables that were undetectable without removal, a known issue prompting a new service bulletin.

synopsis: The pilot's operation of the helicopter at a low-forward airspeed out of ground effect, which resulted in the helicopter's loss of translational lift and tail rotor authority and the pilot's subsequent loss of helicopter control.
summary: A pilot with 41 hours in the model flew a single-engine helicopter with a film crew in an urban area. The aircraft impacted a building after the pilot likely lost translational lift and tail rotor authority while performing flat turns at low airspeed out of ground effect.

synopsis: The failure of the pilot to initiate a go-around and his excessive airspeed on the final landing approach.
summary: The pilot executed a high-speed landing on a wet grass runway after a wind shift, causing the aircraft to overrun the end. The right wing struck a fence and the airplane came to rest in a field with no reported pre-impact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing and the pilot's inadequate remedial action, which resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: A student pilot and private pilot landed at a destination airport where the student applied uneven brakes, causing the airplane to veer left and strike runway lights. After the student added full power, the aircraft departed the runway and collided with a tree, sustaining left wing structural damage.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control of the airplane for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination of the airplane did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: Witnesses observed a local flight pitching up, rolling right, and spiraling into terrain, resulting in a postimpact fire. Postaccident examination found a failed flap control rod end and trace Diphenhydramine in the pilot, but neither was determined to have caused the accident.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the aborted takeoff.
summary: The pilot unintentionally took off during a fast taxi, aborted the takeoff, and lost directional control upon touchdown. The aircraft struck a fence, sustaining substantial wing damage, with the pilot reporting no mechanical deficiencies.

synopsis: The pilot's misjudgment of the landing area, which resulted in the airplane touching down on a grass area adjacent to the runway and between parallel taxiways.
summary: The pilot, cleared to land on runway 1L, misjudged the approach and landed off the runway in the grass between taxiways A and B, striking an airport sign. This caused substantial damage to the airplane, with the pilot noting no mechanical failures prior to the accident.

synopsis: A loss of clearance between the tail rotor drive shaft and the tailboom bulkhead for undetermined reasons, which resulted in the overstress failure of the drive shaft.
summary: The helicopter pilot experienced pedal vibration and lost directional control, forcing an autorotation that damaged the left skid and fuselage. A postaccident exam found the tail rotor drive shaft failed from an overstress fracture caused by contact with the tailboom bulkhead, though the root cause of this contact remained undetermined.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
summary: During approach and landing in 13-knot gusting crosswinds, turbulence from hangars caused the aircraft to touch down left-wing low. The left wing lifted during rollout, causing the airplane to weathervan and strike the ground with the right wing and tail, resulting in substantial damage with no mechanical failure reported.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to exit the runway while still traveling at an excessive speed and his subsequent loss of directional control.
summary: The pilot of an experimental tailwheel airplane tipped onto its left wing during a crosswind taxiway turn after landing, causing gear and wing damage from excessive side loads. The pilot attributed the accident to a wind gust catching the wing and noted it could have been prevented by slowing earlier or continuing to the next taxiway.

synopsis: The pilot's improper response to a loss of power in the No. 2 engine and his failure to ensure that the airplane was airworthy. Contributing to the accident was the inadequate engine maintenance by the operator's maintenance personnel.
summary: The pilot, who was also the company chief, crashed a twin-engine aircraft shortly after takeoff due to a No. 2 engine failure caused by corrosion and poor maintenance. The accident occurred because the pilot did not execute single-engine procedures despite the engine's inability to produce full power.

synopsis: the early rotation of the airplane to an angle at which the fuselage contacted the runway. Contributing to early rotation was the Captain's reaction to the erroneous V1 automated callout, likely assuming that the airplane was at or close to the correct Vr at the same time. The erroneous automated callout was likely due to a keystroke entry error by the FO when manually entering takeoff data for a newly assigned departure runway.
summary: The First Officer manually entered an incorrect V1 of 123 knots into the B737-800's FMC after a runway change, likely due to a keystroke error. The Captain rotated at this erroneous speed, causing a tailstrike and substantial damage to the lower rear fuselage.

synopsis: A Robinson R22 helicopter with a pilot and observer was destroyed after impacting power lines and the ground while inspecting pipelines in mountainous terrain near Sulmona, Italy. Both crew members were fatally injured during this flight operating under Italian regulations.
summary: A Robinson R22 helicopter with a pilot and observer was destroyed after impacting power lines and the ground while inspecting pipelines in mountainous terrain near Sulmona, Italy. Both crew members were fatally injured during this flight operating under Italian regulations.

synopsis: A Robinson R44 Raven II helicopter, D-HBLT, collided with a storage hangar at Straubing-Wallmühle Airport, destroying the aircraft in a post-accident fire. The pilot and passenger sustained minor injuries, and the investigation remains under German jurisdiction.
summary: A Robinson R44 Raven II helicopter, D-HBLT, collided with a storage hangar at Straubing-Wallmühle Airport, destroying the aircraft in a post-accident fire. The pilot and passenger sustained minor injuries, and the investigation remains under German jurisdiction.

synopsis: A Ryanair Boeing 737-800 experienced multiple electrical problems while airborne en route from Stockholm-Skavsta to Beauvais-Tillé. The crew returned to Stockholm for an uneventful landing with no injuries or aircraft damage.
summary: A Ryanair Boeing 737-800 experienced multiple electrical problems while airborne en route from Stockholm-Skavsta to Beauvais-Tillé. The crew returned to Stockholm for an uneventful landing with no injuries or aircraft damage.

synopsis: The overstress fracture of the right aileron midspan hinge bracket due to modal vibrations created by a deflated right main landing gear tire during the takeoff roll.
summary: During takeoff roll at 70 knots, the pilot aborted after the aircraft pulled right due to a blown right main tire. The resulting vibration caused overstress failure of the right aileron midspan hinge bracket, buckling the aileron.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from power lines.
summary: A gyrocopter departed a private airstrip and struck a telephone line shortly after becoming airborne, causing it to descend and impact a road. A postimpact fire resulted in substantial damage, though examination revealed no mechanical anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.

synopsis: The instructor pilot did not maintain adequate helicopter control while maneuvering, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: An instructor pilot conducted night helicopter training flights involving autorotations and simulated failures. Although the pilot reported no hard landings, post-flight inspection revealed tailboom and gearbox damage plus fresh ground-contact marks on the tail guard consistent with a hard landing.

aircraft: Franke Harry C AVID FLYER B
synopsis: The pilot's failure to hold full power for takeoff.
summary: The pilot reported that during the initial climb at 65 feet, the engine lost power because the throttle friction was loose, allowing the throttle to roll back to idle. This caused a hard forced landing that resulted in substantial fuselage damage, with the pilot stating no mechanical failures occurred.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of aircraft control during landing in gusty wind conditions.
summary: During final approach, the pilot flying encountered gusty winds causing airspeed fluctuations and a left roll upon flare. Despite applying full opposite aileron, the left wing impacted the runway, resulting in substantial damage to the outboard forward wing spar.

synopsis: The loss of engine power due to the unintentional closure of the fuel shutoff valve.
summary: A helicopter pilot experienced engine power loss at low altitude when a passenger inadvertently moved the fuel shutoff valve, causing the aircraft to settle and roll onto its right side. The pilot could not autorotate in time, and the accident was attributed to the older valve design allowing accidental actuation.

synopsis: The loss of aircraft control and subsequent impact with terrain for undetermined reasons.
summary: The pilot departed the local airport and climbed to 1,200 feet MSL before descending to 200 feet MSL and impacting the ground with substantial damage. Postaccident examination found no mechanical anomalies, and the reason for the loss of control was not determined.

synopsis: The pilot's excessive application of the brakes, which caused the airplane to nose over.
summary: During a full-stop landing, the pilot aggressively applied brakes while rolling fast with 300 to 400 feet of runway remaining. This action lifted the tail, causing the propeller to strike the ground, flip the aircraft inverted, and substantially damage the vertical stabilizer and wings.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the takeoff roll.
summary: The pilot lost directional control while attempting takeoff on runway 24 after prematurely lifting the tailwheel at 200 feet. The aircraft veered left, struck a runway light, and sustained substantial damage to the right wing and fuselage when the right main gear separated.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate clearance from the wheat crop during takeoff.
summary: The pilot of an aerial-application helicopter settled into a wheat crop shortly after takeoff while accelerating through translational lift due to a wind gust. The aircraft pitched down when spray booms contacted the crop and collided with terrain, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate directional control while landing in a variable crosswind.
summary: The pilot landed with a 6-knot left crosswind, but the aircraft veered left and departed the runway into soft grass despite full right rudder and brake application. Post-accident inspection found no mechanical failures, though wind speeds increased to 17-knot gusts shortly after the event.

synopsis: The student pilot's improper flare, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: A student pilot on his third solo flight flared too steeply during landing, triggering a stall warning before impacting the runway. The nosewheel buckled and the right rudder pedal jammed, causing the aircraft to veer off the runway into a grass apron with substantial firewall damage.

aircraft: Pfouts Alfred L SENIOR AERO SPT D260
synopsis: A total loss of engine power for undetermined reasons.
summary: The pilot reported engine power loss and a forced landing into trees after fuel pressure dropped twice, despite an electric boost pump installed the day prior. Investigation found no fuel in the gascolator but no mechanical pump anomalies, leaving fuel starvation as the likely but unconfirmed cause.

synopsis: An in-flight smoke event on takeoff and the pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
summary: The pilot reported cockpit smoke during initial climb after a right-turn departure clearance. The aircraft subsequently stalled and crashed into trees while executing a low-altitude turn back to the airport, resulting in a post-impact fire that consumed the structure.

synopsis: A loose fuel line fitting, which caused a fuel leak and subsequent in-flight fire.
summary: During a Phase 1 test flight of an experimental amateur-built airplane, the pilot encountered a fire caused by a loose fuel line fitting at the mechanical fuel pump. After extinguishing the fire and opening the door, the pilot executed a forced landing on an uphill slope, resulting in substantial damage to the fuselage and right wing.

synopsis: A loss of engine power due to fuel starvation as a result of the pilot's improper fuel management.
summary: During an aerial pipeline patrol, the pilot's fuel transfer pump failed, causing engine sputter and a forced landing. The aircraft struck tree branches and flipped, sustaining substantial damage to the right wing, fuselage, and vertical stabilizer.

synopsis: The student pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: A student pilot executed a hard nose landing and bounced during the landing phase, prompting a successful go-around. Subsequent inspection by another pilot and maintenance revealed a bent propeller blade tip and a buckled engine firewall, leading to the aircraft's early return.

synopsis: The pilot's controlled flight into terrain for undetermined reasons.
summary: The pilot departed an aerial application work area when the airplane collided with the ground at high speed, causing serious injuries. GPS data showed increasing airspeed and decreasing altitude, consistent with a controlled flight into terrain for undetermined reasons, with no preimpact mechanical abnormalities found.

synopsis: The pilot's improper in-flight fuel management, which resulted in a loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
summary: The pilot declared a fuel emergency during a cross-country flight, but the aircraft impacted a field three miles short of the runway. Investigation found 20 gallons in the right tank while the selector remained on the empty left tank, though the reason for not switching tanks was undetermined.

synopsis: The pilot did not maintain adequate airspeed during takeoff, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
summary: The pilot reported an engine power loss and stall warning immediately after liftoff from a dirt strip, causing the aircraft to bank right and impact a field. Although the pilot attributed the crash to engine failure, propeller damage indicated power was present at impact, and no pre-impact mechanical anomalies were found.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during a touch-and-go landing.
summary: A student pilot aborted a takeoff during the landing roll of a touch-and-go when the aircraft veered right after applying right rudder and power. The nose gear collapsed, causing substantial fuselage and firewall damage, though the pilot reported no mechanical malfunctions.

aircraft: Czech Sport Aircraft As Piper Sport
synopsis: The pilot's inadvertent application of control inputs that resulted in rapid, right-rolling, negative g-forces during night cruise flight and his subsequent ejection from the airplane. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision to fly at night in an airplane not approved for night flight, his unbuckling of the seat belt portion of the restraint harness, and the inadvertent opening of the airplane's canopy.
summary: The pilot of a light sport airplane, not approved for night operations, was ejected after inadvertently applying rapid control inputs during a night flight. The ejection likely resulted from the canopy unlatching due to a loose harness riser or headset wire while the pilot attempted to access the back shelf.

synopsis: A bearing failure in the engine's supercharger section, which resulted in a total loss of engine power during flight. Contributing to the accident was the soft soil of the forced landing site.
summary: During an aerial application flight, the pilot executed a forced landing after total engine power loss caused by seized supercharger bearings. The aircraft nosed over in soft soil, damaging the left wing and vertical section, with no recent maintenance records indicating the bearing failure.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate visual lookout resulting in a collision with power lines while making an off-airport landing.
summary: The glider pilot, competing in a soaring event, attempted an off-airport landing in a hay field due to weakening thermals from cirrus clouds. The aircraft struck two electrical transmission lines 15 feet above ground on final approach, sustaining substantial damage to the fuselage and wing.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the takeoff roll.
summary: A student pilot reported that during the takeoff roll, the aircraft departed the runway to the left, causing the left wing to strike an airport light. The pilot stated there were no mechanical failures or malfunctions.

synopsis: The loss of power transmission to the main rotor for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination of the airframe and engine did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation of the helicopter.
summary: A helicopter pilot experienced a loss of main rotor power transmission at 12,500 feet over mountains, forcing an autorotation landing that damaged the tail rotor in snow. Post-accident testing confirmed the engine and drive train were functional, but the cause of the power loss remained undetermined.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to operate the helicopter at a high density altitude near terrain, which resulted in a settling with power condition.
summary: A helicopter pilot conducting a downhill skateboard race in mountainous terrain experienced an unresponsive engine and low rotor warning while facing upslope. The pilot performed a forced landing on downsloping terrain, resulting in substantial damage to the main rotor, skid tubes, and tail boom, with post-accident examination revealing no mechanical anomalies.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of elevator control, due to control stick's counter-weight binding with the airplane's header tank.
summary: The pilot of an experimental aircraft experienced control stick binding during takeoff, which worsened on approach, forcing an emergency landing. The landing resulted in a propeller strike and left canard separation, caused by a tight pivot bolt allowing the counterweight to bind with the header tank.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of aircraft control during final approach in gusty wind conditions, resulting in a hard landing.
summary: The pilot impacted terrain at 50 feet AGL during final approach to an off-airport site, causing substantial damage to the wings and fuselage. The pilot attributed the accident to erratic winds and noted no mechanical malfunctions, suggesting a prior touch-and-go would have prevented the event.

synopsis: The mechanic's improper installation of the turbocharger's exhaust balance system, which resulted in an in-flight fire.
summary: The pilot diverted and performed an emergency highway landing after an in-flight fire caused by unsecured turbocharger clamps that allowed exhaust gases to ignite fuel lines. Thermal distortion from the fire prevented nose gear extension, though no other mechanical failures were found.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate directional control during a crosswind landing.
summary: The pilot attempted a landing on an island sandbar with a left crosswind in an airplane equipped with oversized tundra tires. Drifting left caused the left wingtip to strike trees, veering the aircraft into a marsh where the right gear sank and the right wing impacted terrain.

synopsis: The failure of the PA24 pilot to maintain adequate clearance from the PA28 resulting in an inflight collision. Contributing to the accident was the PA24 pilot's decision to overtake the PA28. The PA24 pilot's failure to maintain adequate clearance from the PA28, resulting in an in-flight collision. Contributing to the accident was the PA24 pilot's decision to overtake the PA28.
summary: Two pilots flying a Piper PA-24 and a Piper PA-28 collided in flight when the faster PA-24 overtook the PA-28 from below and behind. The PA-24 failed to alter course to pass well clear, resulting in a mid-air collision that destroyed both aircraft with no mechanical failures found.

synopsis: An inadvertent encounter with unforecast convective turbulence.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe clear-air turbulence at 37,000 feet while cruising, despite no adverse weather on onboard radar or from ATC. FDR data indicated an 80-knot vertical wind gradient caused by passing through the top of a rapidly developing convective cell that required active radar adjustment to detect.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate clearance from transmission wires during a low-level maneuvering flight.
summary: A pilot flying an airplane at low altitude during field spraying encountered an unexpected downdraft that shifted the flight path toward transmission wires. The pilot unsuccessfully attempted to fly under the wires, resulting in the propeller and vertical fin striking them and causing substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The Japan Transport Safety Board notified the NTSB of an incident involving a B767-300 and a DHC-8-402 on May 10, 2011. The NTSB appointed a representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the JTSB.
summary: The Japan Transport Safety Board notified the NTSB of an incident involving a B767-300 and a DHC-8-402 on May 10, 2011. The NTSB appointed a representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the JTSB.

synopsis: The pilots' failure to ensure that the airplane had enough fuel to complete the planned flight, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: A flight instructor and pilot-rated passenger experienced fuel exhaustion and total engine power loss during cruise flight, likely due to overestimating fuel quantity. The instructor executed a forced landing where the right wing struck a guy wire, separated, and the aircraft came to rest in a ditch.

synopsis: The failure of a utility pipe beneath the ramp surface, which caused a localized void in the soil and resulting reduction in the load bearing capability of the ramp.
summary: A utility pipe failure eroded soil beneath a concrete ramp, creating a void. As the aircraft taxied over the area, the left main landing gear penetrated the unsupported concrete and sank into the void.

synopsis: The pilot's continued visual flight rules flight into deteriorating weather conditions in an airplane not equipped for instrument flight, which resulted in a collision with terrain.
summary: An instrument-rated pilot flying a VFR-configured aircraft into deteriorating weather without a weather brief descended below terrain while attempting to avoid clouds. The aircraft impacted a mountain ridge at approximately 3,077 feet MSL in conditions with low ceilings and mist.

synopsis: The pilot's delay in aborting the takeoff, which resulted in a runway overrun. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's inadequate preflight planning and excessive loading of the airplane.
summary: The pilot attempted takeoff in an aircraft weighing 230 pounds over the maximum limit, causing it to settle back on the runway and overrun the departure end. Post-accident examination found no mechanical anomalies, but the excessive weight prevented a timely abort despite sufficient runway length.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to obtain a proper touchdown point while landing with a gusting tailwind.
summary: During landing on a turf runway, a gust of wind caused the left wing to drop and impact the ground, skidding the aircraft 150 feet short of the threshold. The plane subsequently caught fire, resulting in substantial damage, with the pilot reporting no mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot's improper airspeed while maneuvering to land, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall/spin at a low altitude.
summary: The pilot stalled and spun the airplane at low altitude while turning to land after a low pass, failing to reduce pitch to maintain airspeed. The aircraft collided with terrain nose down and right wing low, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The student pilot's improper recovery from the bounced landing and the flight instructor's delayed remedial action.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor were involved in an accident during touch-and-go operations when the aircraft bounced, stalled, and rolled left after the student allegedly continued pulling back on the yoke. The instructor reported no mechanical failures, and the aircraft sustained substantial damage to the left wing and fuselage.

synopsis: A pilot flying a Schweizer 269D helicopter from Weert to Lelystad crashed and caught fire near Veghel, Netherlands, sustaining substantial damage to the aircraft. The pilot was not injured during the accident, which occurred in visual meteorological conditions.
summary: A pilot flying a Schweizer 269D helicopter from Weert to Lelystad crashed and caught fire near Veghel, Netherlands, sustaining substantial damage to the aircraft. The pilot was not injured during the accident, which occurred in visual meteorological conditions.

synopsis: A loss of engine power for undetermined reasons.
summary: The pilot found and drained water from fuel tanks before takeoff, but the engine sputtered at 60 to 100 feet, causing a crash into trees and a fire. Post-accident examination could not determine the engine failure source due to extensive fire damage.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of airplane control for reasons that could not be determined from the available evidence.
summary: An experienced pilot flying a properly maintained airplane in cruise flight lost control twice, resulting in an uncontrolled descent and impact with terrain. Although no mechanical failure or acute medical event was found, the pilot had a history of diabetes-related neuropathy.

synopsis: The pilot's impairment due to alcohol and failure to maintain altitude on approach to landing, resulting in an in-flight collision with a tree.
summary: A private pilot flying an experimental light sport airplane with a passenger struck a tree with the right wing during final approach to a private strip. The aircraft subsequently nosed over inverted, and post-accident testing revealed the pilot had a blood alcohol concentration of 0.149 percent.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation, as a result of the pilot's improper fuel management and preflight inspection. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to comply with the manufacturer's published takeoff and emergency procedures.
summary: The pilot departed without a preflight inspection or known fuel quantity, causing engine power loss shortly after takeoff. The pilot failed to follow emergency procedures to switch tanks, resulting in a forced landing due to fuel exhaustion from the selected left tank.

synopsis: The B737-700 pilot did not maintain adequate wing tip clearance while taxiing around the stopped B-737-800. The B737-700 pilot did not maintain adequate wing tip clearance while taxiing around the stopped B-737-800.
summary: While taxiing on the ramp, a B737-700 captain attempted to pass a stopped B737-800 after the latter moved forward per ramp controller request. The B737-700's left winglet struck the B737-800's right elevator, causing substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing.
summary: The pilot of an agricultural aircraft veered left during a northward landing with an estimated 12-knot tailwind and collided with a trailer while attempting an aborted landing. The pilot reported no mechanical failures, noting that landing north was a routine practice to save time despite the crosswind conditions.

synopsis: The pilot's operation of the helicopter with a left, quartering headwind, resulting in conditions conducive to a loss of tail rotor effectiveness.
summary: Shortly after liftoff from a helideck, a helicopter experienced uncommanded right yaw due to suspected loss of tail rotor effectiveness in a left quartering headwind. The pilot's control inputs failed, resulting in a water impact and rollover, with no mechanical failure found.

synopsis: The Transportation Safety Board of Canada notified the NTSB of an incident involving a B727-200 on March 24, 2010. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the TSB investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design.
summary: The Transportation Safety Board of Canada notified the NTSB of an incident involving a B727-200 on March 24, 2010. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the TSB investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design.

synopsis: A partial loss of engine power during low-altitude maneuvering for undetermined reasons.
summary: An agricultural pilot experienced partial engine power loss while climbing to clear a transmission line after spray operations, forcing a landing in a bean field where the aircraft struck a ditch. Post-accident examination found no mechanical failures or fuel contamination to explain the reported surge, though propeller blades were observed in the feather position.

aircraft: Czech Aircraft Works Spol Sro Sportcruiser
synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control during the takeoff climb, which resulted in a stall at low altitude and collision with terrain. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's impaired performance from over-the-counter medications.
summary: A witness observed the aircraft oscillating and stalling shortly after takeoff, resulting in a ground impact. Postaccident analysis found no engine failure but concluded that therapeutic levels of diphenhydramine likely impaired the pilot's performance and caused the accident.

synopsis: The pilot's poor decision to takeoff with a tailwind which resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot reported that a gyroplane impacted a fence line during takeoff from a private grass strip with a tailwind. The pilot attributed the accident to looking down at engine instruments mid-roll, which caused him to lose situational awareness and fail to clear the obstacle.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to attain sufficient altitude to clear terrain while maneuvering.
summary: During agricultural spraying, a helicopter pilot likely flew into rising terrain, causing the main rotor to strike and sever the tail boom. This loss of anti-torque control resulted in the helicopter spinning uncontrollably and crashing.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power for undetermined reasons.
summary: The pilot executed a forced landing in a field after the engine lost power during a precautionary approach due to low fuel. The aircraft impacted soft ground, separating the right main landing gear, though post-accident inspection found no pre-impact mechanical failure or definitive cause for the power loss.

synopsis: The pilot did not maintain sufficient airspeed during an instrument approach in icing conditions, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and loss of control. Contributing to the accident were the pilot's fatigue, the operator's decision to initiate the flight without conducting a formal risk assessment that included time of day, weather, and crew rest, and the lack of guidelines for the medical community to determine the appropriate mode of transportation for patients.
summary: A fatigued pilot flying an EMS aircraft at night in icing conditions lost airspeed below the minimum safe limit of 140 knots during an instrument approach. The pilot failed to recover from the resulting stall, and the aircraft impacted snow-covered terrain.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to ensure that the governor limit switch was properly set, which resulted in reduced engine power.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine-out caution and power reduction shortly after helicopter departure due to a fuel control governor limit switch set near the minimum. This improper setting caused a run-on landing where the tail rotor struck a ditch, though the engine itself showed no defects.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a tree during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot reported that after landing on a loose dirt and gravel road, the airplane's right wing struck a tree, causing a 20-degree right rotation and sideways skid. Despite correction attempts, the aircraft exited the road and nosed over with no preimpact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's improper fuel management, which resulted in a loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
summary: The pilot and passenger experienced engine power loss in level flight due to fuel exhaustion in the right tank, despite the selector being positioned there. This caused a forced landing where the right wing struck a tree, rupturing the tank and separating the wing.

synopsis: The pilot's continued operation of the aircraft with deteriorated wing fabric and his aggressive maneuvering at low altitude, which resulted in the right wing fabric's failure during flight. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's loading of the aircraft in excess of the maximum gross weight limit.
summary: A sport pilot flight instructor crashed a light sport weight-shift-control aircraft into the ocean during a steep turn while 121 pounds overweight. The accident resulted from the pilot aggressively maneuvering the aircraft, causing deteriorated wing fabric to fail under the increased load.

synopsis: An Air Cuenca B737-500 lost directional control during landing on runway 23 at Mariscal Lamar Airport, veering off near the departure end and crossing an adjacent taxiway. The aircraft stopped with minor damage and no injuries, prompting an investigation by Ecuadorian authorities with NTSB assistance.
summary: An Air Cuenca B737-500 lost directional control during landing on runway 23 at Mariscal Lamar Airport, veering off near the departure end and crossing an adjacent taxiway. The aircraft stopped with minor damage and no injuries, prompting an investigation by Ecuadorian authorities with NTSB assistance.

synopsis: The fatigue failure of the nose landing gear (NLG) end cap, which resulted in insufficient hydraulic pressure to secure the left main landing gear into the down and locked position. Contributing to the fatigue failure was the NLG end cap's non-optimum grain direction and the inadequate inspection procedure performed during overhaul.
summary: During approach, the left main landing gear collapsed after a nose gear actuator end cap fatigue failure caused hydraulic pressure loss. An incorrect cockpit lamp module allowed light bleed, creating a false "down-and-locked" indication that led the crew to continue the landing despite warning horns.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing.
summary: A commercial pilot and chief pilot were practicing stop-and-go landings in a tailwheel airplane when it veered right and exited the runway despite full left rudder. The excursion caused the left wing to strike the ground, resulting in substantial damage, though the tailwheel assembly showed no anomalies.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight inspection, resulting in a departure with the fuel selector in the "off" position, a subsequent loss of engine power, and an off-airport emergency landing.
summary: The pilot departed with the fuel selector inadvertently in the "off" position, causing engine power loss at 700 feet. An emergency landing on marshy ground resulted in the airplane nosing over and sustaining substantial damage to the wings and lift struts.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate clearance from a communications cart while taxiing.
summary: The pilot reported that while taxiing to the ramp after landing, his aircraft's right wingtip struck a remote communications cart at the taxiway edge. This collision caused substantial damage to the right wing's leading edge, skin, ribs, and spar.

synopsis: The student pilot's relinquishing of the flight controls during the landing flare and the flight instructor's delay in taking remedial action.
summary: During a flight review, a student pilot relinquished controls to a CFI while flaring, causing the right wingtip to strike the runway. The CFI did not notice the impact, and substantial damage to two wing ribs was discovered only during the postflight inspection.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed during takeoff which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
summary: The pilot and passenger departed for touch-and-go practice in a tailwind but experienced insufficient engine power during the takeoff roll. The aircraft stalled and struck trees at the runway end, sustaining substantial damage, though the pilot reported no mechanical issues and the engine was running at impact.

synopsis: The air traffic controller's failure to adhere to runway separation requirements and his issuance of an improper takeoff clearance. Contributing to the incident was the controller's failure to recall that there was an arrival inbound to a crossing runway. The air traffic controller's failure to adhere to runway separation requirements and his issuance of an improper takeoff clearance. Contributing to the incident was the controller's failure to recall that there was an arrival inbound to a crossing runway.
summary: A tower controller cleared an Embraer ERJ-145 for takeoff from runway 32L while forgetting a Bombardier CRJ2 on final approach to runway 9R, causing a near-midair collision. The CRJ2 passed 480 feet behind and 275 feet above the departing jet due to the controller's unexplained lapse and lack of automated conflict detection.

synopsis: the failure of a midspar fitting, which was susceptible to fatigue cracking and should have been replaced with a newer, more fatigue-resistant version of the fitting as required by an airworthiness directive. Also causal was an erroneous maintenance entry made by a previous aircraft owner, which incorrectly reflected that the newer fitting had been installed.
summary: On May 18, 2011, a modified Boeing 707 (N707AR) operating as Omega flight 70 crashed into a marsh area beyond the departure end of runway 21 at Point Mugu Naval Air Station during takeoff. The aircraft was substantially damaged by postimpact fire, and the three flight crewmembers sustained minor injuries.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain a stabilized glide path which resulted in the airplane touching down short of the runway.
summary: The pilot flying an instrument approach visually descended too steeply, causing the left main gear to strike the ground 120 feet before the runway threshold. Recorded data showed airspeeds of 71–81 knots with a 3–5 knot tailwind, and the pilot reported no mechanical failure.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during the landing rollout, which resulted in a collision with trees.
summary: The pilot lost directional control during landing rollout due to a strong wind gust, causing the airplane to veer off the runway and collide with trees. This resulted in substantial damage to the wing spars, despite nearby weather observations reporting light and variable winds.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to continue flight into an area of known adverse weather, which resulted in an accumulation of structural ice that led to a loss of control and in-flight breakup. Also causal was the pilot's inadequate preflight weather planning.
summary: The pilot departed without an updated weather briefing despite forecasts of icing and precipitation. The aircraft rapidly accumulated ice, entered an uncontrolled descent with wing separation, and impacted terrain due to structural stress beyond design limits.

synopsis: The student pilot's improper flare which resulted in a hard landing, and the flight instructor's lack of remedial action.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor landed an airplane trimmed for 62 knots with half flaps. The aircraft suddenly dropped 15 to 20 feet above the runway, veered left, and sustained substantial right wing damage after striking a precision approach path indicator stanchion.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll, resulting in a ground loop.
summary: The pilot reported that during landing, the airplane ground looped to the right and struck the left wing on the runway. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the left wing, though the pilot reported no mechanical anomalies precluding normal operation.

synopsis: A Cessna 210M with one pilot and two passengers crashed into wooded terrain near Breu Branco, Brazil, while en route from Senador Jose Porfirio to Paragominas. The impact caused substantial damage and fatal injuries to all occupants under unknown circumstances.
summary: A Cessna 210M with one pilot and two passengers crashed into wooded terrain near Breu Branco, Brazil, while en route from Senador Jose Porfirio to Paragominas. The impact caused substantial damage and fatal injuries to all occupants under unknown circumstances.

synopsis: A Sol Lineas Aereas Saab 340A (LV-CEJ) with 21 occupants crashed enroute from Neuquén to Comodoro Rivadavia after the crew declared an emergency and disappeared from radar. The aircraft was found 35 km from Los Menucos with all aboard killed, and the JIAAC is investigating.
summary: A Sol Lineas Aereas Saab 340A (LV-CEJ) with 21 occupants crashed enroute from Neuquén to Comodoro Rivadavia after the crew declared an emergency and disappeared from radar. The aircraft was found 35 km from Los Menucos with all aboard killed, and the JIAAC is investigating.

synopsis: The pilot's continued flight into instrument meteorological conditions at an insufficient altitude to clear terrain.
summary: The pilot of a personal flight aircraft impacted mountainous terrain after continuing into instrument meteorological conditions at an insufficient altitude. Post-accident examination found no mechanical failures, attributing the crash to the pilot's decision to fly into IMC.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff.
summary: The pilot attempted a takeoff in strong crosswinds, causing the aircraft to veer off the airstrip onto soft dirt and nose over. The pilot reported no preimpact mechanical malfunctions or failures that would have precluded normal flight.

synopsis: The pilot's continued visual flight into instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in loss of situational awareness, and a possible encounter with icing conditions.
summary: The pilot flew an unfamiliar mountain route without an updated weather briefing, entering instrument conditions with snow and icing. The aircraft impacted terrain after erratic maneuvers suggesting disorientation, with postmortem results showing recent antihistamine use that may have impaired the pilot.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power while maneuvering due to a seized piston.
summary: The pilot of an experimental light sport aircraft experienced a total engine power loss due to a seized rear piston while climbing after a low pass. The aircraft impacted trees and landed on a road; the non-certificated engine was known to be prone to sudden stoppage.

synopsis: The loss of engine power due to carburetor ice.
summary: The pilot experienced a loss of engine power during initial climb, forcing an off-airport landing where the aircraft struck a fence and trees. The probable cause was carburetor icing due to the pilot's failure to use carburetor heat during ground operations.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane while taxiing in gusty wind conditions.
summary: The pilot reported that during taxi following an off-airport landing, a rear wind gust caused the airplane to nose over. This resulted in substantial damage to the right wing lift struts.

synopsis: An in-flight fire for undetermined reasons.
summary: A private pilot and passenger experienced an in-flight fire with smoke and flames near the pilot's left foot during a local flight. They executed a forced landing in a muddy field and exited before the aircraft was rapidly consumed by fire, though the origin remained undetermined due to extensive damage.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain control of the helicopter while hovering.
summary: A student pilot lost control during a pedal turn while hovering on a taxiway after his first solo helicopter flight. The aircraft struck the ground, damaging the aft skid and tail rotor, with the operator reporting no mechanical failure.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to initiate a go-around after a bounced landing at an airport where go-arounds were not advised and his failure to maintain adequate airspeed during the go-around.
summary: The pilot of a sightseeing aircraft encountered downdrafts during landing at a high-density altitude airport with a nearby cliff. After a hard bounce, the pilot initiated a go-around but stalled during a turn and descended into the ground; no mechanical failures were found.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed in the flare which resulted in a stall and a hard landing.
summary: The pilot reported a wind gust caused the airplane to balloon and stall during the flare, leading to a runway impact, collapsed landing gear, and propeller strike. Witnesses described a high, steep, and fast approach, while post-accident examination found no preimpact mechanical anomalies.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control while landing in gusty, crosswind conditions.
summary: During landing flare, a wind gust pushed the aircraft right, causing the right gear door to strike an airfield sign during a go-around attempt. This resulted in substantial damage to the fuselage, empennage, vertical stabilizer, and elevators, with no mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain an adequate airspeed during landing, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
summary: The pilot landed a cross-country flight with a 5- to 7-knot headwind but stalled at approximately 5 feet during the flare due to a high angle of attack. This caused a hard landing that substantially damaged both wings, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's performance of aerobatic maneuvers at low altitude and his failure to maintain airspeed, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
summary: Witnesses observed the pilot performing aerobatic maneuvers before the aircraft impacted a parking lot, while the pilot claimed an engine power loss necessitated a forced landing. Investigators found fuel system water contamination but concluded the engine likely operated throughout the maneuvers due to lack of witness reports of engine trouble and no flight control abnormalities.

aircraft: Hansen Ib C CASSUTT III M
synopsis: The pilot's incapacitation due to a cardiac event.
summary: During the maiden flight's initial takeoff, the aircraft climbed to 300 feet, turned left, and impacted the ground. The pilot likely suffered sudden cardiac death due to severe coronary artery stenosis, as no mechanical anomalies or control injuries were found.

synopsis: A Bell 206L-3 operated by Aviheco S.A. with two crewmembers collided with terrain near Norte de Santander, Colombia, during a local flight from Bogota. The accident destroyed the aircraft and killed both crewmembers.
summary: A Bell 206L-3 operated by Aviheco S.A. with two crewmembers collided with terrain near Norte de Santander, Colombia, during a local flight from Bogota. The accident destroyed the aircraft and killed both crewmembers.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to continue a visual approach with low visibility and in heavy rain and his subsequent failure to maintain clearance from trees.
summary: The pilot attempted a landing in heavy rain and low visibility, colliding with trees right of the runway before impacting the surface. This caused left wing damage, landing gear collapse, and engine firewall damage, with no prior mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain sufficient altitude to avoid rising terrain. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's visual illusion and disorientation due to the flat light conditions.
summary: The pilot and passenger became disoriented while descending a snow-covered mountain valley in flat light conditions. A visual illusion caused the pilot to misjudge altitude, resulting in a controlled flight into terrain that substantially damaged the fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed during landing, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's lack of experience in the accident airplane.
summary: The pilot nosed over a new airplane while landing on grass after reducing power and pitching up at 32–35 mph with flaps retracted. The aircraft inverted and sustained substantial damage because the approach speed was below the manufacturer's recommended 45–50 mph range.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control while landing in gusty conditions.
summary: The pilot lost directional control during landing in a sudden 36-knot crosswind gust, causing the aircraft to leave the runway. Attempts to fly out resulted in right gear collapse and left wing damage due to side-loading.

synopsis: The pilots' unstabilized approach and excessive airspeed during approach, which resulted in an insufficient landing distance to stop the airplane before overrunning the runway.
summary: The flight crew experienced a runway overrun during landing due to misjudging approach speed, resulting in a high-speed touchdown of 124 knots. Despite maximum braking, the aircraft exited the runway and descended an embankment, with no mechanical failures found.

synopsis: Inadvertant encounter with convective turbulence while in cruise. Contributing to the severity of the accident was the unrestrained status of the passenger, contrary to the lighted seat belt sign.
summary: Delta flight 2001, a Boeing 757-223, encountered turbulence at FL340 while maneuvering between convective cells near Atlanta. The crew inadvertently entered a cumulus buildup, causing an unbelted passenger to fall and sustain a broken ankle, while one flight attendant suffered minor injuries.

synopsis: The Taiwan Aviation Safety Council notified the NTSB of an incident involving an MD-90 on May 12, 2011. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the ASC.
summary: The Taiwan Aviation Safety Council notified the NTSB of an incident involving an MD-90 on May 12, 2011. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the ASC.

synopsis: A Ryanair Boeing 737-800 experienced depressurization while enroute from Liverpool to Dublin. No injuries or aircraft damage occurred, and the Air Accidents Investigation Unit of Ireland is investigating the event.
summary: A Ryanair Boeing 737-800 experienced depressurization while enroute from Liverpool to Dublin. No injuries or aircraft damage occurred, and the Air Accidents Investigation Unit of Ireland is investigating the event.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control upon landing.
summary: During landing, a gust of wind lifted the pilot's left wing, causing the airplane to ground-loop despite control inputs. The pilot reported no preimpact mechanical malfunctions, noting winds were from 240 degrees at 7 knots.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate compensation for crosswind conditions during landing, resulting in a runway excursion and collision with a hangar.
summary: The pilot of an experimental tailwheel airplane drifted right during landing due to crosswind gusts at 15 feet. After aborting the landing, the aircraft struck a hangar, causing substantial wing damage with no pre-impact mechanical failures found.

synopsis: An in-flight fire that mostly likely occurred in the right front cockpit area behind the instrument panel and below the glare shield; the origin of the fire could not be determined because of the extensive fire damage.
summary: The pilot declared an emergency due to an in-flight fire at 9,000 feet, after which the aircraft crashed in a wooded area. Investigators determined the fire likely originated beneath the right instrument panel and was fuel-fed, though the exact source could not be identified due to extensive damage.

synopsis: A Brazilian certificated pilot and three passengers were fatally injured when a Piper PA-34-200 impacted hilly terrain near Sao Pedro, Brazil, under unknown circumstances. The local training flight had departed Piracicaba Airport shortly before the accident.
summary: A Brazilian certificated pilot and three passengers were fatally injured when a Piper PA-34-200 impacted hilly terrain near Sao Pedro, Brazil, under unknown circumstances. The local training flight had departed Piracicaba Airport shortly before the accident.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control during takeoff after he reached to secure a seatbelt that was wedged in the passenger door.
summary: During takeoff, the pilot observed a seatbelt wedged in the right door and reached to open it, causing the aircraft to impact the runway. This resulted in substantial damage to the tail section.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate compensation for wind conditions.
summary: A solo student pilot crashed a damaged aircraft during a second landing attempt after a go-around caused by low-level turbulence from trees. The pilot reported no mechanical issues, stating the airplane turned right and impacted the ground 5 feet above the runway due to wind conditions.

synopsis: A loss of engine power for undetermined reasons because postaccident examination of the airframe and engine revealed no anomalies.
summary: During a maintenance flight, a pilot and flight mechanic experienced unresponsive engine power while recovering from an autorotation at 500 feet, forcing a running landing that separated the tail boom. Although the engine later tested within specifications, the cause of the in-flight power loss remained undetermined.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control on the landing roll out. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision to attempt a landing in crosswind conditions that exceeded the maximum demonstrated capability of the airplane.
summary: The pilot landed on runway 21 in variable winds gusting to 32 knots, exceeding the aircraft's 17-knot crosswind limit. During the landing roll, the airplane veered left, exited the runway, and struck a tree, substantially damaging the left wing.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during landing on a soft, turf runway.
summary: The pilot landed on a soft, rain-soaked turf runway, where the airplane veered right and struck a tree during the landing roll. This caused substantial damage to the right wing and fuselage, with no mechanical malfunction found.

synopsis: The flight crew did not ensure that the landing gear selector handle was in the full down (extend) position. Contributing to the incident was inadequate checklist information.
summary: During a visual approach, the flight crew experienced a landing gear failure where the gear extended but did not lock due to a hydraulic bypass caused by the selector handle not being fully down. The subsequent emergency landing resulted in the right main gear collapsing, leading to post-incident checklist revisions by the manufacturer.

synopsis: El Al Boeing 777-800 pilots returned to Tel Aviv after takeoff when the left main landing gear failed to retract due to a structural failure at the forward trunnion. The aircraft landed safely after fuel dumping and an F16 visual confirmation, with no injuries reported.
summary: El Al Boeing 777-800 pilots returned to Tel Aviv after takeoff when the left main landing gear failed to retract due to a structural failure at the forward trunnion. The aircraft landed safely after fuel dumping and an F16 visual confirmation, with no injuries reported.

synopsis: Failure of the landing gear to fully extend due to a failed o-ring in the nose gear actuator piston and a broken seal in the emergency landing gear extension system.
summary: The pilot experienced a landing gear malfunction after takeoff due to a failed o-ring and seal, resulting in an empty hydraulic reservoir. Despite adding oil and attempting manual extension, the aircraft belly-landed with the nose gear down and main gear retracted, damaging the left horizontal stabilizer.

synopsis: The Belgium Air Accident Investigation Unit notified the NTSB of a May 26, 2011, accident involving a B737-45D. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the AAIU.
summary: The Belgium Air Accident Investigation Unit notified the NTSB of a May 26, 2011, accident involving a B737-45D. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the AAIU.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control of the airplane during takeoff, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's lack of experience in make and model, his lack of currency in FAA required takeoffs and landings, and his excessive loading of the airplane.
summary: The pilot and four passengers departed in an overloaded aircraft when the pilot, lacking recent experience, lost control during takeoff. He applied excessive pitch, failed to maintain airspeed, and the airplane stalled, rolled, and crashed into the ground, resulting in a postcrash fire.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff from an unpaved airstrip, resulting in a collision with trees.
summary: The pilot of a parachute jump aircraft collided with trees during takeoff after the airplane pulled left at rotation. Post-accident examination found no mechanical anomalies, resulting in substantial damage to the wings and fuselage after the left main wheel separated.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during landing, which resulted in a runway excursion. Contributing to the accident were the effects of multiple modifications to the main and tailwheel landing gear through the supplemental type certificate and FAA field approval process, which adversely changed their geometry, and resulted in degraded controllability during landing.
summary: A pilot with no prior experience in this modified tailwheel aircraft lost directional control during a three-point landing, causing the airplane to veer left and collide with a ditch. The accident resulted from improper tailwheel alignment due to unverified landing gear modifications that created negative camber.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power during low-level maneuvering due to an excessively worn carburetor.
summary: During an aerial application pass, the pilot experienced engine power loss and smoke, forcing a landing that caused substantial damage. Investigation attributed the failure to a worn carburetor accelerator pump causing hesitation, while supercharger gear fractures resulted from the impact.

synopsis: The student pilot's decision to fly in windy conditions that exceeded his capabilities, which resulted in his subsequent loss of helicopter control. Contributing to the accident was his lack of flight experience in the accident helicopter.
summary: A student helicopter pilot with 120 hours of training departed solo into gusty winds over mountainous terrain without a weather briefing, violating his endorsement. The aircraft impacted trees level after an apparent autorotation, likely caused by the pilot's poor decision-making and overconfidence in adverse conditions.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate fuel planning, which resulted in a loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion, and his improper control inputs following the loss of engine power, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and subsequent loss of control. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's impaired judgment, which led to his failure to recognize the fuel shortage earlier and his improper decision to fly with disqualifying medical conditions.
summary: The pilot, who had undisclosed depression and took disqualifying medication, improperly planned fuel for a flight, causing fuel exhaustion and engine power loss. This led to an aerodynamic stall and a crash into an urban apartment complex parking lot.

synopsis: The crew of a Korean Air A330-300 experienced a loud bang, high vibration, and fire warning in engine 2 while climbing through 11,500 feet. The pilot shut down the engine, discharged a fire bottle, and landed safely after a post-flight inspection revealed a puncture in the Low Pressure Turbine Case.
summary: The crew of a Korean Air A330-300 experienced a loud bang, high vibration, and fire warning in engine 2 while climbing through 11,500 feet. The pilot shut down the engine, discharged a fire bottle, and landed safely after a post-flight inspection revealed a puncture in the Low Pressure Turbine Case.

synopsis: The drooping electrical conduit, which snagged the vertical fin and resulted in the pilot's inability to control the helicopter. Contributing to the accident was the operator's decision to have the pilot fly the helicopter out of the hangar.
summary: The pilot lost control while hover taxiing a helicopter out of a hangar when a drooped electrical conduit snagged the vertical tail fin. This caused the main rotor blades to separate from the mast, resulting in the aircraft tipping over and impacting the ground.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to recognize and avoid a loss of tail rotor effectiveness, which resulted in a loss of control and hard landing.
summary: A pilot flying a helicopter at low altitude during a search mission lost control due to unrecognized tail rotor effectiveness (LTE) while focused on the mission. The aircraft spun and impacted the ground, prompting the operator to implement additional LTE and emergency procedure training.

synopsis: The pilot's continued visual flight rules flight into instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in a controlled collision with terrain.
summary: The instrument-rated pilot canceled an IFR clearance to fly VFR into deteriorating weather, resulting in a controlled flight into terrain at 6,400 feet MSL. The accident likely occurred because the pilot encountered IMC and overflew the amended destination, possibly impaired by medical conditions or drug use.

synopsis: The flight crew of a Saudi Arabian Airlines Boeing 747-300 experienced an uncommanded full power increase on engine No. 4 while taxiing for takeoff at Lahore. The crew shut down the engine using the fuel cut-off switch, and the aircraft returned to the ramp without further incident.
summary: The flight crew of a Saudi Arabian Airlines Boeing 747-300 experienced an uncommanded full power increase on engine No. 4 while taxiing for takeoff at Lahore. The crew shut down the engine using the fuel cut-off switch, and the aircraft returned to the ramp without further incident.

synopsis: The pilot's improper decision to take off downwind from unsuitable terrain.
summary: The pilot departed a short, rough field with a tailwind and encountered stronger tailwinds at 100 feet, causing the climb to stop. Fearing a stall, the pilot did not turn away from rising terrain, resulting in a tree impact that caused substantial damage to the wings and fuselage.

synopsis: Emirates Flight 132, a B777-200ER, reported a loud noise from Engine 2 during takeoff from Moscow Domodedovo. Although no debris was found on the runway and engine parameters appeared normal, maintenance later discovered missing fan duct and thrust reverser sections after landing in Dubai.
summary: Emirates Flight 132, a B777-200ER, reported a loud noise from Engine 2 during takeoff from Moscow Domodedovo. Although no debris was found on the runway and engine parameters appeared normal, maintenance later discovered missing fan duct and thrust reverser sections after landing in Dubai.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control due to his not maintaining adequate airspeed and altitude during a simulated hydraulic flight control failure. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's inadequate supervision and delayed remedial response.
summary: A pilot and flight instructor crashed a helicopter during a low-speed training approach while simulating hydraulic failure. The accident resulted from loss of control due to excessive workload without hydraulic assistance, potentially compounded by distraction from correcting a radio frequency error.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the aircraft during take-off in a cross wind, which resulted in an inadvertent stall.
summary: The pilot of a weight-shift aircraft with a newly installed dual-surface wing crashed during a test flight takeoff in an 80-degree crosswind. The pilot attributed the accident to insufficient airspeed and wind shear at 100 feet, which caused a right wing stall and resulted in substantial damage.

aircraft: Flournoy Martin R FLOURNOY MR S1S
synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during the landing rollout due to failure of the tailwheel assembly for undetermined reasons.
summary: The pilot reported a ground loop during rollout after the aircraft yawed left despite corrective rudder and brake inputs. Post-accident examination found the tailwheel spring attach bolt had pulled through the fuselage structure, though the cause of separation was undetermined.

aircraft: Aero At Sp Zoo AT-4 LSA
synopsis: The student pilot's loss of aircraft control during a go-around maneuver following a bounced landing.
summary: A student pilot performing a solo cross-country landing bounced and drifted left, prompting a go-around. The aircraft subsequently rolled, pitched erratically, and impacted the ground 180 degrees off runway heading, causing substantial damage with no pre-impact malfunctions found.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to maintain an appropriate glide path and airspeed during the landing approach, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
summary: A certified flight instructor conducting a power-off spot landing demonstration allowed the aircraft to get too low and slow, resulting in a stall and ground impact 30 feet from the runway end. The airplane sustained substantial damage to the left wing and landing gear, with the instructor reporting no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate helicopter preflight inspection and the mechanic's inadequate annual inspection, both of which failed to detect a worn bolt in the tail rotor teeter hinge prior to its fracture due to fatigue.
summary: The pilot experienced abnormal vibration in a helicopter during cruise and performed a precautionary landing. Post-incident examination revealed the tail rotor teeter hinge bolt fractured due to fatigue, attributed to the pilot's inconsistent use of the preflight checklist and missing torque stripe.

synopsis: The pilot's encounter with a berm during the landing roll, resulting in the airplane nosing over.
summary: The pilot executed an off-airport landing on mowed grass, where the airplane impacted a berm and nosed over inverted. The accident crushed the rudder and bent a left wing strut, though the pilot reported no mechanical anomalies prior to the event.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate clearance from terrain while maneuvering in a mountainous area.
summary: A pilot departed with three passengers for a sightseeing flight before the aircraft impacted a tree and mountain side in a right-wing-low attitude. The investigation found no mechanical failure but noted an uncorrected altimeter issue and the presence of unreported medications in the pilot's system.

synopsis: The pilot did not maintain adequate airspeed during the downwind turn resulting in an aerodynamic stall, in-flight loss of control, and spin. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's inadequate preflight planning and exceedance of the approved weight and balance envelope.
summary: The pilot, flying an aircraft with an aft center of gravity and low fuel, attempted a landing in 28-knot crosswinds. A sudden wind shift combined with pitch sensitivity likely induced an aerodynamic stall, causing the airplane to plummet and impact the ground with no mechanical failures found.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from obstacles.
summary: During low-level agricultural operations, a helicopter pilot experienced a tail rotor strike on a tree limb, causing vibration and yaw. Post-accident examination confirmed the tail rotor blade impact caused an imbalance, leading to autorotation and a forced landing.

synopsis: The private pilot's inability to maintain directional control of the airplane during the takeoff roll.
summary: A private pilot with left-sided weakness from a prior stroke veered a tailwheel-equipped airplane off the runway during takeoff while being observed by a commercial pilot. The aircraft nosed over and struck the ground with the propeller, causing substantial damage to the engine firewall and right wing despite no mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The flying pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control and the flight instructor's inadequate supervision while landing with a gusting wind. Contributing to the accident was the lack of communication between the flight instructor and pilot under evaluation regarding who was manipulating the controls.
summary: During a flight review, a glider pilot and instructor disagreed on who controlled the aircraft during a final approach in strong winds. The glider encountered a downdraft, banked violently right, and impacted trees and a guard rail, causing substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff following a loss of left engine power for undetermined reasons.
summary: A solo pilot lost left engine power during takeoff rotation and failed to retard power or apply sufficient right rudder, causing the aircraft to veer off the runway and strike trees. Post-accident inspection found no mechanical anomalies, attributing the crash to the pilot's delayed response.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to attain a positive climb rate following takeoff for reasons that could not be determined because the propeller was not provided for further examination. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's impairment from alcohol.
summary: The pilot flew a single-engine airplane into trees during the crosswind leg after takeoff due to an inability to stop the descent. Post-accident testing revealed the pilot had a blood alcohol concentration of 0.15%, which the FAA notes causes impairment affecting flight performance.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to attain an adequate climb rate during the initial takeoff, resulting in the airplane settling back down and departing the runway. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's inadequate preflight planning and preparation.
summary: The pilot and passenger crashed a single-engine airplane on a 2,130-foot turf runway after veering left and striking a sign and tree. Postaccident analysis found no substantial thrust loss, suggesting the accident resulted from insufficient runway length for the sod surface.

synopsis: The pilot's improper installation of the gascolator gasket during the airplane's last condition inspection, which resulted in a partial loss of engine power while maneuvering.
summary: The pilot experienced partial engine power loss at 7,500 feet due to air entering the fuel system from an improperly installed gascolator gasket. He smelled fuel, shut off the selector, and executed a precautionary landing in a field after determining the runway was unreachable.

synopsis: The certified flight instructor's failure to maintain adequate main rotor RPM during the autorotation.
summary: A certified flight instructor in a helicopter delayed power application during a power-on autorotation demonstration, resulting in insufficient rotor RPM to recover before ground impact. The crash damaged the tail rotor drive shaft and main rotor blades, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The failure of the low pressure switch in the normal landing gear system, which prevented normal operation of that system, and the misrigging of the emergency extension gear release valve, which prevented the system from being depressurized to allow for the freefall of the gear.
summary: The pilot attempted to extend landing gear during descent after canceling IFR, but both normal and emergency systems failed due to a faulty low hydraulic pressure switch and a misrigged emergency release valve. Consequently, the pilot executed a gear-up landing, resulting in a 1,200-foot slide.

synopsis: The student pilot's loss of control during the takeoff.
summary: A student pilot conducting a solo cross-country flight in a tailwheel-equipped airplane lifted off at 50 mph during a takeoff roll on a turf runway. After lowering the nose to gain airspeed, the aircraft contacted the runway and impacted trees, causing substantial wing spar damage with no mechanical malfunctions found.

synopsis: The overheat and failure the brake during landing due to oxidation of the brake rotors, which went undetected by maintenance personnel. Contributing to the accident was maintenance personnel's lack of familiarity with detailed brake oxidation inspection procedures.
summary: Pilots experienced a brake failure and hydraulic leak during landing roll due to a fractured pressure plate and rotor. The incident was attributed to undetected oxidation caused by maintenance personnel lacking the required inspection tool and training.

synopsis: A loss of engine power during cruise flight for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: During a local night flight, the pilot experienced an engine surge and partial power loss, forcing a landing in a field that collapsed the gear and bent the firewall.
