summary: The pilot of a helicopter experienced engine power loss due to fuel exhaustion during the landing sequence. The pilot executed an autorotation to a golf course, attributing the incident to fuel mismanagement and a tailwind component lower than forecast.

synopsis: The pilot's inability to maintain control of the airplane for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination of the rudder control system did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded control of the airplane.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor experienced a loss of rudder and elevator control during climb after takeoff due to a fractured tail skid/rudder control tube. The student deployed the ballistic recovery parachute, resulting in substantial fuselage damage upon ground contact.

synopsis: The non-instrument-rated pilot's spatial disorientation in night instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in his inability to maintain controlled flight. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's improper decision to take off in deteriorating meteorological conditions.
summary: A non-instrument-rated pilot took off in deteriorating fog after sunset and attempted to return to the departure airport. The pilot likely became spatially disoriented in the dark, foggy conditions, resulting in a loss of control and impact with trees.

synopsis: Ground personnel's movement of cargo in windy conditions, which allowed a previously secured cargo sack to blow into the main rotor blades.
summary: A pilot performing an engine cool-down at an off-airport site in windy conditions reported that a worker removed a weight from a cargo sack. The wind lifted the sack into the helicopter's main rotor system, causing substantial damage to the main rotor blades.

synopsis: The non-instrument-rated pilot's decision to fly into known instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in the pilot's spatial disorientation and loss of airplane control.
summary: A non-instrument-rated pilot flying VFR at night without a flight plan entered instrument meteorological conditions near the destination. The pilot likely experienced spatial disorientation and lost control, resulting in a high-speed impact with no mechanical failures found.

synopsis: On January 6, 2012, the pilot of a Robinson R22 Beta, G-CHZN, was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted terrain near Witchford, Cambridgeshire. The accident resulted in substantial damage to the helicopter, and the investigation remains under the jurisdiction of the United Kingdom.
summary: On January 6, 2012, the pilot of a Robinson R22 Beta, G-CHZN, was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted terrain near Witchford, Cambridgeshire. The accident resulted in substantial damage to the helicopter, and the investigation remains under the jurisdiction of the United Kingdom.

synopsis: A Bell 206 L-4 helicopter carrying a pilot and four passengers collided with a mountain during a sightseeing flight near Montaña Auyantepui, Venezuela. Precipitation was noted near the accident location, and all occupants were fatally injured.
summary: A Bell 206 L-4 helicopter carrying a pilot and four passengers collided with a mountain during a sightseeing flight near Montaña Auyantepui, Venezuela. Precipitation was noted near the accident location, and all occupants were fatally injured.

synopsis: A partial loss of engine power during cruise flight due to incorrectly installed airframe components, which came into contact with a high pressure fuel line and resulted in its failure. Contributing to the accident was an undetermined failure of the primary landing gear extension system that could not be identified due to extensive damage.
summary: The pilot of an experimental amateur-built airplane experienced engine power loss at cruise due to a fatigued fuel line contacting airframe components. Unable to extend landing gear or climb during a go-around, he performed a forced landing that caused substantial damage to the fuselage and wings.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during the landing roll, which resulted in a runway excursion. Contributing to the accident was the sunglare.
summary: The pilot landed westward in the late afternoon, where the sun blinded him and limited vision. The aircraft drifted off the runway right side, struck soft ground, and veered into a ditch, causing substantial damage to the wings and fuselage with no mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The Afghanistan Civil Aviation Authority notified the NTSB of an MD-80 accident on January 24, 2012. The Spanish CIAIAC is investigating with NTSB assistance, and all information will be released by the CIAIAC.
summary: The Afghanistan Civil Aviation Authority notified the NTSB of an MD-80 accident on January 24, 2012. The Spanish CIAIAC is investigating with NTSB assistance, and all information will be released by the CIAIAC.

synopsis: The UK AAIB notified the NTSB of a January 17, 2012, incident involving a Boeing 747. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the AAIB investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design.
summary: The UK AAIB notified the NTSB of a January 17, 2012, incident involving a Boeing 747. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the AAIB investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design.

synopsis: The UAE GCAA notified the NTSB of an incident involving a Boeing 777 on December 2, 2011. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the GCAA investigation, which will release all information.
summary: The UAE GCAA notified the NTSB of an incident involving a Boeing 777 on December 2, 2011. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the GCAA investigation, which will release all information.

synopsis: The failure of a crankshaft gear tooth due to fatigue, which resulted in the loss of several additional gear teeth and a subsequent total loss of engine power.
summary: The pilot landed the aircraft on an interstate highway at night after a total loss of engine power caused by a crankshaft gear tooth fatigue failure. Neither of the two occupants were injured, and the airplane remained undamaged.

synopsis: The pilot's improper identification of the runway surface. Contributing to the accident was the snow covering the runway lights.
summary: During a night landing, the pilot misidentified the runway surface and landed in a snowbank due to heavy snow obscuring most runway lights. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to both wings and the horizontal stabilizer.

synopsis: The total loss of engine power for reasons that could not be conclusively determined during postaccident examination.
summary: The pilot experienced a total engine failure on the downwind leg during the first flight after engine installation, forcing a landing in a wooded area. Investigators found unsealed ignition wiring and a potentially disconnected induction tube but could not conclusively determine the cause of the power loss.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control while landing in gusting wind conditions.
summary: The pilot reported that a wind gust during the landing flare caused the airplane to drift left, veer off the runway, and strike a tree with the left wing. Despite rudder inputs, the aircraft came to rest in mud with substantial left wing damage, with no preexisting mechanical anomalies noted.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed and altitude on final approach, resulting in an impact with terrain short of the airport.
summary: The pilot, flying a single-engine airplane on final approach in gusty winds, crashed into a pasture after likely allowing airspeed to decay and descending below the glide path. The pilot attempted a go-around with landing gear in transit, but the aircraft struck the ground and burned, killing the pilot while the passenger survived.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to land on unsuitable terrain, which resulted in the airplane nosing over.
summary: The pilot landing a ski-equipped airplane on a snow-covered lake encountered a snow drift with the left ski, causing the aircraft to nose over. This resulted in substantial damage to the left wing and vertical stabilizer, with no preaccident mechanical anomalies reported.

synopsis: The pilot did not maintain directional control during takeoff.
summary: During takeoff, the pilot reported the aircraft veered left unresponsive to rudder input, prompting an aborted attempt followed by a go-around to avoid runway signs. The aircraft subsequently struck a sign with its right main gear and stabilator, causing substantial damage with no reported mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: A non-certificated foreign pilot flying a Beech A36 from Pontes E Lacerda to Caceres lost control during cruise into deteriorating weather near Mato Grosso. The aircraft impacted terrain, destroying the airplane and fatally injuring the pilot and two passengers.
summary: A non-certificated foreign pilot flying a Beech A36 from Pontes E Lacerda to Caceres lost control during cruise into deteriorating weather near Mato Grosso. The aircraft impacted terrain, destroying the airplane and fatally injuring the pilot and two passengers.

synopsis: The pilot's inability to stop the airplane on a grass runway with undetected ice.
summary: The pilot landed a private aircraft on a turf runway with hidden ice, causing poor braking and an overrun into trees. Post-accident examination found no mechanical failures, attributing the substantial wing damage to the slick surface conditions caused by rain and freezing temperatures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airspeed during an approach in gusty crosswind conditions, which resulted in an inadvertent aerodynamic stall.
summary: A private pilot stalled the aircraft on final approach to runway 17 after landing and re-entering traffic, resulting in a ground impact in a cornfield. The accident occurred because the pilot's ground speed of 45 knots was below the 53-knot stall speed, with no mechanical malfunctions found.

synopsis: The total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident testing of the engine did not reveal any malfunctions or failures that would preclude normal operation. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's improper in-flight fuel management following the loss of engine power.
summary: The pilot departed with the fuel selector on the right tank, which had less fuel, and failed to visually verify quantities. Engine power was lost due to fuel starvation during an uncoordinated turn, leading to a forced landing and collision with a tree because the pilot did not switch to the fuller left tank.

synopsis: The glider pilot released from the tow airplane at a lower altitude than the planned altitude, which resulted in an off-airport landing.
summary: A glider pilot released from a tow plane at 4,000 feet MSL instead of the planned 4,000 feet AGL due to an altimeter setting error. Consequently, the pilot landed short in desert terrain, avoiding a canal but sustaining substantial fuselage damage from a hard landing.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to turn the magneto switch to the off position before moving the propeller to start the engine by hand.
summary: A pilot and passenger were in a small airplane when the pilot failed to start the engine and asked the passenger to exit. The pilot was struck by the propeller after moving it while the magneto switch was in the "both" position, causing the engine to fire and the propeller to rotate rapidly.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate compensation for a wind gust during landing, which resulted in a runway excursion. Contributing to the accident was a windsock partially sheltered by trees that provided inaccurate wind information.
summary: The pilot executed a three-point landing, but a wind gust caused the aircraft to bounce and drift into deep snow, resulting in a nose-over and substantial damage. The pilot attributed the accident to unreported wind gusts caused by trees sheltering the windsock, noting no mechanical failure occurred.

synopsis: The pilot's in-flight misjudgment of fuel remaining resulting in fuel exhaustion and a total loss of engine power. Contributing to the accident was an inadequate fuel quantity for the flight for reasons that could not be determined during postaccident investigation.
summary: The pilot of a twin-engine airplane experienced dual engine power loss due to fuel exhaustion while returning from an offshore island. Despite visual confirmation of 22 gallons preflight, the aircraft ran out of fuel en route, forcing a beach landing after the pilot bypassed an available fuel stop.

synopsis: After landing a Piper J3C-65, the pilot attempted a solo takeoff while the passenger exited the aircraft. The passenger stepped into the rotating propeller and sustained fatal injuries, while the pilot remained uninjured.
summary: After landing a Piper J3C-65, the pilot attempted a solo takeoff while the passenger exited the aircraft. The passenger stepped into the rotating propeller and sustained fatal injuries, while the pilot remained uninjured.

synopsis: The passenger's interference with the flight controls during the initial climb, which resulted in a loss of control and impact with terrain.
summary: During climb through 200 feet, a first-time passenger inadvertently stepped on the rudder pedals, preventing the pilot from controlling the aircraft. The airplane skewed left, descended, and impacted terrain, with post-accident examination confirming no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The student pilot's loss of directional control during the landing roll.
summary: A student pilot conducting solo touch-and-go landings veered left after touchdown on the fifth attempt, exiting the runway despite applying right rudder. The nose gear collapsed, causing substantial firewall damage, with the pilot reporting no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot did not maintain directional control during landing.
summary: The pilot practicing takeoffs and landings in a tailwheel airplane experienced a hard landing that caused the aircraft to veer left. Despite applying full right rudder and brake, the right wing struck the runway, damaging a rib and aileron with no pre-accident mechanical failures found.

synopsis: The pilot-in-command's failure to obtain the proper touchdown point or landing reference speed and failure to initiate a go-around when it became evident that the airplane was landing long and fast. Contributing to the incident was a lack of effective flight crew coordination and communication.
summary: During a night visual approach, the flight crew misidentified the runway and executed a late turn, resulting in a high-speed landing with a tailwind. Despite thrust reverser deployment, the aircraft overran the runway and stopped in mud due to excessive groundspeed and insufficient stopping distance.

synopsis: The pilot did not correctly manage his glide profile during a simulated engine-out forced landing. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision not to add additional engine power, which resulted in a runway undershoot.
summary: During a flight review at a non-controlled airport, a pilot conducting a simulated engine-out landing touched down 300 feet short of the runway in a grassy area. The aircraft's stabilator struck a rebar marker for future lighting located outside the runway safety area.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare and inadequate recovery from a bounced landing.
summary: The pilot reported a hard landing with a bounce and porpoising during the approach phase, leading to a failed go-around attempt where the aircraft yawed left and nosed over. Substantial damage occurred to the left wing and vertical stabilizer, with no preimpact mechanical malfunctions identified.

synopsis: The pilot's premature power reduction, which resulted in a runway undershoot.
summary: The pilot landing an airplane on a snow-bermed runway reduced power to flight idle, causing the main landing gear to strike a snow berm at the threshold. This resulted in substantial damage to the left wheel well bulkhead assembly, with no preaccident mechanical anomalies reported.

synopsis: The separation of the propeller blade tip due to fatigue cracking that initiated at the blade's leading edge.
summary: The pilot experienced extreme vibration at 7,000 feet caused by a propeller blade tip failure due to fatigue cracking. After shutting down the engine and stopping the propeller, the pilot landed safely; post-incident inspection found no anomalies during the prior 72-hour check.

synopsis: The failure of the nosewheel steering pushrod, which resulted in a loss of airplane directional control and runway excursion.
summary: The pilot reported that after touchdown, the aircraft veered off the runway and struck the precision approach path indicator, damaging both wings. A postaccident examination found a failed rod end bearing on the nosewheel steering pushrod, which prevented the pilot from operating the nosewheel steering.

synopsis: A loss or commanded reduction of engine power during the initial climb for reasons that could not be determined because of postaccident impact damage and fire destruction to engine systems and components. Also causal were the pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed and airplane control while attempting to return to the runway despite unpopulated, flat terrain immediately ahead that was suitable for an emergency landing; his decision to take off again with a known problem; and his lack of training in the make and model airplane.
summary: The pilot of an amateur-built Lancair experienced a probable thrust loss during takeoff, likely due to a malfunctioning engine monitoring system. He attempted to return to the runway, stalled the aircraft below 1,500 feet, and crashed in a spin, resulting in a post-impact fire.

synopsis: El Al crew inspected a B747-400F cargo aircraft at Ben Gurion Airport following a hydraulic leak from a flight originating in Australia. A large crack was found in the right-hand body landing gear outer cylinder, with no injuries reported.
summary: El Al crew inspected a B747-400F cargo aircraft at Ben Gurion Airport following a hydraulic leak from a flight originating in Australia. A large crack was found in the right-hand body landing gear outer cylinder, with no injuries reported.

synopsis: an inadvertent encounter with Clear Air Turbulence that resulted in serious injuries to two crewmembers.
summary: Volga-Dnepr flight VDA 4410, an Antonov AN-124-100, encountered severe turbulence at 13,000 feet during approach to Anchorage, recording -0.6 to +2.0 Gs. Two maintenance crew members sustained serious injuries despite one being seated and buckled, while the aircraft remained undamaged.

synopsis: The flight instructor's delayed remedial action, inadequate recovery from a bounced landing, and failure to attain/maintain adequate airspeed during an attempted go-around.
summary: A flight instructor took control from a student pilot during landing, causing the aircraft to bounce, veer off the runway, and stall while attempting a go-around. The plane struck trees, reversed direction, and was consumed by a post-impact fire, with no pre-impact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's encounter with low clouds/low visibility conditions during the initial climb, which resulted in spatial disorientation and loss of airplane control.
summary: A private pilot without an instrument rating crashed a single-engine airplane shortly after dawn departure, likely due to spatial disorientation caused by low clouds and darkness. The pilot's unreported use of anxiety medication may have contributed, though its specific role in the accident could not be conclusively determined.

synopsis: The partial loss of engine power due to magneto malfunction. Contributing to the accident was the lack of adherence to the manufacturer's recommended magneto overhaul schedule.
summary: The pilot experienced engine power loss shortly after takeoff due to a worn magneto bushing causing ignition failure, leading to a forced landing that resulted in a collision with vehicles, trees, and a house. The accident occurred because the magneto had not been overhauled since 1989, exceeding the manufacturer's recommended service interval.

synopsis: The non-certificated pilot's failure to maintain clearance from power lines. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's impairment due to performance-impairing drugs.
summary: A non-certificated pilot flying a stolen aircraft impacted power lines and crashed after the engine sputtered. Post-accident investigation found no mechanical failures, but toxicology results showed drug levels likely caused the pilot's performance failure and loss of clearance.

synopsis: The pilot did not maintain directional control during landing, which resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: During the landing roll, the pilot reported the left main landing gear hit ice, causing the aircraft to veer left and spin over 90 degrees into a snowbank. The airplane nosed over and came to rest inverted, sustaining substantial damage to the fuselage, right wing, and right wing strut.

synopsis: A loss of engine power due to fuel starvation for reasons that could not be determined because the postaccident examination of the airframe and engine did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: A witness reported abnormal engine noise during the motorglider's preflight and takeoff, leading to power loss at 200 feet and a crash into a golf course. Post-accident examination found debris on the fuel pump screen and minimal fuel, but the definitive cause between fuel starvation and carburetor icing could not be determined.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to review or execute any applicable checklist procedures or troubleshoot or take corrective action before landing despite indications that the landing gear was not extended. Contributing to the accident were the pilot's misunderstanding of the air traffic controller's communication that the landing gear was not extended, his desire to land quickly, and an undetermined electrical system anomaly.
summary: The pilot of a twin-engine airplane experienced electrical and landing gear anomalies during a sightseeing diversion and subsequent landing. The pilot landed with the gear retracted due to misinterpreting tower communications and ignoring warning signs, while later unauthorized tampering prevented investigators from determining the root causes.

synopsis: A Robinson R44 II helicopter operated by Bankstown Helicopters collided with terrain near Nowra Aerodrome on February 4, 2012. The aircraft was destroyed and both occupants sustained fatal injuries, with the Australian Transport Safety Bureau investigating the cause.
summary: A Robinson R44 II helicopter operated by Bankstown Helicopters collided with terrain near Nowra Aerodrome on February 4, 2012. The aircraft was destroyed and both occupants sustained fatal injuries, with the Australian Transport Safety Bureau investigating the cause.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed on the base leg for landing, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and loss of airplane control.
summary: The pilot of a rebuilt glider stalled during a left base leg at 100 feet AGL while returning from flight testing. The accident likely resulted from an inaccurate airspeed indicator causing the pilot to fly below the actual stall speed, leading to a collision with trees and the ground.

synopsis: The flight's continued operation through an area containing substantial convective weather activity. Contributing to the accident was the air traffic control/traffic management unit's lack of awareness and recognition of the effect of weather movement on the departure route in use and the flight crew's acceptance of a route and limited weather deviation that was inadequate to maintain a safe distance from the thunderstorms in the area.
summary: A regional jet crew declared an emergency and diverted to Little Rock after a lightning strike during climb-out from Dallas-Fort Worth. The strike damaged the left wing, occurring after controllers delayed providing specific convective weather locations until requested and denied deviation requests due to traffic.

synopsis: the driver's failure to ensure that the belt loader was clear of the airplane before turning.
summary: While SkyWest flight 6261, a Bombardier CL600-2B19, was parked at San Francisco International Airport ready for pushback, a belt loader struck the aircraft. The driver attempted a forward right turn believing there was sufficient room, causing substantial damage to the skin, stringers, and a frame with no injuries.

synopsis: A Ryanair B737-800 crew declared an emergency and descended to 8,000 feet after an AUTO FAIL pressurization message and subsequent manual system failure. Technicians later found ice on the aft outflow valve and water leaking from the tank, with no injuries reported.
summary: A Ryanair B737-800 crew declared an emergency and descended to 8,000 feet after an AUTO FAIL pressurization message and subsequent manual system failure. Technicians later found ice on the aft outflow valve and water leaking from the tank, with no injuries reported.

synopsis: The pilot's incorrect placement of the throttle prior to starting the airplane by hand. Contributing to the accident was that the pilot did not ensure that the airplane was restrained in a manner that would keep it from moving forward.
summary: The pilot hand-started an aircraft with a dead battery and a passenger aboard but failed to chock the wheels. Unexpected high RPM overcame the parking brake, causing the uncontrolled aircraft to roll through a fence and over an embankment, sustaining substantial damage.

synopsis: The captain's failure to maintain airplane control during an attempted crosswind takeoff on a contaminated runway.
summary: Pilots lost directional control during a night takeoff on a contaminated runway in a snowstorm, causing the aircraft to veer off the right side. The excursion resulted in landing gear separation and wing damage, though all occupants evacuated safely with no pre-impact mechanical faults found.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during the landing roll, which resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: During landing, the pilot corrected a crosswind drift but the aircraft veered right despite rudder and brake inputs, departing the runway and striking a sign with the left wing. The pilot suspected a stuck right brake, though post-accident inspection found no brake system anomalies.

synopsis: The failure of the American Airlines aviation maintenance technicians to properly reassemble the two-piece bracket and spray shield on the integrated drive generator fuel-oil heat exchanger that caused a fuel leak that sprayed out and ignited on hot engine cases. Contributing to the cause of the fire was the 767 Aircraft Maintenance Manual's lack of any graphical or pictorial displays of the correct assembly of the two-piece bracket and spray shield.
summary: American Airlines pilots reported a right engine fire on a Boeing 767 shortly after takeoff from JFK, caused by a fuel leak from a misinstalled IDG bracket and missing O-ring following maintenance. The crew shut down the engine, discharged fire bottles, and returned for a safe single-engine landing.

synopsis: The flight instructor's delayed remedial action to prevent the airplane from hitting the hangar door. Contributing to the accident was the student pilot's misuse of the airplane's throttle, and his incorrect use of the wheel brakes.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor lost control of an aircraft while taxiing after the engine spooled up unexpectedly. The instructor failed to stop the plane due to unfamiliarity with the hand brake system, resulting in a collision with a hangar door and substantial airframe damage.

synopsis: The failure of the main rotor mast due to fatigue cracks that originated from corrosion pits. Contributing to the accident was the operator's failure to adhere to the manufacturer's recommended overhaul interval for the main rotor mast.
summary: During takeoff, a pilot aborted after the main rotor mast fractured due to fatigue cracks initiated by corrosion hidden from inspection. The mast had exceeded its recommended overhaul interval by 99 hours, prompting a subsequent FAA Airworthiness Directive to reduce overhaul limits.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power during cruise flight for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: The pilot reported engine roughness and power loss after takeoff, leading to a forced landing where the airplane struck trees. Post-accident examination found fuel in the right tank but no mechanical failures, suggesting the cause was not a pre-existing engine malfunction.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airspeed during a return to the airport after takeoff, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and loss of airplane control.
summary: The pilot requested a return to land during climbout due to an unspecified issue but stalled and crashed while maneuvering for a second approach. Post-accident examination found engine springs shorter than prescribed, though it remains unclear if this caused the incident or resulted from the crash fire.

synopsis: The loss of engine power due to carburetor ice, which resulted in the pilot ditching the airplane into the lake. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision not to apply carburetor heat.
summary: A pilot returning from a cross-country flight ditched the aircraft in a lake due to likely engine power loss from carburetor ice. The pilot drowned, and the investigation found no pre-impact mechanical abnormalities despite conditions favoring ice accumulation.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to ensure that ice and snow were removed from the airplane's surfaces during the preflight inspection, which resulted in an inadvertent aerodynamic stall after takeoff and loss of control of the airplane.
summary: The pilot departed with accumulated ice and snow after declining deicing, causing the left wing to drop and fail to generate lift during takeoff. The aircraft veered left, impacted terrain, and caught fire, with the postaccident examination revealing no mechanical failure.

synopsis: The non-instrument-rated pilot's poor planning and continued visual flight rules flight into instrument meteorological conditions and failure to maintain clearance from mountainous terrain.
summary: A non-instrument-rated pilot flying a volunteer mission diverted due to low ceilings, then collided with mountainous terrain while turning out of a valley. The accident likely resulted from the pilot encountering instrument meteorological conditions without a weather briefing, as no mechanical failures were found.

synopsis: The medical incapacitation of the pilot due to a sudden cardiac arrhythmia or acute myocardial infarction.
summary: During a local flight, the pilot reported returning to the departure airfield before the aircraft disappeared from radar and impacted terrain in a 90-degree nose-low attitude. The investigation concluded the pilot likely became incapacitated by a sudden cardiac arrhythmia or acute myocardial infarction due to extensive coronary artery disease.

synopsis: On February 07, 2012, a Ryanair B737-800 descended below profile during a visual approach to London Gatwick, triggering a terrain message. The flight crew corrected the descent, and the aircraft landed without damage.
summary: On February 07, 2012, a Ryanair B737-800 descended below profile during a visual approach to London Gatwick, triggering a terrain message. The flight crew corrected the descent, and the aircraft landed without damage.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate compensation for the known wind conditions during a hovering maneuver, which resulted in a loss of tail rotor effectiveness and directional control.
summary: During a helicopter training hover, an instructor lost control in 15–20 knot south winds, causing an uncontrollable right yaw and ground impact. The aircraft sustained substantial tailboom and main rotor drive damage, with the instructor reporting no mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The flight crew's loss of directional control during landing on an ice- and water-contaminated runway, which resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: The flight crew landed on a wet, snow-patched runway and lost directional control despite using thrust reversers and brakes. The aircraft veered off the runway at 70 knots, causing main landing gear collapse and substantial right wing damage, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot did not attain and maintain sufficient altitude to clear terrain while maneuvering.
summary: The pilot, while conducting an emergency supply drop for injured snowmobilers, encountered a downdraft after banking left to avoid terrain. Despite control inputs, the aircraft descended and impacted a glacier, sustaining substantial damage to the firewall and wings with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane while landing with a crosswind.
summary: The pilot reported that during landing in a 9-knot left crosswind, the aircraft swerved left, exited the runway, and separated its nosewheel over a grass median dip. The aircraft sustained substantial engine firewall damage, with no mechanical malfunctions found and brake system examination revealing no anomalies.

synopsis: A Gulfstream G-IV operated by Trident Aviation overran the runway and crashed into a ravine during landing at Bukavu-Kamenbe Airport. The accident resulted in four fatalities, including both pilots, and substantial damage to the aircraft with no fire.
summary: A Gulfstream G-IV operated by Trident Aviation overran the runway and crashed into a ravine during landing at Bukavu-Kamenbe Airport. The accident resulted in four fatalities, including both pilots, and substantial damage to the aircraft with no fire.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed during the initial climb, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and a subsequent hard landing, loss of directional control, and ground loop.
summary: During a test flight, the pilot and mechanic experienced a hard landing and ground loop after the aircraft stalled due to inadequate airspeed while the pilot attempted to correct runway alignment. The pilot attributed the incident to right engine power loss, but the mechanic reported no mechanical failures, concluding the stall resulted from the pilot's control inputs.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to apply power during a practice autorotation in order to arrest a high rate of descent, which resulted in an in-flight collision with terrain.
summary: A student pilot and certified flight instructor were involved in a helicopter accident during a straight-in autorotation practice. The aircraft descended too rapidly, struck a mound, and rolled onto its left side due to low rotor RPM and idle power, sustaining substantial damage with no mechanical failure reported.

synopsis: The pilot lost directional control during landing.
summary: The pilot lost directional control while landing on a snow-covered runway, causing the airplane to hit a snow berm and nose over. This resulted in substantial damage to the right wing.

synopsis: The pilot did not reduce the airplane's descent rate prior to the landing flare/touchdown, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: During landing at a remote snow-covered airstrip, a high descent rate caused a hard touchdown that damaged a main landing gear attach fitting. The subsequent partial gear collapse caused the aircraft to veer right, resulting in the right wing impacting a snow bank and sustaining substantial damage.

synopsis: A Liberty Aerospace XL-2 crashed in a field near Coelbe-Bernsdorf, Germany, under unknown circumstances while in visual meteorological conditions. The two crewmembers were fatally injured and the aircraft was destroyed in a post-impact fire.
summary: A Liberty Aerospace XL-2 crashed in a field near Coelbe-Bernsdorf, Germany, under unknown circumstances while in visual meteorological conditions. The two crewmembers were fatally injured and the aircraft was destroyed in a post-impact fire.

synopsis: The student pilot's improper flare and recovery from a bounced landing.
summary: A student pilot with 29 total hours experienced a hard landing and nose gear collapse on runway 27L during his second solo flight after a wind shift caused a bounce. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the firewall, propeller, and left wing, with no pre-accident mechanical failures found.

synopsis: The pilot's physical impairment due to alcohol, which adversely affected his ability to operate the airplane and to maintain clearance from mountainous terrain while operating in dark night conditions.
summary: The pilot of a local night flight crashed into rising terrain after descending below cloud layers and losing radar contact. Post-accident toxicology revealed a blood alcohol concentration of 154 mg/dl, indicating impairment likely caused the loss of terrain clearance.

synopsis: The pilot did not extend the landing gear before landing.
summary: During practice accuracy landings for a checkride, the pilot forgot to extend the landing gear and missed the warning horn due to fixation on maneuvering. The aircraft touched down with gear retracted, causing substantial fuselage damage, with no preimpact mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to conduct low-level passes above a residence and his failure to maintain sufficient altitude.
summary: A witness observed an aircraft making two low-level passes, striking trees on the second pass before impacting the ground. Post-accident examination confirmed the damage but found no evidence of mechanical malfunctions that would have precluded normal operation.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight and in-flight planning and decision-making, including his inadequate weather evaluation and his delayed diversion to a closer airport, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: A pilot flew a single-engine aircraft into known icing conditions despite lacking certification, causing a descent and increased fuel burn that led to power loss. The pilot failed to declare a fuel emergency before the engine stopped, resulting in a crash into a wooded area 15 miles from the diversion airport.

synopsis: The ATSB notified the NTSB of an incident involving a Fairchild SA-227 on February 14, 2012. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the ATSB investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design, with all information to be released by the ATSB.
summary: The ATSB notified the NTSB of an incident involving a Fairchild SA-227 on February 14, 2012. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the ATSB investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design, with all information to be released by the ATSB.

synopsis: The loss of flight instrumentation due to a failed vacuum pump while flying a night without a discernable horizon, which resulted in the pilot's spatial disorientation and an in-flight loss of control and impact with terrain. Contributing was the continued operation of the airplane with a recalled and unsafe vacuum pump.
summary: The pilot lost vacuum-driven instruments due to a failed pump past its replacement time while cruising at 9,500 feet. Reduced visibility and night conditions caused spatial disorientation, leading to a loss of control and a near-vertical collision with terrain.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain yaw control while hovering at high density altitude, which resulted in a loss of tail rotor effectiveness.
summary: The chief pilot of a leased single-main-rotor helicopter experienced a loss of control during a hover while following snowmobilers on a search and rescue mission. The aircraft descended into trees, likely due to loss of tail rotor effectiveness caused by high density altitude, with no mechanical failures found.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during the landing roll, which resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot veered off the runway into mud during the landing roll and, while attempting to climb an incline with added power, skidded into a parked airplane, hangar, and embankment. This caused main landing gear collapse and substantial damage, with no preimpact mechanical failures found.

synopsis: The pilot did not maintain directional control of the airplane during a crosswind landing.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane reported that during the landing roll on runway 34, the left wing suddenly lifted, causing the right wing to strike the runway and the aircraft to tip onto its nose. Postaccident inspection found substantial right wing damage, and the pilot reported no mechanical malfunction.

synopsis: A flight control malfunction while maneuvering for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination revealed no evidence of a mechanical malfunction or failure that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: A pilot conducting documentary flybys in a helicopter experienced an inability to neutralize flight controls during a climbing right turn at 200 feet. The aircraft impacted the ground while maintaining the turn, but post-accident examination found no mechanical failures, leaving the cause undetermined.

synopsis: the maintenance personnel's failure to install the cotter pins that secured castellated nuts on the left elevator vertical hinge bolts, which resulted in the left elevator partially detaching in flight. Contributing to the accident was the failure of maintenance personnel to document the non-routine maintenance procedure that was used to remove and reinstall the elevator during maintenance.
summary: Everts Air Cargo flight 1291, an Embraer EMB-120, experienced uncommanded pitch-downs during descent into Iliamna due to a left elevator partially detaching from missing cotter pins. The damage resulted from maintenance crews using undocumented procedures that removed hinge bolts not specified in the manual, leading to a high-speed, flaps-up landing with substantial aircraft damage.

synopsis: An Embraer EMB-500 experienced an anti-skid brake failure during landing roll at Campo Grande International Airport, causing the right tire to rupture. The pilot and two passengers were not injured, and no other damage was reported.
summary: An Embraer EMB-500 experienced an anti-skid brake failure during landing roll at Campo Grande International Airport, causing the right tire to rupture. The pilot and two passengers were not injured, and no other damage was reported.

synopsis: A loss of engine power due to oil starvation as a result of improper maintenance.
summary: The pilot landed a Mooney on a highway after the engine quit at 4,000 feet due to oil starvation caused by a seized connecting rod bearing. Post-accident examination revealed improper propeller governor gasket installation during maintenance 10 hours prior, which led to the oil leak and subsequent engine failure.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate separation behind a large airplane during landing, which resulted in an encounter with wake turbulence and a loss of control.
summary: The pilot of a small aircraft encountered wake turbulence from a preceding Gulfstream during landing, causing a stall and loss of control. The aircraft struck a light pole and spun into a grass area after the pilot failed to land beyond the larger airplane's touchdown point.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control while landing on a patchy snow-covered runway.
summary: The pilot lost directional control during the landing roll on a patchy snow-covered runway when the airplane contacted a snow patch. The aircraft nosed over and came to rest inverted with substantial damage to the vertical fin and one wing, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's inadvertent stall during a missed approach. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's operation of the airplane in forecasted icing conditions without using all of its anti-ice systems.
summary: The pilot flew an instrument approach in winter storm conditions with anti-ice systems off, flying below the glideslope and decision height. The aircraft likely accumulated ice, causing an aerodynamic stall during a missed approach attempt that resulted in a ground impact.

synopsis: The pilots' inadequate preflight inspection that failed to detect water-contaminated fuel, which resulted in a total loss of engine power.
summary: A pilot and flight instructor experienced engine power loss during a flight review approach due to water contamination in the fuel system. The instructor executed a forced landing that resulted in a collision with a truck, caused by water entering the aircraft while stored outside and undetected during preflight.

synopsis: The failure of both pilots to see and avoid the other aircraft during cruise flight. Contributing to the accident was the failure of air traffic control personnel to issue the helicopter pilot with a prompt and appropriate alternate course of action upon receiving a conflict alert. The failure of both pilots to see and avoid each other during cruise flight, which resulted in a midair collision. Contributing to the accident was the failure of air traffic control personnel to issue the helicopter pilot a prompt and appropriate alternate course of action upon receiving a conflict alert.
summary: A helicopter receiving flight following and an airplane on a local flight collided midair due to ATC call sign confusion, inadequate controller response to radar alerts, and the helicopter pilot's unreported descent and turn into the airplane's path. Both aircraft sustained substantial damage during subsequent forced landings.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: A flight instructor and student in a helicopter experienced a reported loss of engine power during a practice autorotation at 650 feet AGL. The aircraft landed short, became airborne, rotated 180 degrees, and landed on a taxiway, though post-accident examination found no mechanical cause for the power loss.

synopsis: An inadvertent collision with a deer during a night landing.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor experienced a hard landing during a night approach at a non-tower airport, later discovering deer remains on the runway. Post-accident examination revealed substantial damage to the landing gear, engine, fuselage, and propeller with no preexisting mechanical anomalies.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airspeed during the initial climb after takeoff, which resulted in an uncontrolled descent and collision with terrain.
summary: The pilot departed runway 28 and turned right at 75–200 feet AGL following a misinterpreted AFD terrain warning. The aircraft stalled due to excessive pitch and low airspeed, descending into a field and sustaining substantial damage to the right wing spar and fuselage.

synopsis: The fracture of the fan mid shaft due to a stress corrosion cracking initiated by local regions of corrosion pitting, which resulted from oil migration within the shaft and its subsequent degradation.
summary: A FedEx MD-10-30 rejected takeoff from Portland to Oakland due to a No. 1 engine failure caused by a fractured fan mid shaft. The fracture resulted from stress corrosion cracking triggered by synthetic oil breakdown within the engine's dry cavity.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to use the manufacturer's checklist to troubleshoot the perceived malfunction and thereby ensure the position of the landing gear before landing. The reason the landing gear were not down and locked could not be determined, as no mechanical failures or anomalies were reported before the accident or observed during postaccident testing.
summary: During approach, a pilot failed to see the dim landing gear light due to navigation lights being on, leading to a collapsed gear upon touchdown. The investigation found the gear extended normally, but the pilot's checklist omitted checking navigation lights, which masked the indicator.

synopsis: The flight crew of an Eclipse EA-500 experienced a loss of altitude during an ILS approach to Groningen Airport. They executed a missed approach and landed safely with no injuries to the three occupants.
summary: The flight crew of an Eclipse EA-500 experienced a loss of altitude during an ILS approach to Groningen Airport. They executed a missed approach and landed safely with no injuries to the three occupants.

synopsis: The student pilot's loss of directional control during a crosswind landing.
summary: A student pilot aborting a landing due to gusts lost control on a second attempt when a right gust blew the aircraft left off the runway. The plane struck a taxiway sign, collapsing the left main gear and damaging the left horizontal stabilizer, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's inadvertent landing on a frozen lake in dark night conditions.
summary: A pilot flying a wheel-equipped airplane at night mistakenly landed on a frozen lake adjacent to a gravel airstrip instead of the runway. The aircraft nosed over in deep snow, sustaining substantial damage to the wings and fuselage, as the pilot was unaware he had missed the intended landing surface.

synopsis: The AAIB notified the NTSB of a Boeing 737 accident on February 11, 2012. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the AAIB investigation, which will release all information.
summary: The AAIB notified the NTSB of a Boeing 737 accident on February 11, 2012. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the AAIB investigation, which will release all information.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate fuel planning, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: A private pilot without a multi-engine rating experienced dual engine failure in a multi-engine airplane due to fuel exhaustion, resulting in an off-airport landing. The aircraft sustained substantial damage to the left wing and aft fuselage after entering a ditch, with postaccident examination revealing no visible fuel in the tanks.

synopsis: An in-flight encounter with forecasted turbulence, which resulted in a serious injury to a flight attendant. Contributing to the accident was the flight attendant not being seated with her seatbelt fastened when the encounter occurred.
summary: The flight crew received severe turbulence advisories for 22,000 to 30,000 feet and instructed cabin crew to secure service before descent. While descending through 29,000 feet, unfastened seatbelts caused serious injury to one flight attendant and minor injuries to two attendants and one passenger during severe turbulence.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain the proper glidepath during final approach in night visual meteorological conditions, which resulted in a collision with trees.
summary: The pilot reported striking trees 2,400 feet before the runway threshold during a night visual approach due to distraction from red localizer hazard lights and diluted threshold lights caused by high-intensity runway lighting. The impact damaged the left wing spar, lower fuselage, and stabilator, with no preimpact mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The pilot did not maintain directional control while landing on a snow-contaminated runway.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane veered right after applying reverse thrust on a snow-packed runway due to limited braking action. The aircraft struck an ice chunk, causing the right main landing gear to collapse and substantially damaging the right wing.

synopsis: A loss of airplane control for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination of the airplane and engine did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: The airplane impacted a field in a near-vertical attitude 1.2 miles from the airport while returning to the departure airport. GPS data showed the aircraft was above stall speed with no mechanical anomalies found to explain the mishap.

synopsis: The in-flight fatigue failure of the engine's crankshaft, which resulted in the separation of the forward portion of the crankshaft and the propeller.
summary: During climb after takeoff, a pilot experienced total engine power loss when the crankshaft fractured at 6,000 feet, causing the propeller to separate. The pilot forced-landed with minor nose gear damage; investigation attributed the fracture to fatigue cracks near an oil transfer tube, possibly linked to prior cylinder maintenance.

synopsis: Improper clearance and inadequate heat shielding between engine components and the exhaust system, which resulted in an in-flight fire.
summary: The pilot of an experimental aircraft experienced an in-flight engine fire during return to the airport, forcing a landing where the nosewheel separated. Post-accident examination attributed the fire to missing heat shielding between the exhaust and engine components, a modification not required for experimental aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot did not maintain directional control during landing.
summary: The pilot lost directional control during the landing roll on runway 36, causing the aircraft to veer off into a drainage ditch. No mechanical failure was reported, though post-accident examination revealed bent wing ribs, an elevator tube, and a fuselage frame component.

synopsis: The overload fracture of the right main landing gear bellcrank and a securing bolt, which resulted in the collapse of the right main landing gear.
summary: The pilot returned to the departure airport after losing communications with the destination. Upon landing, the right wing lowered due to a fractured bellcrank assembly and bolt, caused by overload separation with no preexisting cracks or corrosion found.

The Iceland Air Accident Investigation Board notified the NTSB of a February 20, 2012, incident involving a Dornier D328. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation as the State of Registry under ICAO Annex 13.

synopsis: The in-flight separation of the wood portion of one main rotor blade while maneuvering at low level, the reason for which could not be determined because postaccident examination did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a single main rotor helicopter for aerial application crashed after a main rotor blade separated in flight. The blade's metal core fractured from overstress, causing rotor imbalance and structural failure, though the specific cause of the wood failure remained undetermined due to incomplete maintenance records.

synopsis: The partial loss of engine power due to the failure of the exhaust valve spring seat for reasons that could not be determined.
summary: The pilot reported an in-flight engine power loss and vibration during cruise, leading to an emergency field landing where the aircraft struck an embankment. A broken No. 4 valve spring seat caused the failure, though the investigation could not determine why the seat broke 134.66 hours before the recommended overhaul.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's delayed intervention and the pilot's lack of experience in tailwheel airplanes.
summary: During a personal flight in a tailwheel airplane, a private pilot practicing landings veered off the runway centerline. The flight instructor took over controls but could not regain directional control, resulting in a left wingtip strike and a ground loop.

synopsis: In-flight collision with birds during initial climb, which resulted in substantial damage to the aircraft.
summary: Delta Flight 1691, an A320-211, struck a flock of birds during initial climb from Minneapolis-St. Paul, causing cabin pressure loss and erratic right airspeed indication. The crew declared an emergency and landed safely, revealing substantial damage to the forward pressure bulkhead and minor damage to the right engine.

synopsis: The pilot's improper preflight planning/preparation and in-flight fuel management, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion during the approach to the destination airport.
summary: The pilot experienced a total loss of power in both engines while descending beneath clouds during an instrument approach. Examination revealed the cause was a complete lack of usable fuel aboard the aircraft.

synopsis: An encounter with convective turbulence during the descent.
summary: Southwest Airlines flight 983, a B737-700, encountered turbulence below 14,000 feet during descent to Fort Lauderdale. Two flight attendants were thrown to the floor while cleaning the galley, resulting in one sustaining a broken leg, though the aircraft remained undamaged.

synopsis: The non-night-qualified pilot's improper decision to depart in dark night visual meteorological conditions, which resulted in his subsequent spatial disorientation, loss of control, and impact with water.
summary: A private pilot and pilot-rated passenger crashed a rented airplane into water during a night VFR flight from Key West to Miami. The accident resulted from the pilot's spatial disorientation due to a lack of horizon and his ineligibility for night VFR operations under his license restrictions.

synopsis: The airplane's encounter with forecast low-level windshear conditions during takeoff, which resulted in a loss of lift.
summary: The pilot departed with two passengers into gusting crosswinds and a tailwind shift, causing the aircraft to sink and strike the ground 2,400 feet beyond the runway. The pilot attributed the accident to low-level windshear and turbulence, reporting no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot exceeded the helicopter's performance, resulting in low rotor rpm and settling.
summary: A commercial helicopter check flight involving a pilot and CFI resulted in an accident during a confined-area landing on a 4,750-foot MSL ridgeline. After the pilot maneuvered off the platform due to a skid not being on the surface, the right skid caught snow, causing the helicopter to flip and sustain damage to the tailboom and main rotor blades.

synopsis: The pilot's inadvertent overboost of the turbocharged engine during initial climb, which resulted in detonation and a partial loss of engine power followed by the pilot's failure to maintain airspeed and the instructor's delayed remedial action, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall. Contributing to the accident was the instructor's improper judgment in acting as a pilot with disqualifying medical conditions and while taking impairing medications.
summary: An instructor pilot flying a turbocharged aircraft stalled and crashed shortly after takeoff due to likely engine overboost and loss of control. The accident was attributed to the pilot's inexperience, cognitive impairment from depression and psychotropic medications, and failure to attempt an emergency landing.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate compensation for wind conditions during landing, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: A helicopter pilot encountered an updraft during a shallow approach to a flat pinnacle with a tailwind. Exiting the updraft caused an abrupt descent resulting in a hard landing that buckled the tail boom and sheared the left landing gear skid.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during a low-altitude maneuver. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's lack of the required rating to operate the airplane.
summary: An unqualified pilot attempted to land an amphibious airplane in a flooded field after a witness waved him off. The aircraft entered a steep bank and impacted the ground left-wing-low due to the pilot's lack of specific seaplane training and an expired flight review.

synopsis: The unexpected engine start during hand propping, which resulted in a serious injury. Contributing to the accident was the lack of communication between the pilot and the individual hand propping the engine.
summary: During a hand-prop start attempt, the individual motioned to pull the propeller without a verbal callout, and the engine unexpectedly started before the pilot could secure the magnetos. The rotating propeller struck the individual's right arm, causing a fracture.

synopsis: The pilot's improper decision to taxi in wind conditions that exceeded the airplane's capability.
summary: The pilot taxiing for takeoff in winds exceeding manufacturer and operator limits experienced the aircraft's tail lifting and nose-over. This occurred on a taxiway subject to an almost direct crosswind.

synopsis: The failure of maintenance personnel to properly secure a portion of the right wing leading edge, which resulted in the separation of the associated section of the leading edge during takeoff and the loss of directional control during the subsequent landing.
summary: During a maintenance test flight at 75 feet, the aircraft pulled right due to right wing leading edge separation caused by missing and improperly torqued screws. The pilot landed but the airplane veered off the runway, crossing a taxiway and ditch before stopping 300 feet away.

synopsis: The pilot's abrupt maneuver in response to a perceived traffic conflict, which resulted in an accelerated stall and a loss of airplane control at low altitude. Contributing to the accident was the air traffic controller's incomplete instructions, which resulted in improper sequencing of traffic landing on the same runway.
summary: An accident pilot and a tower controller were involved during a landing at a tower-controlled airport. The pilot lost control and impacted terrain after over-controlling the aircraft while attempting to follow the controller's late instruction to cut in tight behind another airplane on final approach.

synopsis: The pilot's did not properly secure the airplane prior to rotating the propeller by hand, resulting in inadvertent movement of the airplane and collision with a building.
summary: The pilot hand-propped the engine after electric starter failure, but the parking brake failed to hold, causing the aircraft to roll. Unable to open the door to reduce throttle, the pilot lost control and struck a building, sustaining substantial damage to the left wing, fuselage, and engine mount.

synopsis: The airplane's encounter with moderate turbulence during cruise flight, which resulted in a serious injury to a flight attendant.
summary: During cruise, an aircraft encountered unreported moderate turbulence, causing momentary altitude and roll deviations corrected by the autopilot. This event threw a flight attendant against the structure, resulting in a serious hand injury, with no prior advisories from controllers or other aircraft.

synopsis: The failure of the airplane's engine air inlet system resulting in a total loss of engine power.
summary: The pilot experienced a total engine power loss while turning from downwind to base, causing the aircraft to strike the perimeter fence and sustain substantial right wing damage. Postaccident examination found separated air inlet cowling ducting blocked the carburetor air inlet.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from power lines while maneuvering after takeoff. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision to operate the airplane during the hours of darkness when he had a restriction for daytime flight only due to color vision limitations.
summary: An experimental airplane with two occupants collided with power lines shortly after takeoff before sunrise. The likely cause was conducting the flight before sunrise despite the pilot's daytime-only restriction, which hindered visibility of the barely visible lines.

synopsis: The loss of engine power during climb due to carburetor icing. Contributing to the accident was the limited travel of the carburetor heat valve which prevented application of maximum carburetor heat.
summary: During an instrument instructional climb, a flight instructor and student encountered carburetor icing that caused partial then total engine power loss. The instructor's attempt to use carburetor heat failed due to a restricted valve, forcing a landing despite preflight checks indicating satisfactory conditions.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate compensation for the gusting wind, which resulted in an excessive descent rate and hard landing.
summary: During annual refresher training, a helicopter practicing an autorotation to runway 18 descended below the tree line and suddenly dropped due to lost lift and wind advantage. The hard landing fractured the tail boom, though the pilot reported no mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing.
summary: The pilot reported the aircraft veered and exited the runway upon landing, damaging the left wing, likely due to non-mechanical loss of directional control. Although a metal shaving was found in the left brake bleed valve, examination showed no evidence the brake was locked or malfunctioning.

synopsis: The cargo compartment door of a Learjet 60 en route from Saint Petersburg to Rome separated from the airframe in flight. The aircraft sustained minor damage, but the two crewmembers and four passengers were not injured.
summary: The cargo compartment door of a Learjet 60 en route from Saint Petersburg to Rome separated from the airframe in flight. The aircraft sustained minor damage, but the two crewmembers and four passengers were not injured.

synopsis: the flight attendant inadvertently tripping over a passenger's luggage strap that was protruding into the isle.
summary: During cruise on Delta Air Lines flight 143, a Boeing 767-432ER, one flight attendant sustained serious injuries while delivering meal service. The crew reported the attendant tripped over a passenger's bag, causing the fall.

synopsis: A commercial pilot flying a Cessna T210N from MM16 to MMTC struck high tension wires and impacted terrain near Torreon International Airport. The sole occupant was fatally injured, and the aircraft was destroyed in a postimpact fire.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a Cessna T210N from MM16 to MMTC struck high tension wires and impacted terrain near Torreon International Airport. The sole occupant was fatally injured, and the aircraft was destroyed in a postimpact fire.

synopsis: an encounter with convective turbulence that resulted in injury to a passenger who was not seated when the seatbelt sign was illuminated.
summary: A passenger was severely injured while exiting the lavatory during severe turbulence and lightning strikes at 13,000 feet in IMC. The passenger had ignored the illuminated seatbelt sign despite forecasted convection and a SIGMET for severe thunderstorms in the area.

synopsis: The flight instructor's improper use of the collective control during a practice hovering autorotation, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: A flight instructor conducting a hovering autorotation demonstration for a second pilot executed a firm landing that damaged the helicopter's tailboom. The instructor reported no mechanical failure, noting that improper up-collective application during hovering autorotations is a known cause of hard landings.

synopsis: The pilot did not maintain runway alignment during landing in a gusting crosswind.
summary: The pilot overflew the airport due to unavailable weather data, then initiated a go-around after encountering a 25-knot gust on touchdown. The aircraft drifted left uncontrollably and collided with a stationary airplane, automobile, and hangar, causing substantial damage with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A Cessna 208B operated by Cleiton Taxi Aereo Ltda. impacted a lamppost and terrain during initial climb after takeoff from SWFN. The sole occupant, the pilot, was fatally injured, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft.
summary: A Cessna 208B operated by Cleiton Taxi Aereo Ltda. impacted a lamppost and terrain during initial climb after takeoff from SWFN. The sole occupant, the pilot, was fatally injured, resulting in substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The non-instrument-rated pilot's decision to continue flight into instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in spatial disorientation and a loss of control.
summary: The pilot departed a cross-country flight in marginal weather, intending to stay below 1,900 feet, but encountered instrument meteorological conditions and crashed into a lake. The investigation attributed the uncontrolled, high-speed descent to spatial disorientation, as no mechanical failures were found.

synopsis: The pilot receiving instruction's inadvertent movement of the pitch trim control to the nose-down position while attempting a go-around.
summary: A flight instructor and student practicing simulated engine failures in a traffic pattern descended too low during S-turns. While attempting a go-around, the aircraft pitched down and impacted the ground due to the pitch trim being set to full forward.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power during cruise flight for reasons that could not be determined because of the damage due to the postcrash fire.
summary: The pilot experienced total engine power loss while descending into turbulence at 5,000 feet, likely due to fuel starvation from not switching tanks. Unable to reach an airport, he performed a forced landing in a field, resulting in a post-crash fire that destroyed the fuel system evidence.

synopsis: The pilot did not maintain directional control of the airplane during the takeoff roll.
summary: The pilot veered off the left runway during takeoff, striking a light and embedding the aircraft nose-first into a hangar, causing wing separation and serious injury. Postaccident examination found no mechanical malfunctions, and the pilot could not recall the events.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control while on final approach as he was executing a turn to provide spacing between his airplane and an airplane on the runway.
summary: The pilot of an experimental home-built aircraft, lacking a current medical certificate, attempted a 180-degree turn at 400 feet to avoid another airplane on final approach. The aircraft entered a 45-degree banked turn, descended, and impacted terrain with no preimpact mechanical anomalies found.

synopsis: On February 21, 2012, a commercial pilot flying a Bell 407 helicopter (XA-JMB) near Loma Bonita, Mexico, experienced a loss of engine power and impacted terrain. The sole occupant was seriously injured and the helicopter was substantially damaged.
summary: On February 21, 2012, a commercial pilot flying a Bell 407 helicopter (XA-JMB) near Loma Bonita, Mexico, experienced a loss of engine power and impacted terrain. The sole occupant was seriously injured and the helicopter was substantially damaged.

synopsis: The flightcrew's loss of visual reference to the runway after encountering severe in-flight icing conditions, which resulted in a loss of control while landing and exceedence of the capabilities of the airplane's windscreen anti-ice systems. Contributing to this incident was the failure of the approach controller to relay a pilot report of severe icing conditions near the route of flight to the incident flight crew.
summary: During a night instrument approach in icing conditions, a medical transport flight crew lost visibility due to windscreen ice exceeding anti-ice system capabilities, resulting in a runway excursion and wing strike. The incident was exacerbated by the failure to relay a nearby severe icing pilot report to the crew.

synopsis: The flight instructor's attempted takeoff in gusting wind conditions while the student pilot was adjusting her anti-torque pedals, which resulted in a dynamic rollover event.
summary: During a training takeoff in 28-knot winds, a helicopter rolled right and inverted after the instructor raised the collective. The accident, consistent with a dynamic rollover, occurred because a student was adjusting anti-torque pedals at takeoff, with no mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed and airplane control while maneuvering at a low altitude, which resulted in a stall and subsequent impact with terrain.
summary: Witnesses observed the aircraft performing low-altitude turns before stalling and impacting an elevated drive due to insufficient recovery altitude. Post-accident examination found no mechanical failures, and the engine sounded normal throughout the sequence.

synopsis: The pilot did not maintain control of the airplane while landing in crosswind conditions.
summary: During approach to runway 9, a pilot encountered an unexpected strong crosswind despite calm conditions, causing the aircraft to veer off and nose over after a failed go-around attempt. The pilot reported no mechanical failures, attributing the substantial damage to the left wing and airframe to the sudden wind shift.

synopsis: A Cessna 172N (YV105E) impacted terrain during cruise flight near Zamora, Venezuela, destroying the aircraft and fatally injuring the pilot. The flight originated from SVCS earlier that day, and the investigation remains under Venezuelan jurisdiction.
summary: A Cessna 172N (YV105E) impacted terrain during cruise flight near Zamora, Venezuela, destroying the aircraft and fatally injuring the pilot. The flight originated from SVCS earlier that day, and the investigation remains under Venezuelan jurisdiction.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to follow instruction and to relinquish control of the airplane to the flight instructor in a timely manner, which resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: During a simulated engine-out training flight, a student pilot overrotated and failed to reduce power or relinquish controls to the instructor. Consequently, the aircraft departed the runway and struck a sign, causing substantial right wing damage with no reported mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate compensation for gusting crosswind conditions during landing, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: During a touch-and-go on runway 1, a gust lifted the aircraft to 8 feet before a hard landing prompted an aborted takeoff. The pilot returned safely, but post-flight inspection revealed engine firewall damage with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: fuel exhaustion following missed approaches due to deficient ATC handling under weather conditions which were significantly lower than forecast. The second missed approach may have been initiated due to limited pilot instrument proficiency. Contributing to the severity of the accident was the pilot's decision to attempt an emergency landing in low visibility instead of ejecting when fuel exhaustion was imminent. Also contributing to the accident was an organizational and oversight environment which did not require airman, aircraft, or risk management controls or standards expected of a commercial civil aviation operation.
summary: An ATAC pilot flying an IAI Kfir crashed at Naval Air Station Fallon during an emergency landing attempt due to low fuel, high winds, and snow. Contributing factors included deficient ATC handling, the pilot's lack of instrument proficiency in the Kfir, and a decision to attempt a hazardous low-altitude approach instead of ejecting.

synopsis: The separation of the left rudder cable turnbuckle and the pilot's subsequent loss of directional control during landing.
summary: During the landing roll, the pilot reported the left rudder pedal went slack, causing a skid, main gear failure, and substantial damage. Postaccident examination found the left rudder cable turnbuckle was disconnected with broken safety wire, despite an annual inspection five months prior.

synopsis: Undetermined; the airplane and pilot are missing.
summary: The pilot departed with 25 to 30 gallons of fuel and was lost from radar 23 minutes after takeoff while flying VFR over the Atlantic. The aircraft and pilot remain missing, and while multiple medications were found, the investigation could not determine if impairment or suicide caused the accident due to a lack of physical evidence.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control while taxiing in gusty wind conditions.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped agricultural airplane lost directional control during taxi due to a left quartering tailwind gust, causing the aircraft to veer off the runway. The tailwheel block bolts failed, allowing the spring to strike the ground and stop the rotation, resulting in substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate fuel management, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot experienced a total loss of engine power en route after an intermediate stop, forcing a landing. Examination revealed no usable fuel and no fuel system leaks, indicating fuel exhaustion as the cause.

synopsis: Fuel leaking from the left engine fuel strainer onto electrical connections after engine start, which resulted in a fire.
summary: The pilot observed smoke from the left engine nacelle and rudder pedals shortly after starting the left engine, prompting an immediate shutdown and evacuation. Local personnel extinguished the fire, which likely originated from fuel leaking from the left engine fuel strainer onto adjacent electrical connections.

synopsis: A partial loss of engine power while maneuvering over rough/uneven terrain that was precipitated by the failure of a 3rd stage turbine blade as a result of high-cycle fatigue.
summary: During external load operations, a helicopter's No. 2 engine lost power due to a turbine blade separation caused by high-cycle fatigue. The pilot executed a running landing on rough terrain, resulting in tail boom deformation, as the susceptible turbine wheel had not been replaced per service bulletins.

synopsis: The pilot did not maintain adequate airspeed and airplane control during the go-around, which resulted in the airplane impacting trees.
summary: The pilot reported that while landing a private aircraft on his property, turbulence and gusts prompted a go-around. During a right turn to avoid rising terrain, the pilot failed to maintain flying speed, causing the airplane to impact trees and sustain substantial wing spar damage.

synopsis: The student pilot did not maintain an adequate approach/glide path and altitude, which resulted in a runway undershoot and subsequent collision with trees. Contributing to the accident was the student pilot's lack of flight experience.
summary: A student pilot on his first solo flight crashed a light aircraft 20 feet short of a private dirt strip after a tailwind caused a rapid descent. The right wing clipped treetops during the impact, and the pilot reported no preimpact mechanical malfunctions.
