synopsis: A Piper PA-34-200 conducting a local training flight in Brazil lost control and impacted a lagoon, destroying the aircraft. The two occupants onboard were fatally injured in the accident.
summary: A Piper PA-34-200 conducting a local training flight in Brazil lost control and impacted a lagoon, destroying the aircraft. The two occupants onboard were fatally injured in the accident.

synopsis: The pilot's incorrect glide path, which resulted in a landing area overshoot and a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot departed for a destination with a closed runway, then landed on a short, uphill runway 30 after misjudging its elevation. Being high and fast, he could not go around due to trees, resulting in an off-runway excursion where the left wing struck a tree.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed while in a steep turn, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall/mush at a low altitude.
summary: The pilot of a local flight encountered an aerodynamic stall while executing a steep right turn to enter the downwind leg. Despite applying full engine power, the aircraft lost altitude and collided with a tree, with no mechanical failure found.

synopsis: A loss of control due to spatial disorientation. Contributing to the accident were the private pilot's impairment due to a sedating antihistamine and both pilots' fatigue.
summary: A flight instructor and private pilot crashed a business aircraft during a night instrument approach in IMC, likely due to spatial disorientation, fatigue, and diphenhydramine impairment. The airplane turned left off course and descended rapidly into terrain after the last radar contact, with no mechanical failures found.

synopsis: The South African Civil Aviation Authority notified the NTSB of an October 29, 2013, accident involving a Robinson R22 helicopter. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by SACAA.
summary: The South African Civil Aviation Authority notified the NTSB of an October 29, 2013, accident involving a Robinson R22 helicopter. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by SACAA.

synopsis: The AAIB notified the NTSB of an August 2, 2013, accident involving a Boeing 737-300. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the AAIB investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design.
summary: The AAIB notified the NTSB of an August 2, 2013, accident involving a Boeing 737-300. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the AAIB investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from terrain while maneuvering in likely low-ceiling and low-visibility conditions in mountainous terrain.
summary: The accident pilot flew a single-engine airplane into terrain while crossing mountainous terrain in marginal weather. The pilot likely lost visual contact due to low clouds and high humidity, resulting in controlled flight into terrain despite no mechanical anomalies.

synopsis: The Tanzania Ministry of Transport notified the NTSB of an accident on September 01, 2013, involving a Boeing 737-800 and a Boeing 767-300. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the Ministry.
summary: The Tanzania Ministry of Transport notified the NTSB of an accident on September 01, 2013, involving a Boeing 737-800 and a Boeing 767-300. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the Ministry.

synopsis: A landing gear brake malfunction during the landing for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: The pilot reported that during landing after a glider tow, the airplane nosed over due to a locked right brake, sustaining substantial damage to the rudder, wings, and lift struts. Subsequent examinations found no anomalies in the disassembled brake, which operated normally after reassembly.

synopsis: The fatigue failure of a propeller pitch change pin due to excessive shot peening of the pin's surface during the manufacturing process.
summary: During cruise, a pilot experienced vibration and speed loss caused by a broken propeller pitch change pin, forcing a nose-landing in the desert that substantially damaged the aircraft. The pin failed due to a fatigue crack initiated by excessive shot peening during manufacturing.

synopsis: The pilot's delayed reaction and loss of directional control while performing a simulated engine failure during the takeoff roll. A factor in the accident was the CFI's delayed reaction to the loss of directional control.
summary: During a proficiency check takeoff roll, a simulated engine failure caused the aircraft to veer right and exit the runway. The pilot delayed power reduction while attempting to avoid an antenna, resulting in a collision that caused substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: A Piper PA-28R-200 with one pilot and four passengers impacted terrain near Corumba, Brazil, while en route from Teruel Ipanema Estancia to Santa Gertrudes Airport. The aircraft was destroyed and all occupants were fatally injured under unknown circumstances.
summary: A Piper PA-28R-200 with one pilot and four passengers impacted terrain near Corumba, Brazil, while en route from Teruel Ipanema Estancia to Santa Gertrudes Airport. The aircraft was destroyed and all occupants were fatally injured under unknown circumstances.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing resulting in collision with equipment off the side of the runway. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's intentional landing on a closed runway with a tailwind.
summary: The pilot departed and later landed downwind on a closed runway, striking a construction vehicle with the left wing after technicians moved equipment. The pilot reported no mechanical issues, though NTSB records show this was his fourth accident in three years.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to land on a rough surface with hidden obstructions (holes).
summary: The pilot reported that after landing on a grass airstrip, the aircraft abruptly stopped and nosed over, damaging the rudder and wings. The cause was identified as a 24-inch deep animal-dug hole in the right tire track that was not visible during the approach.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of airplane control during a known one-engine-inoperative condition. The reasons for the loss of control and engine shutdown could not be determined because the airplane was not equipped with a crash-resistant recorder and postaccident examination and testing did not reveal evidence of any malfunction that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: The solo pilot of a Mitsubishi MU-2B-25 reported a left engine shutdown during approach, then lost control and crashed. The investigation concluded the pilot failed to appropriately manage the one-engine-inoperative condition, as the aircraft was not configured per single-engine landing procedures.

synopsis: The noninstrument-rated pilot's improper decision to fly a night instrument approach in instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in the pilot's spatial disorientation and loss of control of the airplane during an attempted missed approach.
summary: A noninstrument-rated private pilot flying an instrument flight plan in night IMC lost radar contact and impacted terrain during a missed approach. The accident likely resulted from spatial disorientation, potentially exacerbated by the pilot's undisclosed use of disqualifying sedating medications.

synopsis: The Transportation Safety Board of Canada notified the NTSB of an accident involving a Swearingen SA227 on November 10, 2013. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the TSB investigation, with all information to be released by the TSB.
summary: The Transportation Safety Board of Canada notified the NTSB of an accident involving a Swearingen SA227 on November 10, 2013. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the TSB investigation, with all information to be released by the TSB.

synopsis: The JIAAC notified the NTSB of an accident on November 7, 2013, involving a Boeing 757-700 and an Embraer E-190. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the JIAAC investigation as the State of Manufacture and Design for the Boeing 757.
summary: The JIAAC notified the NTSB of an accident on November 7, 2013, involving a Boeing 757-700 and an Embraer E-190. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the JIAAC investigation as the State of Manufacture and Design for the Boeing 757.

synopsis: The mechanic's improper installation of the antitorque pedals, which resulted in an in-flight loss of helicopter control.
summary: During a local maintenance hover test, a helicopter lost control when antitorque pedals separated from levers due to missing attachment hardware. The pilot executed an autorotation but the aircraft landed hard and rolled after a mechanic likely failed to reinstall the required bolts nine days prior.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power due to the in-flight separation of the No. 3 cylinder because of the fatigue cracking of its respective mounting studs and through bolts, which resulted from inadequate maintenance by unknown personnel.
summary: A student pilot experienced a catastrophic engine failure at 5,500 feet during cruise, forcing a landing in a swamp that caused substantial fuselage damage. The accident resulted from a No. 3 cylinder separation due to fatigue cracking, likely caused by insufficient torque on through bolts or unapproved sealant.

synopsis: The pilot did not maintain control of the airplane during the go around.
summary: The pilot executing a landing on runway 33 experienced an unresponsive engine during a go-around attempt after a light touchdown. The aircraft bounced, drifted left, and sustained substantial damage to the wings, fuselage, and firewall, though engine inspection revealed no anomalies.

synopsis: The noninstrument-rated private pilot's decision to continue a visual flight rules flight into instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in the loss of airplane control. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to obtain a weather briefing before departure.
summary: A noninstrument-rated private pilot departed on a cross-country flight without a weather briefing or ATC communication, encountering instrument meteorological conditions. The pilot likely lost control of the airplane, resulting in a high-velocity, nose-low impact into overcast skies with a cloud base at 800 feet AGL.

A Bell 206B helicopter suffered substantial damage after losing engine power and executing a forced landing in Matões do Norte, Brazil. The pilot and passenger were not injured during this local flight originating from Flamboyant Heliport.

synopsis: The flight instructor's improper decision to attempt a climb with an excessive pitch attitude for the tailwind condition and flap setting, which resulted in an approach to stall and subsequent off-field landing.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot in a high-pitch attitude with partial flaps and a tailwind approached a stall during a simulated obstacle climb. The instructor executed an off-field landing, causing substantial left wing damage, with no mechanical failures found.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to see and avoid wires while maneuvering at a low-altitude, which resulted in the main rotor blades striking the wires.
summary: A helicopter pilot conducting a low-level survey with two biologist passengers contacted a power line while turning near a river channel. The impact caused substantial damage and the aircraft came to rest in water, with the pilot reporting no pre-impact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed during the initial climb after an excessive takeoff run from a grass airstrip, which resulted in the exceedance of the airplane's critical angle-of-attack and a subsequent aerodynamic stall and loss of control. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's inadequate supervision and delayed remediation.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor stalled a Cessna during takeoff from a 2,600-ft grass runway after lifting off too late. The student raised the nose to clear trees, causing an aerodynamic stall and impact with a tree due to insufficient remaining runway distance.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain terrain clearance while maneuvering at low altitude in hilly terrain.
summary: The pilot flying a small aircraft in rising terrain descended to orbit two black bears, resulting in a collision with the ground. The accident occurred because slow airspeed and bank angle prevented recovery, causing substantial damage to the wings and fuselage with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to follow the Landing checklist and his inadvertent contact with the blast valve after landing, which released propane that was then ignited by an undetermined source.
summary: A commercial pilot and four passengers sustained serious injuries when a balloon burner ignited propane during post-landing defueling. The fire occurred because the pilot failed to close valves or bleed fuel lines per the checklist, allowing gas to release when he bumped the blast valve.

synopsis: The failure of the left brake master cylinder seal, which rendered the left brake inoperative during landing.
summary: During landing, the pilot's left brake pedal hit the floor due to a failed master cylinder seal, rendering the brake inoperative. The aircraft departed the runway, struck a berm, and the nose gear collapsed after the recently rebuilt cylinder failed following 40 service hours.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain the proper pitch attitude during the landing, which resulted in the nose landing gear contacting the surface hard and then separating from the airplane.
summary: The pilot reported that during a straight-in approach, the aircraft became unresponsive to pitch control at speeds between 90 and 80 KIAS, causing a hard nosewheel impact that sheared off the landing gear. The investigation found no pre-impact mechanical failure, concluding the pilot likely failed to maintain appropriate pitch attitude, resulting in the gear strut rupture.

synopsis: The airplane's encounter with a flock of American White Pelicans, which resulted in one bird striking the right outboard wing during en route climb from the departure airport.
summary: During climb to 10,000 feet MSL, the flight crew encountered a flock of birds, and one struck the right outboard wing, causing spar damage. The aircraft returned to the departure airport and landed safely despite a known medium avian hazard risk.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
summary: A student pilot lost directional control while exiting a taxiway at high speed after a final landing, causing the aircraft to veer off the runway and strike a sign. The collision collapsed the nose gear and damaged the firewall, with no reported pre-impact mechanical failure.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to land on an unsuitable surface, which resulted in a nose over.
summary: The pilot landing a tricycle gear airplane on a soft tidal beach nosed over when the gear contacted soft sand, causing substantial damage to the right wing and left lift strut. The pilot attributed the accident to a lack of knowledge regarding tidal beach landing conditions rather than mechanical failure.

synopsis: A loss of engine power due to a crankshaft failure, which resulted in a forced landing.
summary: After takeoff, the pilot returned to the runway following an engine power loss, resulting in a hard landing that crushed the right wing. The pilot attributed the failure to a broken crankshaft likely caused by a center main shaft bearing issue, though no test results were provided.

synopsis: A dragging right brake, which resulted in an un-commanded right turn, and subsequent ground loop.
summary: A flight instructor and student landed a tailwheel airplane that veered right after touchdown, causing the instructor to apply left rudder and brake. The aircraft departed the runway, collapsing the left main gear and damaging the wing, likely due to right brake rotor heat damage.

synopsis: The incorrect installation by the pilot, who was not a certificated mechanic or repairman, of the main rotor head bearing block, which resulted in the in-flight separation of the rotor head.
summary: The pilot/owner of a gyroplane in the traffic pattern suffered a main rotor head separation and impact after installing a bearing block upside down. The unlicensed pilot performed the maintenance, relying on friction to hold the inverted part, which caused the in-flight failure.

The Russian Interstate Aviation Committee notified the NTSB of a Boeing 737-500 accident on November 17, 2013. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the IAC.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to maintain airspeed following a partial loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined during postaccident examination, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and subsequent loss of airplane control.
summary: During a night instructional flight, a flight instructor reported engine problems and attempted a turn back to the airport, resulting in a stall and crash. The investigation could not definitively determine if carburetor icing or a flooded float caused the power loss, but noted the instructor likely failed to maintain airspeed during the maneuver.

synopsis: The pilot/owner's failure to comply with the engine manufacturer's maintenance guidance, which resulted in the total loss of engine power due to the fracture failure of the plastic drive gear for the engine lubricating oil pump.
summary: The pilot of an experimental amateur-built airplane experienced total engine power loss at 1,800 feet AGL due to a fractured plastic oil pump drive gear. The aircraft collided with a sand dune during a forced landing, caused by the gear failure resulting from an engine overhaul performed 12 years prior to the recommended 5-year interval.

synopsis: A partial loss of engine power after departure due to the collapse of the carburetor air inlet duct, which restricted the airflow to the engine. Contributing to the accident was the overdue annual inspection and the installation of the improper air inlet duct.
summary: The pilot experienced a power loss shortly after takeoff due to a compressed, non-compliant carburetor air duct restricting airflow. The aircraft impacted terrain and a tree while returning to the runway, an event linked to the damaged duct and the airplane being overdue for its annual inspection.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to attain a proper glidepath for landing which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: The pilot reported the gyroplane was too high and slow on landing approach, causing a hard landing that collapsed the gear. This resulted in substantial damage to the main rotor blades and tail boom, with no pre-accident system failures reported.

synopsis: On November 16, 2013, a Sikorsky S76 C++ helicopter operated by LG Electronics collided with a 26-story apartment building in Seoul, Korea. Both crew members sustained fatal injuries, and the Republic of Korea Aviation and Railway Accident Investigation Board is investigating the accident.
summary: On November 16, 2013, a Sikorsky S76 C++ helicopter operated by LG Electronics collided with a 26-story apartment building in Seoul, Korea. Both crew members sustained fatal injuries, and the Republic of Korea Aviation and Railway Accident Investigation Board is investigating the accident.

synopsis: A partial loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined in postaccident examinations because fire damage precluded testing of the fuel and several engine accessories.
summary: The pilot reported partial engine power loss and backfiring at 400 feet AGL, forcing a landing into trees that resulted in a post-impact fire. Examination found no pre-impact mechanical malfunctions, but heat damage prevented testing of accessories and fuel, leaving the cause undetermined.

synopsis: A Robinson R22 helicopter (F-GPKA) collided with terrain in Torreilles, France, during an autorotation following a loss of power. The pilot and passenger were uninjured, but the helicopter sustained substantial damage.
summary: A Robinson R22 helicopter (F-GPKA) collided with terrain in Torreilles, France, during an autorotation following a loss of power. The pilot and passenger were uninjured, but the helicopter sustained substantial damage.

The Argentine JIAAC notified the NTSB of an Embraer E-190 accident on November 15, 2013. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation as the State of Manufacture and Design for the engines.

synopsis: An inadvertent collision with a deer during landing.
summary: During the landing flare, a pilot attempted to avoid a deer by raising the left wing, but the left main landing gear struck the animal and separated. The aircraft skidded to a stop with substantial damage to the wing spar where the gear detached.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control during landing which resulted in an impact with the runway surface.
summary: The pilot of a tail-wheel airplane flipped the aircraft inverted during a wheel landing on a dry grass runway after the nose pitched down and the propeller contacted the ground. The pilot attributed the accident to not reacting quickly enough to the downward pitching attitude, resulting in substantial damage to the left wing, strut, aileron, vertical fin, and rudder.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control in instrument meteorological conditions for reasons that could not be determined because examination of the airframe and engine revealed no anomalies that would have precluded normal operation. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's self-induced pressure to make the flight.
summary: The pilot departed in instrument meteorological conditions without a flight plan or weather briefing to attend a funeral. The aircraft crashed into a tree near the destination due to low ceilings and fog, likely caused by the pilot's self-imposed pressure to fly.

synopsis: The pilot's spatial disorientation while operating in dark night conditions in snow showers and his subsequent failure to maintain airplane control, which resulted in overstress of the airplane and an in-flight breakup. Contributing to the loss of control was the pilot's diverted attention while coordinating for an instrument flight rules clearance.
summary: An instrument-rated pilot flying a night VFR flight to Aspen-Pitkin County Airport requested an IFR clearance at 13,500 feet. After the autopilot disconnected, the pilot became spatially disoriented, failed to recognize a left turn, and the aircraft exceeded design stress limits during a rapid descent, resulting in an in-flight breakup.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff.
summary: A student pilot in a single-engine airplane departed the left side of runway 13 during takeoff after the right wing rose unexpectedly despite left crosswind correction. The aircraft struck a thousand-foot marker, sustaining right wing spar damage, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to complete a landing checklist and extend the landing gear, which resulted in a gear-up landing. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's diverted attention to the weather during approach.
summary: The pilot encountered windshear and turbulence during final approach, causing an overshoot and high-speed landing. Distracted by controlling the aircraft, he failed to perform the gear check, resulting in a landing with partially extended gear despite no mechanical faults found.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane following an inflight deployment of the left engine thrust reverser. Contributing to the accident was the flight crew's failure to perform the appropriate emergency procedures, the copilot's lack of qualification and capability to act as a required flight crewmember for the flight, and the inflight deployment of the left engine thrust reverser for reasons that could not be determined through postaccident investigation.
summary: A twin-engine jet crashed into the ocean after the crew failed to identify an in-flight left thrust reverser deployment during takeoff. The pilot and unqualified copilot did not use checklists or follow emergency procedures, resulting in loss of control and impact.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airspeed while maneuvering for a precautionary landing after the light sport airplane started vibrating, which led to an inadvertent aerodynamic stall.
summary: The pilot reported vibration in a light sport airplane during initial climb after takeoff. After an improper runway landing attempt, the aircraft stalled and impacted an adjacent field, though post-accident examination found no mechanical anomalies or determined vibration source.

synopsis: The airplane's inadvertent encounter with clear air turbulence during cruise flight, which resulted in a serious injury to a flight attendant.
summary: During cruise at FL360, the aircraft encountered clear air turbulence for 3 to 5 seconds while the seatbelt sign was illuminated. A flight attendant fell and fractured her ankle, though the flight subsequently returned to smooth conditions and landed uneventfully.

The Swiss Accident Investigation Board notified the NTSB of an incident involving a Boeing 737-400 on November 10, 2013. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the SAIB.

A flight instructor and student in a Robinson R44 II were fatally injured when the aircraft impacted forested terrain near Neuhausen ob Eck, Germany, during a training flight in foggy instrument meteorological conditions with 100 meters visibility.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to determine the actual onboard fuel quantity before beginning the flight, which resulted in a complete loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's habitual reliance solely on the cockpit fuel flow/totalizer unit to determine fuel quantity rather than measuring the actual amount.
summary: The owner/pilot and passengers experienced a complete engine power loss during cruise due to fuel exhaustion after relying solely on a fuel totalizer without verifying tank levels. The aircraft subsequently crashed into a berm at a military facility after the pilot failed to align with the runway in time.

A Bell 407 helicopter sustained substantial damage during a hard landing near Rio Ablajo, Honduras, while en route from Tegucigalpa to Juticalpa. The pilot and six passengers were uninjured, and the cause of the incident remains undetermined.

synopsis: the flight crew's failure to properly identify the airport and runway of intended landing. Contributing to the incident was the flight crew's failure to follow company procedures for crosschecking navigational information and visual cues to verify the airport and runway of intended landing.
summary: The flight crew descended below 4,000 feet and landed at the wrong airport (KAAO) instead of KIAB after misidentifying a well-lit runway. The error occurred because the pilots discontinued the RNAV approach without verifying their position, and the minimum safe altitude software failed to warn the controller.

A Bell 212 helicopter operated by United Heli Charters collided with terrain during cruise flight near Murbad, India, while en route from Juhu to Nagpur. The accident destroyed the aircraft and resulted in the fatal injuries of two flight crew members and three passengers.

synopsis: The student pilot's improper flare while performing an autorotation and the flight instructor's delayed remedial action to correct the high sink rate, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot experienced a hard landing during a helicopter autorotation training exercise. The student flared too low, causing an unrecoverable high descent rate that resulted in skid spread and a severed tailboom from rotor blade flex.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control after starting the engine, which resulted in a collision with a building.
summary: The pilot reported that after opening the throttle slightly to start a warm engine, the aircraft surged to high RPM and collided with a fixed base operator building despite the parking brake being set and feet on the brakes. Examination of the brake system revealed no anomalies.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to extend the landing gear before landing. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's improper use of the checklist.
summary: The pilot accepted an ATC instruction to cross a passenger jet on final, which disrupted his checklist and caused him to forget extending the landing gear. The aircraft subsequently landed gear up, resulting in substantial fuselage damage with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion, which resulted from the pilot's inadequate preflight inspection and preflight and inflight fuel planning that did not account for increased headwind.
summary: The pilot departed with an estimated 6.5 to 8.5 gallons of usable fuel but encountered stronger headwinds than anticipated, increasing flight time to 1 hour 15 minutes. The engine lost total power due to fuel exhaustion, forcing a landing in a field with only 0.5 gallon remaining.

synopsis: The pilot's improper maintenance of the airplane's fuel system, which resulted a loss of power in the left engine due to fuel starvation. Also causal was the pilot's failure to maintain minimum controllable airspeed following the loss of engine power, which resulted in a loss of airplane control.
summary: The pilot, who was not a certified mechanic, lost control during initial climb after the left engine suffered fuel starvation due to improperly reconnected fuel control cables from his unauthorized troubleshooting. The aircraft struck trees and crashed because the pilot failed to feather the propeller or retract the landing gear, causing airspeed to drop below minimum controllable limits.

A BAE 146 experienced an engine fire during a power check at Norwich International Airport. Maintenance crews successfully shut down the engine and extinguished the fire with no injuries reported, while the AAIB investigates the incident.

synopsis: A Tropicair Cessna Grand Caravan experienced an engine failure and crashed during a forced landing near Kamusi airport, Papua New Guinea. The accident resulted in three fatalities and substantial damage to the aircraft.
summary: A Tropicair Cessna Grand Caravan experienced an engine failure and crashed during a forced landing near Kamusi airport, Papua New Guinea. The accident resulted in three fatalities and substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The captain's decision to initiate a visual flight rules approach and attempted landing into an area of instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in the airplane touching down short of the runway. Contributing to the accident was the operator's inadequate procedures for operational control and flight release and its inadequate training and oversight of operational control personnel. Also contributing to the accident was the Federal Aviation Administration's failure to hold the operator accountable for correcting known operational deficiencies and ensure compliance with its operational control procedures.
summary: The flight crew of a charter flight landed short of the runway during a visual approach in deteriorating visibility, causing gear separation and substantial damage. The accident resulted from the crew losing sight of the runway and an untrained flight coordinator failing to properly assess risks or discuss weather conditions before releasing the flight.

aircraft: Quad City Ultralight Acft Corp CHALLENGER II
synopsis: A loss of engine power due to the spark plug coming out of the cylinder head.
summary: A sport pilot experienced engine power loss during takeoff in an experimental light sport airplane, forcing an off-airport landing where the aircraft struck a fence post. Postaccident examination revealed the number 2 spark plug had pulled out of the cylinder head, causing substantial damage to the horizontal stabilizer and fuselage.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined based on the available evidence.
summary: The pilot/owner flew an airplane containing mixed aviation and automotive gasoline, experiencing total engine power loss on downwind. This caused a forced landing into a ditch with substantial fuselage damage, likely due to fuel contamination despite pre-flight samples appearing clear.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to check the fuel tanks for contaminants after fueling, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to water contamination.
summary: The pilot failed to check fuel tanks for contaminants after refueling, leading to water freezing in the manifold valve and total engine power loss at 8,500 feet. This caused a forced landing attempt where the aircraft struck an unmarked power line before contacting the ground.

synopsis: The failure of the No. 2 connecting rod due to oil starvation, which resulted in a total loss of engine power.
summary: During approach, the pilot experienced a loud pop and total engine power loss, forcing a field landing that caused substantial fuselage damage. Teardown revealed No. 2 connecting rod separation due to oil starvation, possibly linked to flaking unapproved coating in the rocker covers.

synopsis: The student pilot's decision to attempt flight into instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in a loss of control and ground impact.
summary: A solo student pilot departed an uncontrolled airport in poor weather and impacted terrain two miles away while attempting to climb through overcast clouds. The accident was likely caused by the pilot's stress-induced decision to fly despite having insufficient instrument training and losing control in the clouds.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to initiate a visual flight rules approach into an area of instrument meteorological conditions at night and the flight coordinators' release of the flight without discussing the risks with the pilot, which resulted in the pilot experiencing a loss of situational awareness and subsequent controlled flight into terrain. Contributing to the accident were the operator's inadequate procedures for operational control and flight release and its inadequate training and oversight of operational control personnel. Also contributing to the accident was the Federal Aviation Administration's failure to hold the operator accountable for correcting known operational deficiencies and ensuring compliance with its operational control procedures.
summary: A commuter pilot diverted a night VFR flight due to deteriorating weather but failed to activate airport lighting because his radio was tuned to the wrong frequency. The pilot subsequently lost situational awareness in fog and ice, resulting in a controlled flight into terrain, while company risk management failures and inadequate FAA enforcement contributed to the accident.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain control of the helicopter during the attempted takeoff, and the flight instructor's inadequate supervision of the student pilot.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor practicing hovering autorotations in a helicopter experienced a ground strike when the student rapidly increased throttle and applied full left anti-torque pedals. This caused the tail to strike the ground, resulting in substantial damage before the instructor regained control and performed a successful autorotation.

synopsis: A stuck exhaust valve, which resulted in a total loss of engine power at low altitude. Contributing to the accident were the pilot's decision to fly at a low altitude, which reduced his forced landing options when the loss of engine power occurred; and poor long-term engine maintenance, which resulted in the buildup of combustion by-products on exhaust valve parts. Contributing to the pilot's poor aeronautical decision-making was his underlying attention deficit hyperactivity disorder.
summary: An inexperienced pilot maneuvering a newly acquired airplane at low altitude suffered an engine power loss caused by a stuck exhaust valve due to poor maintenance. The pilot's undisclosed ADHD and low experience likely contributed to the low-altitude flight, resulting in a crash into a telephone pole and house when forced to land in confined terrain.

The Namibia Ministry of Works and Transport notified the NTSB of an Embraer ERJ-190 accident on November 30, 2013. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design of the engines.

synopsis: The failure of the hydraulic power pack, which prevented the extension of the landing gear and resulted in a partial gear-up landing.
summary: During a maintenance test flight, the pilot could not extend the main landing gear due to a failed hydraulic power pack containing a defective thermal relief valve and four poppet assemblies. This malfunction forced a partial gear-up landing where the left horizontal stabilizer struck the runway.

synopsis: The pilot's abrupt maneuver, which exceeded the structural limits of the left wing and resulted in its in-flight separation.
summary: The pilot of an experimental, amateur-built airplane experienced left wing separation during the climb phase of a cross-country flight. The accident likely resulted from an abrupt maneuver, possibly to avoid migrating birds, which caused excessive g-forces leading to structural overload and wing failure.

synopsis: The pilot's in-flight loss of airplane control due to spatial disorientation while operating in dark night instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in the exceedance of the airplane's design stress limitations and a subsequent in-flight breakup. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's distraction by the reported malfunction of the autopilot system.
summary: A pilot flying an instrument flight rules flight at night reported autopilot trouble to air traffic control before losing radar contact. Investigators concluded the pilot likely became distracted by the malfunction, experienced spatial disorientation in instrument meteorological conditions, and lost control, causing the aircraft to descend and break up.

aircraft: Moffitt Oscar/ Kit Prostar A/C PT2
synopsis: The airplane owner/pilot 's failure to follow the gascolator manufacturer's recommendations for installing and safety wiring the gascolator strainer bowl, which resulted in the bowl separating and a total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
summary: During a test flight of an experimental amateur-built airplane, the pilot experienced total engine power loss on final approach due to fuel starvation. The cause was a missing gascolator strainer bowl, which separated because it was not installed and safety wired per the manufacturer's service letter.

synopsis: On November 29, 2013, a UK-registered EC-135 T2 helicopter, G-SPAO, impacted a public house near Glasgow. The crew of three and six other persons were fatally injured, and the investigation is under the jurisdiction of the United Kingdom government.
summary: On November 29, 2013, a UK-registered EC-135 T2 helicopter, G-SPAO, impacted a public house near Glasgow. The crew of three and six other persons were fatally injured, and the investigation is under the jurisdiction of the United Kingdom government.

synopsis: The airplane's collision with a deer on the runway during landing.
summary: The pilot struck a deer with the right wing during landing, causing substantial damage and veering off the runway down an embankment. The pilot reported no preimpact mechanical malfunctions and stated there was insufficient room to abort the landing.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane, which resulted in a collision with terrain.
summary: The pilot landing a wheel/ski-equipped airplane on a frozen lake struck a hidden hole while correcting a veer, causing the right main landing gear leg to separate. This resulted in substantial damage to the right wing and aileron, with no preaccident mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The noninstrument-rated pilot's failure to obtain weather briefings immediately before and during the flight and his continued flight into icing conditions, which resulted in the airplane's loss of performance and the subsequent controlled descent into trees and terrain.
summary: A noninstrument-rated private pilot flying a night cross-country flight entered instrument meteorological conditions and encountered structural icing. Unable to maintain altitude, the aircraft descended and impacted trees and the ground, sustaining substantial damage to the wings, landing gear, and horizontal stabilizer.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff.
summary: The pilot reported that during takeoff from a grass strip, added passenger weight caused hesitation, and uneven engine acceleration at rotation induced adverse yaw. This led to a collision with trees and terrain on the runway's right side, causing substantial airframe damage despite no reported mechanical deficiencies.

synopsis: The flight crew's excessive elevator input during a rapid descent under night lighting conditions, which resulted in the overstress and breakup of the airplane. Contributing to the accident was an initial loss of airplane control for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination revealed no mechanical anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: The captain and first officer of a twin-engine turboprop cargo aircraft lost control during a night descent to 3,000 ft, causing the airplane to break up at 1,500 ft. Investigators found no mechanical failures but concluded the crew likely overstressed the airframe while attempting to arrest a rapid descent in darkness.

synopsis: The inflight separation of the upper and lower right engine cowlings for reasons that could not be determined based on available evidence.
summary: The flight crew of a twin-engine jet heard a bang and experienced yawing during initial descent when the right engine cowlings separated and struck the horizontal stabilizer. The aircraft landed normally, but the cause remained undetermined because the quick-release fasteners were not recovered.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to continue visual flight into deteriorating weather, which resulted in an encounter with instrument meteorological conditions and subsequent inability to maintain clearance with terrain.
summary: A pilot operating a single-engine aircraft under day VFR en route from Nashville to Greenville at 9,500 feet became disoriented while climbing back to VFR on top after encountering lower-than-reported ceilings. The pilot subsequently struck a tree and impacted a mountain, causing substantial damage to the fuselage, wings, and empennage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's mismanagement of available fuel and incorrect use of the fuel boost pump which resulted in a total loss of engine power at a low altitude.
summary: The pilot of a single-engine aircraft experienced engine power loss during cruise at 500 feet after switching fuel tanks and activating the boost pump, likely flooding the engine. This resulted in a forced landing where the aircraft nosed over on wet ground, with no mechanical failures found.
A Piper PA-34-220T with one pilot and two passengers collided with Corisco Mountain during climb from Parati to Sao Paulo. The aircraft was destroyed and all three occupants were fatally injured.

synopsis: The failure of the pilot to maintain directional control during landing.
summary: A pilot flying a tailwheel aircraft on final approach to runway 18 encountered a sudden left wing lift and yaw during the flare in crosswind conditions. The right wing contacted the runway, causing a bounce and 180-degree turn, though the pilot reported no mechanical failure.

synopsis: The operation of the airplane by the uncertificated student pilot, his failure to recognize conditions conducive to structural icing, and subsequent decision to depart in conditions conducive to structural icing, resulting in a severe icing encounter and forced landing.
summary: An uncertificated student pilot and passenger encountered rapid ice accumulation during a cross-country climb, leading to a forced landing attempt. The aircraft struck a power line guy wire and road sign after the engine lost power during a second go-around, sustaining substantial damage.

synopsis: The loss of engine power during cruise flight for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examinations of the airplane and engine did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: During a personal cross-country flight, the pilot experienced an engine failure at 3,500 feet MSL after turning off carburetor heat. Despite failed restart attempts, he executed a forced landing into a soccer field where the aircraft collided with a car, trees, and terrain; the cause of the power loss remained undetermined.

synopsis: A partial loss of engine power as a result of contamination of the engine's fuel supply, and the pilot's impaired performance due to his use of diphenhydramine, which resulted in his inability to complete a forced or precautionary autorotative landing successfully.
summary: A helicopter pilot crashed into a field after refueling from a truck, likely due to fuel contamination causing engine power loss. The pilot's ability to perform an emergency autorotation was further impaired by therapeutic levels of diphenhydramine in his system.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of airplane control while maneuvering after takeoff in gusty wind conditions.
summary: The pilot and passenger departed west against airport norms, entered a steep left turn, and impacted terrain. The accident occurred in gusty westerly winds with no pre-impact mechanical failure found.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control during a missed approach in night instrument meteorological conditions due to spatial disorientation and a lack of instrument proficiency.
summary: A pilot flying an IFR night approach in low IFR conditions deviated below and right of the final approach fix before executing a nonstandard missed approach. The aircraft subsequently collided with a retaining pond, likely due to spatial disorientation and a lack of instrument proficiency.

synopsis: The student pilot's in-flight loss of control while attempting to return to the runway following a loss of engine power. The cause of the loss of engine power could not be determined because the postaccident examination did not reveal any anomalies.
summary: A student pilot without a solo endorsement or mechanic certificate crashed a farm aircraft with a new carburetor after an unexplained engine power loss. Investigators could not determine if the cause was mechanical or carburetor icing, as no pre-impact anomalies were found.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate flight planning and decision to land on the soft grass/turf runway which resulted in a nose over.
summary: The pilot departed paved Runway 36L to land on grass Runway 36R due to ice on the paved surface. During rollout, the aircraft hit a soft spot in the turf, causing it to nose over and sustain substantial damage to the wings and tail with no reported mechanical failure.

synopsis: The failure of the torsional drive coupling, which resulted in a loss of drive to the main rotor system during low-altitude flight.
summary: The pilot-owner experienced an engine overspeed and rotor slowdown during low-altitude frost control, forcing a hard autorotation landing. The main transmission torsional drive coupling failed due to sheared lugs, likely from prior damage or exceeding service life, as maintenance records were unavailable.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate wing clearance from a runway sign while taxiing.
summary: A student pilot flying a glider struck a runway sign with the left wing while turning left after landing. The aircraft exited the runway onto grass with substantial wing damage, though the pilot reported no mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control during landing, which resulted in impact with a runway identifier sign, and the flight instructor's delayed remedial action to take the controls and initiate a go-around.
summary: A flight instructor and private pilot practicing touch-and-go landings drifted right and struck a runway identifier sign. The impact separated a wing spar section and bent the aileron, prompting a go-around after the instructor felt a buffet.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during landing due to his inadequate compensation for the tailwind.
summary: The pilot landed an ice-accumulating aircraft with asymmetric gear extension and a quartering tailwind, exiting the runway and collapsing both main landing gear. The investigation attributed the loss of directional control to inadequate compensation for the tailwind rather than runway ice.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane lost control during the landing roll, causing the aircraft to ground loop right. The left wing and elevator sustained substantial damage upon impact, with the pilot reporting no mechanical failures.

synopsis: The passenger's accidental discharge of the net gun which resulted in the net going through a main rotor blade.
summary: During a hover at 100 feet, a passenger accidentally discharged a net gun, causing the net to strike and damage the main rotor blades. The pilot landed the helicopter safely, and post-accident examination confirmed no pre-existing mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control during the landing sequence.
summary: The pilot reported ice on the wings prior to landing and activated de-ice boots. During the flare at 12 feet, the aircraft buffeted, stalled during a go-around, and the left wing impacted the ground, causing substantial damage before skidding off the runway.

synopsis: The total loss of engine power due to oil starvation because of a fractured governor oil line, which resulted from the improper installation of the governor oil line assembly during the last oil line replacement.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine failure in cruise due to an oil leak from a fractured governor line, forcing a landing that damaged the left wing. The line fractured because it was inadequately supported by a single clamp, violating an airworthiness directive and service bulletin requiring two supports.

A Brazilian pilot and four passengers were fatally injured when a Britten Norman BN-2A (PT-WMY) impacted the ground shortly after takeoff from Novo Progresso Airport. Witnesses reported the aircraft made a forced landing en route to Aldeia Pykany Airport.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control of the helicopter when it entered a settling with power condition during sudden gusty wind conditions on takeoff resulting in the helicopter subsequently impacting terrain.
summary: A helicopter pilot departing a helipad experienced an unexplained sink during climb near a roadway and elected to impact terrain to avoid occupied trailers. The pilot reported no mechanical issues or weight and balance problems, noting that calm winds had shifted to gusting from the southwest after the accident.

synopsis: The loss of engine power due to the fracture of multiple blades on the compressor turbine wheel, which resulted in a ditching. The reason for the blade failures could not be determined due to secondary thermal damage to the blades.
summary: An airline transport pilot ditched a commuter aircraft in the ocean shortly after takeoff due to total engine power loss caused by fractured compressor turbine blades. One passenger died from cardiac arrhythmia while wearing an infant life vest, likely because the pilot failed to provide a required safety briefing on flotation equipment usage.

synopsis: The pilots improper flare, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: The pilot landing a tailwheel-equipped airplane at an off-airport site added power after feeling the aircraft sink, causing a hard bounce and substantial fuselage damage. The pilot reported no pre-accident mechanical malfunctions.

On March 16, 2011, a Bell 412EP helicopter (A6-FLV) experienced a failure of the landing gear aft cross tube while loading at Zakum Field, UAE. The General Civil Aviation Authority is investigating the incident with assistance from the NTSB.

On October 4, 2013, the pilot of a Rockwell Commander 112, SE-FLS, lost directional control during rollout after landing, causing a runway excursion. The aircraft was substantially damaged, but there were no injuries.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed while maneuvering at a low altitude, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall/spin and subsequent impact with terrain.
summary: A pilot flying with two passengers for cattle search maneuvered at 300–500 feet AGL in mountainous terrain before impacting the ground in a nose-low attitude. The accident resulted from an inadvertent stall/spin due to low airspeed, with toxicology showing recent marijuana use but no confirmed impairment.

synopsis: The flight crew's improper in-flight fuel planning lead to fuel exhaustion, which resulted in a complete loss of engine power.
summary: A private pilot and certified flight instructor flying a Cessna 150 experienced an engine power loss at 6,000 feet MSL, forcing a landing that damaged the aircraft. Investigators found no fuel in the tanks and no mechanical failure, indicating fuel exhaustion caused the accident.

synopsis: The failure of the copilot's windshield inner layer due to a peel chip that developed as a result of mechanical and thermal expansion stresses.
summary: During cruise at flight level 190, the copilot's inner windshield cracked due to a peel adhesion chip caused by thermal expansion stresses between the glass and vinyl interlayer. The pilot executed a precautionary landing without incident, and the windshield was later redesigned to reduce these stresses.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to correct for the student pilot's loss of aircraft control in a timely manner during takeoff. Contributing to the accident was the instructor's inability to see the taxiway sign from the rear seat.
summary: A student pilot and certified flight instructor in a tailwheel airplane drifted off the runway right after liftoff and struck a taxiway sign. The impact tore the fuselage fabric and bent structural tubing, though the CFI attributed the veer to student handling rather than mechanical failure.

synopsis: The pilot's continued flight into known light-to-moderate icing conditions over mountainous terrain. Contributing to the accident was the loss of engine power due to induction icing.
summary: An instrument-rated pilot flying an aircraft not certified for icing encountered moderate icing and engine power loss while descending below the controller's 12,000-foot terrain clearance minimum. The pilot crashed into terrain after losing engine power, likely caused by structural and induction icing during continued flight in known icing conditions.

synopsis: The pilot's operation of the airplane with underinflated tires, which resulted in the right tire's failure during takeoff and a subsequent runway excursion.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff after the right main tire failed due to underinflation, causing the aircraft to depart the runway and sustain substantial right aileron damage from uneven ground. Examination confirmed the tire failure resulted from low pressure rather than manufacturing defects or foreign objects.

On September 15, 2013, a solo pilot operating a Piper PA-32-301T sustained minor damage to the aircraft during landing at Lille Lesquin airport. The pilot was not injured while returning from a local pleasure flight.

synopsis: The student pilot's loss of control during landing in gusting wind conditions. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision to land with gusting wind.
summary: A student pilot conducting a supervised solo flight experienced a right wing lift and left veer shortly after touchdown in winds exceeding 10 knots gusting above 20 knots. Despite applying right rudder and full right aileron, the aircraft nosed over and impacted the runway surface.

synopsis: The ANSV notified the NTSB of an incident involving a Boeing 737-800 on October 29, 2013. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation as the State of Design and Manufacture.
summary: The ANSV notified the NTSB of an incident involving a Boeing 737-800 on October 29, 2013. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation as the State of Design and Manufacture.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control while maneuvering the airplane in the traffic pattern at night. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's impairment from the use of illicit drugs.
summary: A pilot and passenger departed on a night personal flight, but the pilot returned to the airport due to cabin heat issues. The aircraft impacted terrain after the pilot, likely impaired by methylone, failed to maintain control despite multiple EGPWS warnings.

synopsis: A loss of airplane control during takeoff for reasons that could not be determined due to the postaccident condition of the elevator control system.
summary: During a night takeoff practice, a pilot lost elevator control at 10–20 feet, causing the aircraft to pitch down and collapse its nose gear upon landing. Although the pilot cited recent trim issues, post-accident examination found no pre-impact mechanical malfunctions, though impact damage prevented a complete functional check.

synopsis: A bird strike during takeoff.
summary: During a power-off landing practice climb at 100 feet, a bird struck the left wing leading edge. The pilot landed safely, but post-flight inspection revealed substantial damage to the left wing.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during an attempted go-around for reasons that could not be determined based on the available evidence. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's and pilot's decision to continue flight after experiencing repeated problems upon landing.
summary: A flight instructor and private pilot experienced a runway excursion and landing gear collapse during a flight review landing due to a severe left turn. Investigators could not determine if an unrecovered landing gear bolt caused the loss of control or if the loss of control caused the gear failure.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane after the canopy opened on takeoff. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to properly secure the canopy latch before takeoff.
summary: The pilot reported that shortly after takeoff, the canopy popped open due to an unsecured latch, causing excessive drag and a hard landing. Post-accident examination found no mechanical faults, suggesting the pilot failed to properly secure the latch before departure.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight and inflight fuel planning, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion. Contributing to the pilot's injuries was his failure to use the available shoulder harness.
summary: The pilot reported total engine power loss 60 miles from the destination and crashed into a swamp after radio contact was lost. The accident resulted from fuel exhaustion, as only 2.5 gallons remained, and the pilot died of head trauma because he was not wearing his shoulder harness.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to position the fuel selector handle in a fuel tank detent, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation. Contributing to the pilot's fatal injuries was the separation of his shoulder harness due to overload in an area of excessive fraying.
summary: During approach, the pilot lost engine power after inadvertently leaving the fuel selector between tank detents, causing a crash into trees. The pilot died from blunt force trauma after his shoulder harness separated due to excessive webbing fraying that exceeded maintenance limits.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to abort the takeoff with insufficient runway remaining, which resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: During takeoff for a scheduled commuter flight, the pilot aborted after the aircraft briefly became airborne and settled back on the runway. With insufficient runway remaining to stop, the pilot reapplied power, causing the airplane to impact the perimeter fence and sustain substantial damage to the right wing and empennage.

synopsis: The noncertificated pilot's failure to maintain airspeed, which resulted in an inadvertent stall during landing.
summary: A noncertificated pilot flying an unregistered airplane stalled while attempting to land on a runway. The aircraft nosed down onto the runway in calm wind conditions, though the pilot recalled no details of the accident.

On November 28, 2013, a SAAB 2000 (HB-IZW) experienced an engine failure during climb out after takeoff in Switzerland. The two pilots, one crew member, and 25 passengers were not injured, and no aircraft damage was reported.

synopsis: The total loss of engine power during takeoff due to fuel starvation, which resulted from the pilot's failure to adequately manage the fuel supply.
summary: The pilot experienced a total engine power loss on the crosswind leg after a takeoff, likely due to fuel exhaustion despite preflight gauges indicating 12 gallons per tank. An emergency landing in soft terrain caused nose gear collapse and firewall damage, though post-accident testing found no mechanical anomalies.

synopsis: A load shift during takeoff, which resulted in substantial damage to the aft bulkhead and associated structures.
summary: The flight crew reported that ice-covered oil drilling tools shifted aft during takeoff due to loosened nylon straps, damaging the aft pressure bulkhead and elevator control attachments. The aircraft landed safely, though postflight inspection revealed substantial structural damage to frames, stringers, and longerons.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power due to the fatigue failure of the No. 4 connecting rod. Contributing to the accident was a likely loss of lubrication for reasons that could not be determined during a postaccident engine examination.
summary: During an on-demand cargo approach, the pilot reported engine oil pressure loss, and after being cleared to an alternate runway, the aircraft impacted a berm short of the threshold. The accident caused serious pilot injury and substantial airframe damage due to a fatigue failure of the No. 4 connecting rod, though the root cause of the oil starvation remained undetermined.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing which resulted in the airplane veering off the runway and nosing over.
summary: The pilot returned to the departure airport after a one-hour flight and executed a three-point landing 300 feet past the threshold. The aircraft veered right, exited the runway, and nosed over inverted, damaging the vertical stabilizer and rudder, with no pre-impact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The Air Accident Investigation Bureau of Singapore notified the NTSB of a December 19, 2013, accident involving a Boeing 777. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design.
summary: The Air Accident Investigation Bureau of Singapore notified the NTSB of a December 19, 2013, accident involving a Boeing 777. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design.

On December 20, 2013, a pilot and three passengers were fatally injured when a Robinson R44 helicopter, F-GPJG, impacted the Dordogne River near Bordeaux, France. The accident occurred under visual meteorological conditions under unknown circumstances.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate landing flare, which resulted in a bounced landing.
summary: A student pilot with over 40 hours experienced a hard landing and multiple bounces during a local practice flight. The aircraft sustained substantial firewall damage, with the operator reporting no pre-impact mechanical malfunctions.

On December 15, 2013, the sole pilot of a Milford Helicopters Hughes 369E, ZK-HNA, collided with terrain near Lake Ross, New Zealand, under unknown circumstances. The helicopter was destroyed and the pilot was fatally injured.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed during takeoff, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and collision with terrain.
summary: During takeoff, the pilot rotated at 67 knots, but the airplane descended and the propeller struck the runway despite control inputs. The aircraft impacted a ravine after the pilot diverted to grass; post-accident examination found no mechanical failures, and a witness suspected a stall.

synopsis: The initial damage to the fan blades was caused by the ingestion of two mallard ducks that caused one or more fan blades to fracture, striking the fan shroud, as well as other passing fan blades, producing various sized blades fragments that created a cascading effect of collateral impact damage to the other fan blades, the fan case, and the inlet cowl. One large blade fragment was deflected out of the fan containment plane, which pierced and exited the inlet cowl in a benign direction. The engine and airplane met the applicable bird and containment design standards since the engine did not catch on fire, no engine cases exhibited any penetrations, the engine was able to be shutdown normally, and the airplane damage did not impact the safe operation of the airplane or create a hazard to the persons on board.
summary: Southwest Airlines Flight 1091, a Boeing 737-344, struck two mallard ducks at 1,700 feet after takeoff from St. Louis, damaging the right engine fan blades. The crew declared an emergency and landed safely with no injuries, though the engine sustained significant impact damage while meeting certification requirements.

synopsis: The non-certificated pilot's failure to maintain a stabilized approach for landing that resulted in a long landing and subsequent runway overrun.
summary: A non-certified pilot flying a pleasure flight landed long on a 2,610-foot runway and lost directional control while braking. The aircraft veered, struck a snow berm with its nose, and inverted, causing substantial damage with no mechanical failure found.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during a crosswind landing.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane drifted left and weather-vaned into a ditch during landing on a gravel airstrip due to a gust and ineffective rudder control. The aircraft sustained substantial right wing damage, with the pilot reporting no preaccident mechanical anomalies.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate clearance from trees while on approach, which subsequently led to a loss of airplane control. Also causal was the pilot's continued operation of the airplane at night with a diagnosed medical condition that degraded his night vision.
summary: A non-instrument rated pilot crashed a single-engine airplane into a tree and the ground during a night VFR approach to an unfamiliar airport. The accident likely resulted from progressive bilateral cataracts degrading the pilot's night vision, causing disorientation and failed landing attempts.

synopsis: The pilot's improper flare during a gusty, crosswind landing.
summary: During landing in gusty crosswinds, the pilot crabbed until 50 feet, then straightened the aircraft. A gust under the right wing caused the right main gear to touch down first, resulting in nose gear collapse and engine firewall damage.

A Cessna 172 with a pilot, copilot, and two passengers was destroyed shortly after its second takeoff from Teresina International Airport. The aircraft impacted the ground 130 meters left of the runway and exploded, resulting in fatal injuries to all occupants.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff with a gusting crosswind, which resulted in the collision with terrain. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's distraction when the door popped open.
summary: During takeoff in gusting crosswinds, the pilot reported the right door popped open as the wing lifted, causing an unsuccessful leveling attempt. The left wing tip struck grass, pivoting the aircraft and collapsing the right landing gear, resulting in substantial damage to the wing and fuselage.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to continue the instrument approach beyond the published missed approach point.
summary: During an ILS approach in fog, the pilot descended below minimums and drifted right of the runway, landing hard in a grassy, mud-covered area. The aircraft sustained structural fuselage damage, with the pilot reporting no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The noninstrument-rated pilot's spatial disorientation after inadvertently encountering instrument meteorological conditions at night and his subsequent loss of airplane control.
summary: A pilot with limited night and instrument experience departed without a flight plan in night VMC but likely encountered IMC in snow. The pilot probably suffered spatial disorientation, entered a descending left turn, and lost control, impacting terrain with no mechanical or medical causes found.

synopsis: The fatigue failure of the crankshaft, which resulted in a total loss of engine power and subsequent forced landing.
summary: The pilot reported an engine power loss shortly after takeoff, forcing a landing in a field where the aircraft struck a berm and inverted. Post-accident examination revealed crankshaft fatigue and camshaft overstress, possibly caused by a shifting connecting rod bearing.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to maintain airspeed during a practice autorotation, which resulted in a hard landing and subsequent loss of control
summary: During a 180-degree autorotation demonstration at 100 feet AGL, a flight instructor and student pilot experienced a sudden airspeed drop to 40 knots. The helicopter bounced on the runway, spun four to five times, and impacted the ground on its left side with substantial damage, though no mechanical failure was reported.

synopsis: The flight instructor's inadequate compensation for the gusting crosswind conditions during landing, which resulted in a loss of airplane control.
summary: A private pilot and flight instructor experienced a landing accident in high crosswinds when the aircraft became airborne after touchdown. The instructor lost control while attempting to avoid the tower, causing the airplane to roll, strike power lines and a building, and rest in a parking lot.

synopsis: The pilot's selection of unsuitable terrain during taxi, which resulted in a loss of directional control.
summary: The pilot landed a private aircraft on a snow-covered airstrip. While taxiing to parking, the right main landing gear broke through the snow crust, causing the airplane to flip inverted and substantially damage the vertical stabilizer.

synopsis: The collision with a bird which resulted in substantial damage to the airplane.
summary: The pilot experienced a bird strike on the right wing leading edge, causing vibration and requiring left control inputs to maintain level flight. During final approach, the right wing dropped and the aircraft rolled 45 to 90 degrees before the pilot recovered and landed safely at a nearby airport with substantial wing damage.

synopsis: The loss of engine power due to carburetor icing.
summary: The pilot experienced engine power loss and RPM decrease during the approach phase of a practice flight, forcing a landing in a nearby clearing. The investigation attributed the failure to likely carburetor icing caused by reduced power settings in conducive atmospheric conditions.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll, which resulted in a ground loop.
summary: During the landing roll in a constant crosswind, the pilot overcorrected a left veer with right rudder and braking, causing a 270-degree ground loop. This resulted in substantial fuselage damage near the main landing gear and firewall, with no preaccident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The student pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: A student pilot executing a landing reduced power to idle over the runway numbers, resulting in a hard touchdown and multiple bounces. The aircraft came to rest with a blown nose tire and substantial engine firewall damage, though the pilot reported no mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff.
summary: During a cross-country flight, a pilot performed a precautionary landing in a field after engine sputtering. On the subsequent takeoff from the L-shaped field, the airplane drifted right and struck a culvert, damaging the nosegear, lower fuselage, and firewall.

synopsis: A loss of engine power due to fuel starvation as a result of the noncertificated maintenance technician's failure to properly tighten and safety wire a B-nut fitting. Contributing to the accident was the maintenance technician's failure to follow the manufacturer's maintenance manual instructions.
summary: During a post-maintenance check flight on final approach, a helicopter engine flamed out due to a loose fuel line B-nut fitting, causing a hard landing and rollover. The failure resulted from improper reassembly by a noncertificated technician who disconnected the line contrary to manual instructions, omitting safety wire and proper tightening.

synopsis: The pilot's improper fuel management, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
summary: The pilot reported an en route engine power loss after rough running, leading to a forced landing where the aircraft impacted trees and inverted. Postaccident examination suggested fuel starvation likely caused by the fuel selector being set to an empty tank during flight.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain a proper glidepath during approach which resulted in the airplane landing long, and his decision to turn off of the runway during the landing roll which resulted in a collision with an earth berm.
summary: During landing on a grass runway, the pilot floated and used 200 feet of runway before braking proved ineffective. The aircraft turned off into a field, struck a hidden ridge, and nosed over, severing the nose gear with no pre-impact mechanical issues reported.

synopsis: The pilot's incapacitation due to a cardiac event during taxi.
summary: The pilot's son reported the aircraft drifted off the taxiway during a slow departure taxi and stopped near a snowbank. The pilot was found deceased at the controls; an autopsy attributed the death to severe coronary artery atherosclerosis, despite no reported medical history on his certificate.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff in variable wind conditions, resulting in a collision with trees lining the left side of the runway.
summary: A pilot flying a single-engine amphibious aircraft lost control and rolled left into trees immediately after departing a narrow island airstrip. While the pilot suspected a control surface malfunction, post-accident examination found no mechanical failures, suggesting wind shear or gusts caused the accident.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control while landing on a mobile helipad.
summary: The pilot of a Bell 206B helicopter rolled the aircraft over while landing on a mobile helipad after the left rear skid slipped off. The incident caused substantial damage, including main rotor blade separation and tail boom separation, but the pilot was not injured.

A Bell 206 helicopter (PK-DAL) crashed shortly after takeoff from a hospital near Berastagi, Indonesia, resulting in one fatality and two serious injuries. The National Transportation Safety Committee is investigating the accident, with the NTSB appointed as the U.S. Accredited Representative.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power during cruise flight for reasons that could not be determined because the airplane was not recovered.
summary: The pilot and passenger experienced a total engine power loss over water 15 miles from land, leading to an unsuccessful restart attempt and emergency descent. They ditched near a private vessel, evacuated before the aircraft sank, and were rescued, though the airplane was not recovered.

synopsis: The total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation for reasons that could not be determined during postaccident engine examination or testing.
summary: The pilot experienced engine power loss at 2,200 feet due to fuel starvation, forcing a hard landing on an expressway that caused substantial damage. Although 45 gallons of fuel remained in the tanks, the specific cause of the starvation could not be determined.

synopsis: The pilot's improper in-flight fuel mixture management and failure to use the appropriate checklist or manuals during approach to landing, which resulted in a loss of engine power.
summary: A private pilot lost engine power during the final approach of a personal cross-country flight due to failing to set the mixture control to full rich. The pilot deployed the ballistic parachute, but the aircraft struck terrain and a vehicle after the mixture remained in a cruise setting despite available display data.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane as he attempted to return to the airport after encountering dark night conditions and heavy snow showers.
summary: An instrument-rated pilot flying in dark night conditions with heavy snow and whiteout lost control while attempting to return to the departure airport. The aircraft impacted terrain in a wooded valley, sustaining substantial damage and a postimpact fire, with no preimpact mechanical anomalies found.

The Saudi Arabia Aviation Investigation Bureau notified the NTSB of a January 5, 2014, accident involving a Boeing 767-300. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the AIB.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain tail rotor clearance from a handrail on a crane davit on an oil platform during landing.
