summary: The pilot of a float-equipped airplane nosed over and sank while attempting a water landing after inadvertently contacting glassy water harder than normal. Post-accident examination found no mechanical abnormalities, though the right float showed propeller contact and the fuselage sustained substantial damage.

synopsis: The total loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined because examination of the engine did not reveal any evidence of preimpact failures or malfunctions that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: Shortly after takeoff at 100–200 ft, the pilot reported total engine power loss following a normal preflight run-up. The aircraft landed hard in the overrun area; post-accident examination found no fuel or mechanical failure, suggesting fuel exhaustion caused the incident.

synopsis: The total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion. Contributing to the fuel exhaustion was the pilot's failure during the building process to properly determine the unusable quantity of fuel.
summary: The pilot of an amateur-built aircraft executed a forced landing after engine failure caused by fuel starvation due to incorrect unusable fuel calculations during construction. The aircraft nosed over on touchdown, and post-accident inspection confirmed the tanks were empty despite gauges indicating fuel.

synopsis: The flight instructor's delayed reaction to the loss of directional control, which resulted in a ground loop.
summary: During a student's first tailwheel flight, the aircraft swerved right on landing, prompting the instructor to apply full power for a go-around. The plane subsequently ground looped, pitched forward, and landed inverted, sustaining substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer with no pre-existing anomalies reported.

synopsis: The sport pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control during taxi as a result of improperly manipulating the engine power.
summary: A sport pilot taxiing to his hangar added power instead of reducing it due to confusion with engine controls while positioning for pushback. The aircraft taxied off the movement area into a ditch, sustaining substantial damage to the firewall and forward fuselage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's improper approach, which resulted in a long landing right of the runway centerline and the airplane's subsequent collision with a riding mower that would have been difficult for the pilot to see due to its color and the nose-high attitude of the tailwheel-equipped airplane during landing.
summary: A private pilot flying a tailwheel-equipped airplane struck a dark green riding mower during landing, causing the aircraft to nose over and fatally injure the mower operator. The accident resulted from landing right of centerline beyond the recommended first third of the runway, compounded by poor visibility of the mower due to its color and the aircraft's nose-high attitude.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during landing, resulting in a ground loop.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane ground looped during the landing roll on a dry asphalt runway after overcorrecting a left veer with right rudder. The incident caused substantial damage to the left wing, with the pilot reporting no preaccident mechanical anomalies.

synopsis: A loss of engine power while the helicopter was hovering for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination of the engine and rotor drive system revealed no evidence of a mechanical malfunction or failure that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: During a hover over steep terrain, a helicopter experienced uncommanded left yaw and dropping rotor RPM, likely due to undetermined engine power loss. The pilot autorotated to a ledge, but the aircraft tipped, tumbled downslope, and suffered a severed tailboom.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to correctly use carburetor heat, resulting in a loss of engine power and collision with terrain.
summary: The pilot flying a low-power descent over a glacier without carburetor heat experienced an engine power loss near the glacier toe. He landed on the moraine, causing the airplane to nose over and sustain substantial damage due to probable carburetor icing.

synopsis: The pilots' failure to maintain clearance from terrain while operating in dark night, visual meteorological conditions. Contributing to the accident was the pilots' failure to enable the aural terrain warning system.
summary: A sport pilot and flight instructor collided with terrain during a night visual descent in a light sport airplane. The accident occurred due to dark conditions preventing visual reference and a disabled aural terrain warning function on the Electronic Flight Information System.
On August 23, 2013, an Airbus Helicopters AS332 L2, G-WNSB, ditched into the North Sea near the Shetland Islands. The helicopter was destroyed and four passengers were fatally injured.

synopsis: An inadvertent collision with wildlife while landing.
summary: The pilot experienced a runway strike involving three deer during a visual approach at night, causing the nose gear to collapse upon touchdown. While all three occupants escaped uninjured, the aircraft was substantially damaged, prompting the state to accelerate wildlife mitigation fencing.

synopsis: The pilot's distraction with traffic on the runway, and his subsequent failure to retract the air brakes prior to touchdown, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: The glider pilot sustained serious injuries during a hard landing on final approach after raising the nose to clear another glider on the runway while keeping air brakes deployed. Postaccident examination found minor tail skid damage and no mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The instructor's failure to obtain the proper touchdown point in a multiengine airplane, during a single-engine approach in a strong gusty headwind.
summary: An instructor and student in a multiengine airplane landed short of Runway 14 in a grass basin after failing to restart the right engine and encountering gusty winds. The landing gear extension caused high descent rates, leading to a right wing strike and nosegear collapse with substantial damage.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control and early rotation during takeoff. Contributing to the accident was the failure of the pilots to exercise adequate communication techniques.
summary: The pilot and a flight instructor experienced confusion during takeoff on runway 35, where the instructor could not reach the rudder pedals. The aircraft rotated early at 70 knots, porpoised, and skidded off the runway end, sustaining substantial damage to the fuselage and right wing spar.

synopsis: The fatigue failure of the No. 4 cylinder exhaust valve due to excessive wear of the corresponding train tappet, which resulted in a total loss of engine power.
summary: A private pilot experienced a total engine failure and nosed over during a forced landing after a routine flight. Post-accident examination revealed the No. 4 exhaust valve failed due to bending fatigue caused by severe wear on the exhaust train tappet.

synopsis: The flightcrew's improper recovery from a simulated engine failure after takeoff. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's failure to clarify who had control of the helicopter.
summary: During a simulated engine failure training exercise, a helicopter porpoised on an uneven runway surface, causing a main rotor blade to sever the tail boom. The flight instructor and pilot under instruction landed safely, but the aircraft turned and stopped after the structural damage occurred.

aircraft: Coulter Hugh Clarke PULSAR XP SERIES I
synopsis: Fatigue failure of the nose landing gear retention and pivot shaft, which resulted in the in-flight separation of the nose gear wheel and tire assembly.
summary: The pilot of an experimental kit-built airplane discovered a missing nose gear wheel and tire assembly after takeoff and landed with substantial firewall damage. Examination revealed the nose gear pivot shaft failed due to reverse bending fatigue, a known issue on this model, though the specific cause of the fatigue could not be determined.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the hover, and the flight instructors lack of remedial action, resulting in a dynamic rollover and structural damage to the helicopter.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor were practicing hover operations in a helicopter when the aircraft drifted right, causing the skid and main rotor blades to contact the ground. The helicopter rolled onto its right side, sustaining substantial damage to the fuselage, tail boom, and blades, with no pre-impact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control during the landing approach due to his diverted attention to the partially opened main cabin door and the unsecured dog. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to securely latch the main cabin door before takeoff and to secure his dog.
summary: A private pilot flying a newly purchased airplane with an unrestrained dog lost control during landing after the main cabin door likely opened in flight. The distraction caused the pilot to bank away from the runway and impact the ground, resulting in a post-crash fire.

synopsis: A partial loss of engine power during climbout due to a malfunctioning magneto and spark plugs.
summary: During climbout, a helicopter pilot experienced partial engine power loss and violent shaking, likely caused by a malfunctioning left magneto and No. 5 cylinder spark plugs. The pilot executed a precautionary landing where the right skid caught the ground, causing the helicopter to roll onto its side.

synopsis: The pilot's inability to maintain control of the glider after the tow cable separated prematurely due to an incomplete engagement of the cable in the control tow release system due to a missing spring.
summary: A glider pilot lost control and impacted terrain shortly after takeoff when the aircraft separated prematurely from the tow cable at 100 feet. Post-accident examination found a missing spring in the release system likely caused the cable to fail to engage, resulting in the premature release.

aircraft: Czech Sport Aircraft A S SPORTCRUISER
synopsis: The pilot's failure to apply carburetor heat during a descent with reduced engine power while operating in conditions conducive to carburetor icing, which resulted in a total loss of engine power.
summary: During a local flight descent, the pilot experienced a total engine power loss likely caused by carburetor icing due to delayed heat application and contaminated fuel. She performed an emergency field landing, sustaining substantial damage to the firewall, fuselage, and right wing.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from the runway during a low-level aerobatic maneuver due to his impairment by an over-the-counter antihistamine. Contributing to the severity of the pilot's injuries were the pilot's lack of fire protective clothing, his inability to egress the cockpit, the rapid spread of the fire, and the decision of the air show's organizers not to have the airport rescue and firefighting services at their highest level of readiness, which delayed arrival of fire suppression equipment.
summary: An experienced air show pilot flying a biplane inverted at a USAF base struck the runway while attempting a ribbon-cutting maneuver, likely due to impairment from diphenhydramine. The pilot died after a rapid fire engulfed the aircraft, exacerbated by egress difficulties, lack of protective gear, and a delayed fire response caused by insufficient ARFF readiness.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to operate the banner-tow flight below the minimum safe altitude specified by federal regulation, which likely limited his ability to recover from a potential loss of airspeed due to a gusting wind condition. Also causal was the pilot's delayed decision to release the banner, which allowed the airplane to exceed its critical angle-of-attack and resulted in an aerodynamic stall/spin from which he was unable to recover.
summary: The pilot flying a banner-tow aircraft over a congested area encountered a stall/spin after delaying banner release during a turn in gusty winds. The aircraft crashed into a house and burned, caused by intentional flight below minimum safe altitudes and delayed recovery actions.

synopsis: The flight instructor's inadequate autorotation, which resulted in a hard landing and postcrash fire. Contributing was the flight instructor's lack of experience in performing an autorotation in the accident make and model of helicopter.
summary: During an instructional cruise at 800 feet AGL, a flight instructor heard a noise and saw a caution light, prompting a precautionary autorotation in a helicopter he had not previously flown. The hard landing caused a postcrash fire that destroyed the aircraft, though no mechanical anomalies were found.

A Piper PA-31 (C-GSVM) conducting a local survey flight near Santander, Colombia, impacted terrain, substantially damaging the aircraft and fatally injuring the pilot and passenger. The investigation remains under the jurisdiction of the Colombian Government.

synopsis: A partial loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined because a full examination of the engine could not be performed.
summary: The pilot experienced a radial engine power loss while approaching a rice field for spraying, forcing a landing on a levee where the aircraft flipped after hitting a soft spot. Although the pilot suspected blower failure, the cause remained undetermined as the engine was inaccessible and the airplane was totaled.

synopsis: The failure of the pilot to maintain airspeed while maneuvering shortly after takeoff, resulting in the airplane exceeding its critical angle of attack and experiencing an aerodynamic stall, uncontrolled descent, and impact with the ground.
summary: The pilot flew a single-engine airplane that impacted a field and nosed over shortly after takeoff while climbing to 200 feet. Although the pilot reported no mechanical issues, the nose-down pitch was consistent with an aerodynamic stall, and potential alcohol impairment could not be determined as the pilot left the hospital before testing.

synopsis: Wear in the left cabin door assembly parts, which resulted in the door partially opening in flight, dislodging from the lower door track assembly, and then separating from the helicopter.
summary: During an EMS helicopter repositioning flight at cruise altitude, a partially opened cabin door dislodged and struck the main rotor, causing separation and forcing a landing. The incident resulted from worn door assembly components that failed to meet maintenance manual tolerances despite a recent inspection.

synopsis: The loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion, which resulted from the pilot's inadequate preflight planning and inflight decision making.
summary: The pilot of a single-engine aircraft with three passengers experienced engine power loss during the return leg due to fuel exhaustion despite visual estimates. This resulted in a forced landing at a construction site, causing substantial damage to the fuselage and left wing.

synopsis: The pilot's improper selection of an off-airport landing site and his subsequent failure to maintain clearance from trees during an off airport landing.
summary: A glider pilot practicing cross-country maneuvers encountered weak lift and initiated an off-field landing at 1,000 feet AGL. The glider impacted trees, sustaining substantial damage to the right wing and empennage, with no pre-impact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The probable cause of the uncontained No. 2 engine failure on the Raytheon Beechjet 400A was a herring gull birdstrike that resulted in fan blade contact with the inlet case and rub induced excitation of a previously unidentified natural frequency (resonance) within the engine operating range.
summary: A herring gull strike on the No. 2 engine during takeoff climb from Rochester International Airport caused fan blade separation and catastrophic failure. Analysis attributed the damage to overload-induced rub excitation at 72% N1 speed, with no evidence of fatigue found.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to recognize a wind shift, resulting in a tailwind landing, loss of control, and ground loop.
summary: A student pilot soloing a tailwheel airplane ground looped during a landing with a slight tailwind, sustaining substantial right wing damage. The pilot reported no preaccident mechanical anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate weather evaluation, which resulted in a turbulence encounter at low altitude and collision with trees. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's lack of knowledge of local wind conditions.
summary: A pilot departing a private grass airstrip in a tailwheel airplane encountered a rotor and downdraft above the tree line, forcing a landing in trees that damaged wing lift struts. The pilot attributed the accident to unfamiliarity with local wind shift conditions rather than mechanical failure.

synopsis: A complete loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined because of insufficient evidence.
summary: A private pilot flying an experimental aircraft experienced total engine power loss during the second leg of a cross-country trip, forcing a landing that resulted in the airplane nosing over and resting inverted. The probable cause was undetermined due to damage, but fuel exhaustion was suspected because the pilot used incorrect fuel burn rates for a modified engine and relied on an unverified fuel quantity system.

On May 6, 2014, an Airbus A330-223 rejected takeoff at Melbourne Aerodrome due to a failure of the No. 2 Pratt & Whitney PW4168 engine. No injuries were reported, and the Australian Transport Safety Board is investigating with NTSB participation.

synopsis: The pilot's improper preflight and in-flight fuel planning, which resulted in fuel exhaustion and a subsequent total loss of engine power over unsuitable terrain.
summary: The pilot of a general aviation aircraft impacted terrain three miles from the destination after declaring "out of fuel" during cruise. The accident resulted from fuel exhaustion caused by unaccounted headwinds and higher-than-estimated fuel consumption, with no mechanical anomalies found.

synopsis: the flight attendant's inadvertent trip and fall over a passenger bag that was in the aisle.
summary: A flight attendant on Delta Air Lines flight 1248, a Boeing 737-900ER, tripped over a passenger's bag in the aisle while carrying a drink tray during boarding at San Diego International Airport. The obscured view caused the fall, resulting in a broken arm requiring hospital transport.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: The pilot executed a go-around on the first landing attempt. On the second attempt, the airplane ballooned during flare, impacting the runway with the propeller and nose gear, causing the gear to collapse and separate and sustaining substantial engine mount damage.

synopsis: The flight instructor's failure to arrest the airplane's descent and maintain clearance from mountainous terrain while maneuvering at a low altitude.
summary: A witness observed a flight instructor's aircraft sputtering and entering a nose-down attitude at 800 to 1,000 feet before impacting terrain. The investigation concluded the instructor failed to recover from the steep descent at a sufficient altitude to avoid the crash.

On April 30, 2014, the pilot of a Robinson R44 II (RA-06217) was fatally injured when the aircraft impacted terrain near Inta, Russia. The Russian Federation Interstate Aviation Committee is investigating the incident.

synopsis: The pilot's improper flare, which resulted in abnormal contact with the water and separation of the right pontoon..
summary: The pilot of an amphibian airplane experienced a right wing pontoon separation immediately after lake touchdown, causing the aircraft to spin and sink. Witnesses attributed the accident to the pontoon contacting water first, likely due to the pilot's limited water landing experience affecting depth perception.

synopsis: The pilot's inability to control the airplane while taxiing due to a strong crosswind condition.
summary: The pilot of a single-engine airplane flipped inverted while taxiing on a parallel taxiway after landing for fuel due to stronger-than-forecast headwinds. Despite using proper crosswind technique, gusts similar to the reported 25 knots lifted the upwind wing, causing substantial damage to the rudder and left front wing strut.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during takeoff. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to abort the takeoff at the initial veer off.
summary: The pilot of a high-wing tailwheel airplane lost directional control during takeoff from a sloped grass strip after failing to straighten the tailwheel before applying power. The aircraft veered left, struck a hummock while avoiding a golf cart, and sustained substantial damage to the fuselage and left wing.

synopsis: The failure of the power turbine thrust (No. 5) bearing due to overheating as a result of oil starvation, which led to the engine failure. Also causal to the accident was an undocumented repair to the gearbox cover oil delivery tube port during which an insert was threaded into the oil delivery tube port that subsequently restricted the oil flow to the power turbine thrust bearing.
summary: During a search and rescue mission, a helicopter pilot experienced engine failure at 200 feet due to a modified gearbox cover blocking oil flow to a bearing. The pilot attempted an autorotation, but the aircraft rolled onto its left side after the skid caught on an object under the snow.

synopsis: Fuel starvation due to the deterioration of the fuel selector valve, which allowed fuel to be fed from only the right tip tank. Contributing to the accident was the inadequate annual inspection, which failed to detect the deteriorated valve.
summary: The pilot and passenger experienced a partial engine power loss during night touch-and-go landings due to a worn fuel selector valve stuck in the OFF position. This defect allowed fuel flow only from the exhausted right tip tank, forcing an emergency field landing despite a recent annual inspection.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate approach and his failure to maintain clearance from power lines, which resulted in a subsequent fire.
summary: A balloon pilot struck power lines while attempting to land, causing a fire and an accelerated climb that led to a crash six miles away. The report suggests the pilot identified the obstacle too late to clear it safely, with no preexisting mechanical anomalies found.

synopsis: The pilot's mismanagement of the onboard fuel supply, which resulted in fuel starvation to the engine and a subsequent loss of engine power. Contributing to the death of the right front passenger was the inadequate occupant restraint.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a single-engine aircraft lost engine power during a climb to an alternate airport after inadvertently selecting a nearly depleted left tip tank, causing fuel starvation. The subsequent crash resulted in the fatal injury of a front-seat passenger, an outcome likely mitigated had shoulder harnesses been installed.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from the water while operating at a low altitude.
summary: The pilot of a float-equipped airplane scouting for fish encountered a huge gust of wind at 30 feet, causing the aircraft to bounce and ground loop after the right pontoon contacted the water. The incident resulted in substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer, with no mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during the landing, and the flight instructor's inadequate supervision of the student pilot resulting in abnormal runway contact and damage to the airplane.
summary: During a short field landing practice, a student pilot misinterpreted the flight instructor's "full power" command as "pull power," reducing engine power and causing a runway impact. The resulting bounce damaged the nose gear and firewall, prompting the operator to reemphasize standard phraseology like "go around."

synopsis: The pilot's inability to maintain aircraft control due to a partial loss of engine power and an encounter with downdrafts and gusting crosswinds while on final approach to the runway. The reason for the partial loss of engine power could not be determined because postaccident examination revealed no mechanical malfunction or failure that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: During a local sightseeing flight, the pilot experienced an unexplained partial engine power loss and encountered strong downdrafts on final approach. The aircraft landed hard short of the runway and nosed over inverted, though post-accident testing found no mechanical failures.

aircraft: Sam R Peachey JUST AIRCRAFT HIGHLA
synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed during low altitude maneuvering.
summary: The pilot crashed the airplane while flying 500 feet above ground during a church candy drop. A rotor wind from a nearby mountain caused a wing stall during a turn, resulting in loss of control and substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot's improper flap retraction during a short field takeoff, which resulted in the aircraft experiencing an aerodynamic stall and impact with trees.
summary: The pilot attempted a short-field takeoff from a 2,350-foot runway with 10 degrees of flaps but raised them immediately after liftoff, causing the nose to pitch down. The aircraft struck trees and the ground, sustaining substantial damage, while post-accident inspection found no mechanical anomalies.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing and separation of the left main landing gear.
summary: A commercial pilot experienced left main landing gear separation during a landing attempt after a skydiving operation, likely caused by an improper flare resulting in a hard landing. The pilot executed a go-around and emergency landing, sustaining substantial damage to the left wing spar.

synopsis: The total loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination and testing of the engine revealed no anomalies.
summary: The pilot experienced a total loss of engine power on the base leg during a practice landing, forcing a crash landing that caused substantial damage and serious injury. Post-accident examinations found no mechanical failures, and the engine later demonstrated rated horsepower during manufacturer testing.

synopsis: The non-instrument rated pilots' decision to continue flight into known instrument meteorological conditions over mountainous terrain, which resulted in controlled flight into terrain.
summary: Two non-instrument rated pilots flew a multi-leg trip in visual conditions but entered instrument meteorological conditions over mountainous terrain without a weather briefing. The aircraft struck a mountain at an altitude 2,500 feet below the maximum elevation figure, likely due to an intentional decision to fly through clouds without adequate clearance.

synopsis: A loss of propeller thrust due to a failure of the reduction drive unit resulting from the improper installation of the unit. Contributing to the accident was a lack of documentation for the reduction drive unit installation.
summary: The pilot experienced a complete loss of thrust and increased engine speed while in the traffic pattern, forcing a landing in an open field. The cause was a propeller reduction drive pulley moving downward due to missing secondary fittings, as the manufacturer provided no installation documentation.

synopsis: The pilot's selection of an inadequate altitude during low level maneuvering, which resulted in an in-flight collision with trees.
summary: During a local photo flight, the pilot entered a left turn and the aircraft impacted tree tops. The pilot reported no mechanical issues, and an FAA inspection confirmed no pre-impact failures, with evidence showing the plane struck trees in a level attitude.

aircraft: Morris Thomas Lee STOLP STRDSTR SA300
synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control while landing in gusty crosswinds in a tail wheel equipped airplane.
summary: The pilot of a tail-wheel airplane experienced a tailwheel shimmy and yaw during landing on runway 35 in gusty winds. The right landing gear buckled and the wing contacted the ground, causing substantial damage and a runway departure, with no preimpact anomalies found.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control during landing.
summary: A pilot approaching a 2,400-foot farm strip from the west encountered wind shear that pushed the aircraft off the runway edge, causing a wingtip collision with brush and a broken nose wheel. The pilot attributed the incident to sudden wind changes despite reported winds of 10 knots from 230 degrees at a nearby airport.

synopsis: The pilot's repeated attempts to take off from an unimproved field with tall grass.
summary: The pilot attempted takeoff from an unimproved field with 3-foot tall grass. After the aircraft lifted off but failed to climb, the pilot rejected the takeoff, resulting in a nose-over upon touchdown.

synopsis: The flight crew's decision to attempt an engine start in conditions that exceeded the engine's maximum allowable ground start crosswind component limitation.
summary: The flight crew of a multi-engine turbofan experienced an uncontained left engine fire during start in 24-knot crosswinds, exceeding the 19-knot limit. The crew shut down both engines and evacuated, causing substantial damage likely due to airflow disruption from the excessive wind.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to attain a proper touchdown point during landing and his failure to go around when he recognized that he would not be able to stop the airplane on the runway, which resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot of a turbine-powered multiengine airplane executed a long visual approach, touching down one-third down a 4,000-ft runway and rolling off the end into a pond. The pilot attributed the incident to a short final approach, unfamiliarity with the airport, and failing to reject the landing, noting no mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate obstacle clearance, which resulted in the inflight collision with a power line.
summary: The pilot attempted a precautionary landing on a wet private grass strip due to deteriorating weather and low fuel. After experiencing poor braking, he initiated a go-around, struck a power line and trees, and collided with the ground, sustaining substantial damage to the aircraft.

A Bell 407GX helicopter operated by Eastern General Aviation Limited Corporation impacted water near Beijing under unknown circumstances. One pilot was fatally injured and the second pilot sustained minor injuries while the accident is being investigated by the CAAC.

synopsis: A partial loss of engine power due to encounter with weather conditions conducive to carburetor icing. Contributing the accident was the pilot's inadequate weather planning.
summary: The pilot of an amphibious airplane experienced total engine power loss during the base leg descent, likely due to carburetor icing. The aircraft struck a vehicle and sustained substantial damage during a forced landing, with post-accident examination revealing no pre-impact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The improper installation of the hose fuel fitting, which resulted in the fitting becoming disconnected and the subsequent loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
summary: A pilot flying a single-engine airplane experienced fuel starvation and engine power loss shortly after takeoff due to a disconnected inlet hose on the mechanical fuel pump. The pilot executed a wheels-up forced landing after the hose fitting, likely improperly installed, vibrated loose during flight.

synopsis: The probable cause of the uncontained No. 2 engine failure on the Raytheon Beechjet 400A was a yellow-crowned night-heron birdstrike that resulted in fan blade contact with the inlet case and rub induced excitation of a previously unidentified natural frequency (resonance) within the engine operating range.
summary: A yellow-crowned night-heron birdstrike on the No. 2 engine during takeoff from Sugar Land Regional Airport caused fan blade separation, an engine fire, and fuel tank puncture. Analysis attributed the failure to overload-induced rub excitation at 72% N1 speed, with no evidence of fatigue.

On April 12, 2014, a pilot operating a Maule M-5-235C (VH-HOG) near Lismore Aerodrome struck a power line and impacted terrain. The aircraft was substantially damaged, resulting in minor injuries to the pilot and a fatality to the passenger.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate flare resulting in a hard landing.
summary: The pilot reported a hard landing that caused the right main landing gear to collapse and substantial fuselage deformation. The pilot stated there were no mechanical malfunctions during the flight.

A private pilot flying a Cessna T210N collided with trees during a go-around at night at an unprepared airstrip in Para, Brazil. Witnesses observed a steep left bank followed by an aerodynamic stall, resulting in a fatal crash and postcrash fire for the pilot and one passenger.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff.
summary: A student pilot with 11 hours of experience departed the left side of the runway during a takeoff attempt after the airplane yawed left despite right rudder input. The aircraft struck parked construction equipment, causing damage to the nosegear, left wing, and firewall, with no mechanical malfunctions found.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
summary: During the landing roll, the pilot reported the airplane drifted left, and his over-correction with right rudder caused it to veer off the runway and ground loop. The left wing contacted the surface and was substantially damaged, with no preimpact mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: the captain's failure to verify the communications between himself and the tug operator, which resulted in him applying of brakes while the airplane was being pushed back from the gate by the tug with tow bar attached.
summary: Delta flight crew and a tug operator were involved when a Boeing MD-90's nose gear partially collapsed during pushback at Boston Logan. The captain applied brakes believing he heard a command due to poor interphone quality, stopping the aircraft while the tug was still pushing.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate flare, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: The pilot reported that during final approach, the airplane unexpectedly dropped after flaring higher than normal, causing a hard runway impact. The aircraft skidded off into a grassy area, sustaining substantial damage to the lower fuselage and rudder, with no preimpact malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed and his exceedance of the airplane's critical angle-of-attack while maneuvering at low altitude, which led to an aerodynamic stall and loss of control. Contributing to the accident was the installation of an inappropriate airspeed indicator that did not provide airspeed indications near the airplane's stall speed.
summary: A private pilot flying an amateur-built light sport airplane stalled and impacted the ground during low-altitude maneuvering. The accident likely resulted from the pilot's failure to maintain airspeed due to an inappropriate airspeed indicator that did not display the aircraft's actual stall speed.

synopsis: The air traffic controller's failure to provide required advisories about significant radar-observed convective precipitation along both airplanes' flight routes and the air route traffic control center's lack of a program to ensure that air traffic controllers provide this required information to pilots, which led to both airplanes encountering severe turbulence. Contributing to the airplanes' encounters with severe turbulence was the flight crews' failure to detect the precipitation using on-board radar and request deviations, as necessary, to avoid the hazard.
summary: Pilots of a Boeing 757 and a regional jet encountered severe turbulence and hail en route, causing passenger injuries and radome damage on the 757. The controller failed to advise crews of radar-observed precipitation despite FAA requirements, though the regional jet crew avoided damage after requesting a deviation.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed and his exceedance of the airplane's critical angle-of-attack after a total loss of engine power during the takeoff initial climb, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and impact with terrain. The reason for the total loss of engine power could not be determined because an examination of the airframe and engines did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: A commercial pilot and a new ATP conducted a check flight when the aircraft likely suffered total engine power loss shortly after takeoff. The ATP attempted a return to the airport but stalled due to insufficient airspeed, causing the airplane to impact the ground.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to exit the helicopter while it was running and his failure to properly secure the flight controls with the engine operating at flight idle before exiting the helicopter.
summary: A commercial pilot left a running helicopter at flight idle to relieve himself, violating company policy requiring a pilot at the controls. Unsecured flight controls in crosswinds caused the aircraft to pitch, roll, and yaw until the rotor blades impacted the ground.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control after the helicopter's skid catching on the side of a trailer during takeoff, which resulted in a dynamic rollover.
summary: During a helicopter move from a trailer to the ground, a landing gear skid bolt caught on the trailer skirting, causing a dynamic rollover onto the right side. The pilot reported no pre-impact mechanical failures, but a fire subsequently erupted and consumed the cabin.

synopsis: The pilot's improper preflight planning and in-flight fuel management, which resulted in fuel starvation and a total loss of engine power. Also causal to the accident was the pilot's failure to see and avoid the wires on the airport boundary.
summary: The pilot departed a 40-mile flight with insufficient fuel, causing engine power loss during landing approach. The aircraft struck wires and terrain short of the runway due to fuel exhaustion, confirmed by post-accident testing showing the engine ran normally after refueling.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during an attempted go around in gusty wind conditions which resulted in a collision with terrain.
summary: The pilot diverted due to strong winds and lost directional control on landing after a perpendicular gust lifted the left wing. During the subsequent go-around attempt, the right gear collapsed, causing the right wingtip and propeller to impact the ground and damage the forward fuselage.

synopsis: The loss of engine power as a result of carburetor icing.
summary: The pilot ferrying a newly purchased airplane experienced engine power loss and vibration shortly after departure on the second leg, leading to a collision with trees. The investigation concluded the likely cause was carburetor icing, as post-accident testing found no mechanical anomalies despite operating in an icing risk area.

synopsis: The Aviation Safety Council of Taiwan is investigating an incident involving a Boeing 737-800 that occurred on 11 May 2014. The NTSB has appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation as the State of Manufacturer.
summary: The Aviation Safety Council of Taiwan is investigating an incident involving a Boeing 737-800 that occurred on 11 May 2014. The NTSB has appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation as the State of Manufacturer.

A foreign certificated pilot flying a Cessna T188C on a local aerial application flight lost engine power and impacted terrain near Canton Naranjal, Ecuador. The aircraft was substantially damaged by a post-accident fire, and the pilot sustained minor injuries.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control after the airplane encountered a wind gust during takeoff roll. Contributing to the accident was the pilot inadvertently using a runway that resulted in a gusty tailwind condition.
summary: The pilot attempted a takeoff on runway 16 in gusty winds, resulting in a tailwind condition. A wind gust raised the right wing, causing the aircraft to depart the runway and impact a drainage ditch due to the pilot's inability to maintain directional control at high ground speed.

synopsis: A fire in the airplane's engine compartment that initiated for reasons that could not be determined due to extensive fire damage.
summary: The pilot smelled smoke while taxiing for departure, shut down the engine, and evacuated passengers. Smoke from the engine cowling caused a fire that destroyed most of the fuselage, and the fire's source could not be determined due to extensive damage.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control while landing at night, which resulted in a runway excursion and collision with airport signage. Contributing to the accident was the total loss of electrical power, which necessitated the pilot having to land without the aid of the airplane's landing lights and some of the available runway lighting.
summary: The pilot experienced a total electrical failure due to an alternator malfunction shortly after night departure. Unable to use landing lights or radio, the pilot misjudged the flare height, resulting in a runway excursion and substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during landing and subsequent go around attempt.
summary: The pilot, flying a single-engine aircraft on a straight-in approach with restricted visibility, landed fast and overcorrected for a crosswind. This caused the airplane to skid off the runway, collapsing the right main gear and striking the ground with the right wing and propeller.

Two pilots in a Cessna 140A operated by Aero Agrícola Santos Dumont Ltda lost control during an instructional flight departing Cachoeira do Su Airport. The aircraft impacted terrain near the airport, resulting in the fatal injuries of both pilots.

synopsis: Maintenance personnel's inadequate inspection of the engine's outer combustion case, which resulted in the failure of the case due to fatigue cracks that initiated on the inside surface of the case and the subsequent total loss of engine power.
summary: The helicopter pilot experienced an abrupt engine power loss shortly after takeoff, forcing a grass landing where rotor blades severed the tail boom. The accident was caused by fatigue cracks in the engine's combustion case weld, likely missed during a recent 150-hour inspection.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight inspection, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot departed a cargo flight believing tanks held 1,000 lbs per side, but engines shut down in cruise due to fuel exhaustion caused by a missed refueling and inadequate preflight inspection. The aircraft diverted, and aggressive braking during landing caused tire deflation and a runway excursion.

synopsis: The pilot's use of excessive brakes during landing, which resulted in a nose over. Contributing to the accident was a partial loss of engine power during takeoff initial climb, likely due to carburetor ice.
summary: The pilot of a personal flight experienced partial engine power loss at 150 feet after recent cylinder replacement and a ground run without carburetor heat. The aircraft nosed over during a hard-braked landing, sustaining substantial damage, likely due to carburetor icing despite no water found in the fuel.

A Cessna T206H with one pilot and four passengers was substantially damaged and caused serious injuries when it struck power lines while returning to land at Edmundo Carvajal Airport. The incident occurred with smoke in the cockpit during the approach phase.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll, which resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot landed normally but lost directional control during rollout due to a gust of wind, causing the aircraft to veer off the right runway side. The airplane came to rest inverted, sustaining substantial damage to the left wing and vertical stabilizer, with no mechanical anomalies reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot reported that after touchdown on short final, a wind shift caused the aircraft to depart the right runway side, strike a ditch, and collapse its landing gear. The airplane came to rest on its belly with substantial fuselage damage, and the pilot reported no preimpact mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control and sufficient altitude to clear terrain during a low-altitude maneuver.
summary: The pilot lost control and altitude while turning left after aerial application, resulting in a terrain impact with the left wing striking first. No mechanical anomalies were found, and the accident was likely caused by the pilot's failure to maintain control and sufficient altitude.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to attain the proper touchdown point during a no-flap landing to a wet, down-sloping runway, and the airplane's dynamic hydroplaning after touchdown, which resulted in a runway overrun. Contributing to the accident was a total loss of electrical power due to an alternator failure.
summary: An airline transport pilot flying in IMC experienced total electrical failure due to a worn alternator brush, leading to a no-flap landing on a wet, down-sloping runway. Ineffective braking, likely caused by dynamic hydroplaning and a long touchdown, prevented the aircraft from stopping, resulting in an excursion where it struck a fence.

synopsis: The improperly attached fuel line and cracked fuel diaphragm due to unknown personnel's inadequate maintenance, which resulted in the loss of engine power during cruise flight and the subsequent forced landing onto rough terrain.
summary: A flight instructor and pilot-rated owner experienced engine power loss in cruise due to a loose fuel return line and a leaking manifold valve diaphragm. They executed a forced landing on rough terrain, resulting in nose gear collapse and substantial right wing damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing which resulted in a ground-loop and nose over.
summary: A solo pilot ground-looped a tailwheel-equipped airplane during the fourth stop-and-go landing while becoming current. Excessive brake application caused the aircraft to nose over, sustaining substantial damage to the vertical stabilizer and rudder with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The failure of the pilot to identify poor engine performance during the engine run-up before takeoff. Also causal to the accident was the mistimed right magneto and the poor condition of the spark plugs in the No. 4 cylinder.
summary: The pilot took off a single-engine airplane with an excessive right magneto drop, later discovering the engine produced only 1,900 rpm instead of 2,400 rpm. This power loss, caused by a mistimed right magneto and spark plug discrepancies, forced a landing where the right wing struck a tree.
A British Aerospace AVRO 146-RJ100 experienced a No. 2 engine fire during climb from Perth, Australia. The aircraft returned to Perth for an uneventful landing with no injuries reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain proper airspeed while on approach, and his subsequent failure to recover from a bounced landing, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: A private pilot landing a private airplane on a 3,499-foot asphalt runway experienced a hard landing after three bounces caused by excessive approach speed. This resulted in substantial damage to the nose landing gear and firewall, with the pilot noting no pre-accident malfunctions and admitting he should have aborted after the first bounce.

synopsis: The assembler's improper fabrication of a fuel line (hose) and the subsequent failure to verify that it was not occluded, which resulted in fuel starvation and a total loss of engine power during takeoff.
summary: A commercial pilot lost engine power during takeoff in an agricultural aircraft, colliding with a berm due to fuel starvation. The cause was a blocked fuel hose installed incorrectly during a turbine conversion, where assembly friction detached the inner liner, obstructing fuel flow.

aircraft: John V Rawson Jr SPRINT II
synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control during the approach to land. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's unfamiliarity with and lack of training in the accident airplane make and model.
summary: An unlicensed owner/builder took an unqualified pilot for a solo flight in an experimental amphibious airplane outside its geographic limits. The pilot lost control during two final approaches due to uncommanded left turns, impacting terrain, with no mechanical failure found and insufficient specific training cited as a factor.

synopsis: The airplane's encounter with a strong tailwind and/or windshear, which resulted in an inadvertent stall. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's continuation of the unstable approach, long landing, and delayed decision to conduct a go-around.
summary: The pilot of a returning aircraft encountered strong crosswinds and gusts, leading to an unstable approach, a bounced landing, and a rejected landing. The airplane subsequently stalled during climbout, likely due to tailwind or windshear, and collided with a transmission wire and terrain.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll, which resulted in a ground loop.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane ground looped right shortly after a three-point landing, causing landing gear collapse and left wing impact. Postaccident examination found the tailwheel heavily worn but functional, with no mechanical failure identified as the cause.

synopsis: An extreme vibration immediately after entering forward flight for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination of the helicopter did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's inability to maintain helicopter control during the landing.
summary: A commercial pilot lost control of a helicopter during an agricultural cherry drying takeoff after experiencing violent vibration while transitioning to forward flight. The pilot aborted the takeoff but impacted the ground, though post-accident examination revealed no mechanical anomalies.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from power lines while flying at a low altitude.
summary: A helicopter pilot flying low along a river struck three unmarked overhead power lines while descending. The investigation found no mechanical failures, concluding the pilot likely did not see the lines due to the low altitude.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control while departing from a wet runway.
summary: The pilot reported that during takeoff on a wet dirt airstrip, the aircraft briefly lifted off but settled back down before becoming airborne again near the runway end. The pilot lost control while turning toward lower terrain, resulting in a collision with a fence and a nose-over that substantially damaged the wings, vertical stabilizer, and rudder.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain pitch control during takeoff after encountering a boat wake, which resulted in the airplane bouncing, impacting the water's surface, and subsequently becoming submerged.
summary: A private pilot attempting to take off an experimental amphibious airplane from a choppy lake encountered a boat wake, causing the aircraft to bounce and nose down into the water. The pilot was recovered by swimmers, but the airplane sank and the wreckage was not recovered.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to reconnect the air-oil separator return line after completing an oil change, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to oil starvation.
summary: A commercial pilot performing an oil change 4.3 hours prior to flight failed to reconnect the air-oil separator return line, causing oil starvation and engine failure during cruise. The pilot declared an emergency and attempted a forced landing, but the aircraft struck berms and came to rest inverted.

synopsis: The total loss of engine power due to carburetor icing, which resulted from the pilot's failure to use carburetor heat in cruise flight while operating in an area conducive to carburetor icing.
summary: A commercial pilot experienced partial then total engine power loss at 12,500 ft MSL due to carburetor icing with the heat control off. The pilot performed a forced landing on a dirt road, resulting in firewall damage and collapsed right main landing gear.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to recover from an intentional spin. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's lack of adequate spin entry and recovery training.
summary: The pilot of an experimental amateur-built airplane entered a left spin while attempting self-taught aerobatics and impacted a wheat field after seven revolutions. The flight instructor attributed the accident to the pilot's inadequate spin knowledge and refusal to receive further training in the instructor's aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to depart from a soft runway with a tailwind and toward obstructions, and his failure to follow the manufacturer's recommended procedures for the takeoff. Contributing to the accident were the degradation of airplane and engine performance due to the high density altitude and the pilot's failure to properly configure the airplane's carburetor heat.
summary: The pilot departed a turf runway with three passengers toward trees, using no flaps, a tailwind, and intermediate carburetor heat, which reduced engine power and climb performance. The aircraft stalled after clearing the trees, rolled right, and crashed into the forest, resulting in a post-impact fire.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain helicopter control during landing resulting in a hard landing and a roll over.
summary: During a hover practice flight, the pilot reported the helicopter rotated uncontrollably and impacted the ground after the passenger interfered with the flight controls. Post-accident examination found no mechanical failures, attributing the crash to the passenger's actions.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate inflight fuel monitoring, which resulted in fuel exhaustion and the subsequent total loss of engine power. Contributing to the accident was the loose fuel cap, which allowed fuel to syphon out in flight.
summary: The pilot departed a cross-country flight with a loose fuel cap, causing fuel to siphon from the right tank and resulting in engine power loss due to fuel exhaustion. The accident was delayed in discovery because the emergency locator transmitter was switched off, preventing signal detection for three days.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control of the airplane during landing roll on a rough, grass airstrip in gusting wind.
summary: The pilot executed a go-around due to turbulence and gusts before landing on runway 13, where frost heaves caused the aircraft to bounce and the right wing to lift. Despite control inputs, the airplane veered left of the centerline and collided with two parked aircraft, with no mechanical malfunction reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll, which resulted in a runway excursion and subsequent collision with a fence.
summary: During a simulated engine failure training maneuver at 400 feet, the pilot and passenger executed a downwind landing that resulted in the aircraft swerving off the runway. Despite recovering onto the runway, the pilot could not clear the perimeter fence during a subsequent takeoff attempt, causing substantial damage to the fuselage and wings with no reported mechanical failure.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control during engine startup, which resulted in a collision with a parked airplane. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to follow engine startup procedures and a sudden surge of engine power for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination did not reveal any mechanical malfunctions.
summary: The pilot of a weight-shift aircraft collided with a parked airplane and a hangar door during startup after the engine advanced to takeoff power on the eighth attempt. The investigation found no mechanical anomalies, though the pilot failed to follow POH procedures regarding startup orientation and excessive start attempts.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during the takeoff roll.
summary: A student pilot lost directional control during a solo simulated soft-field takeoff due to improper rudder use. The aircraft departed the runway, crossed a taxiway, and struck an embankment, causing substantial damage with no mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control while entering a vortex ring state (settling with power) condition, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: The helicopter pilot entered a vortex ring state during a westerly landing approach, causing an unexpected rapid descent despite increasing collective. The aircraft landed hard and bounced, sustaining substantial damage to the right fuselage and vertical stabilizer with no pre-accident mechanical failures.

aircraft: Smythe Donald F KITFOX CLASSIC IV
synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight planning, which resulted in his attempt to takeoff in conditions under which the airplane was unable to attain a positive rate of climb and resulted in its failure to clear trees.
summary: The pilot attempted a takeoff from a grassy field in a 65-horsepower aircraft but failed to clear 60-foot trees due to degraded climb performance. The accident, caused by tall grass, a tailwind, high density altitude, and limited power, resulted in a ground contact and cartwheel.

synopsis: A loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident testing revealed no anomalies.
summary: The pilot reported an abrupt engine power loss 20 minutes into flight, leading to a forced landing on uneven terrain after failing to reach the airport. The right main gear did not fully extend, causing a ground loop that buckled the fuselage and tore off the right wing, though post-accident engine tests showed no anomalies.

On May 26, 2014, the pilot of an Air Tractor AT-802 (EC-LCA) sustained fatal injuries when the aircraft impacted terrain during a firefighting operation near Seron, Spain. A post-impact fire subsequently destroyed the airplane.

synopsis: The pilot's delayed use of carburetor heat during the approach to landing, which resulted in the formation of carburetor ice, a partial loss of engine power, and the airplane's subsequent inability to sustain flight.
summary: The pilot experienced a considerable loss of engine power during a scenic flight approach, attributing it to carburetor ice. Despite applying carburetor heat, the aircraft impacted trees and a power pole before colliding with a barn, an outcome the pilot attributed to delaying heat application.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control, which resulted in a stall and subsequent collision with power lines.
summary: The pilot crashed an agricultural airplane into power lines while performing a steep downwind turn during spraying operations. Although the aircraft had sustained prior bird strike damage to the right wing that the pilot continued to fly, the investigation could not determine if this damage caused the stall.

synopsis: The pilot's improper flare during landing.
summary: The pilot flared too soon during landing, causing the aircraft to bounce and touch down nose-wheel first, which collapsed the nose gear strut and substantially damaged the firewall. No pre-impact mechanical malfunctions were reported.

synopsis: The pilot's improper application of brakes during taxi in tailwind conditions, which resulted in a loss of aircraft control and subsequent nose over.
summary: The pilot and passenger nosed over a tailwheel-equipped airplane during taxi when a crosswind shifted to a tailwind and both applied brakes simultaneously. This caused substantial tail damage with no reported preimpact mechanical failure.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airspeed while maneuvering at low altitude, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and impact with water.
summary: The pilot of a weight-shift control aircraft stalled while descending near a bird's nest to allow a passenger to take photos. Despite applying full power, the aircraft impacted the river with substantial damage, though both occupants swam to shore safely with no mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control during the takeoff roll, which resulted in inadvertent terrain contact by the wing.
summary: A glider pilot reported a right wing drop during tow for takeoff, causing the left wing to strike grass and turn the aircraft 180 degrees. The safety link released, the glider rolled backward, and the left aileron separated from its mounts, with no pre-impact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to select and attain a proper touchdown point during landing which resulted in a runway overrun.
summary: A pilot practicing takeoffs and landings encountered turbulence and overran the runway on the third landing attempt. The aircraft nosed over and inverted after striking logs, sustaining substantial damage, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The failure of the drive mechanism for the gearbox motor, which resulted in the gear not extending for the landing.
summary: The pilot reported a loud bang and failed nose gear extension during landing gear deployment, leading to a collapsed gear and runway skid with substantial fuselage damage. Examination revealed the cause was a failed drive mechanism for the gearbox motor, with no other mechanical malfunctions found.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll, which resulted in the airplane nosing over.
summary: During a full stop landing on a grass strip at 20 mph, the pilot reported the airplane veered left, prompting right rudder and brake application. The aircraft abruptly nosed over and came to rest inverted with substantial aft fuselage damage, with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during the landing.
summary: The pilot encountered a strong right gust during final approach to an island airport, causing an awkward touchdown and subsequent hard landing. The aircraft veered off the runway, struck a tree, and suffered right wing separation before coming to rest.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control on takeoff.
summary: A private pilot flying a tailwheel aircraft veered left and flipped during takeoff roll after lifting the tail at 50 feet, causing substantial damage to the wings, vertical stabilizer, and engine mount. The pilot reported 5-knot tailwinds and no mechanical deficiencies.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to adequately monitor the airplane's actual fuel consumption rate, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot experienced total engine power loss due to fuel exhaustion during the return leg of a glider aero-tow flight. The aircraft subsequently crashed into a fence and ditch after a forced landing, caused by an unexplained high fuel consumption rate that depleted the tank before flight completion.

synopsis: The pilot's downwind takeoff from a grass airstrip, which resulted in inadequate climb performance and the subsequent impact with terrain.
summary: The pilot of a loaded agriculture airplane departed a 2,600-foot grass airstrip downwind, striking a levee with the landing gear. The aircraft failed to climb due to degraded takeoff performance from the downwind departure and gusty winds, resulting in a forced landing with substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain lateral control during the initial climb. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to obtain sufficient training and experience to operate the high-performance airplane.
summary: During the initial climb of a high-performance airplane, the pilot lost control when the left wing dropped and the aircraft turned left, leading to a ground impact and postcrash fire that destroyed the airplane. The pilot attributed the accident to insufficient time, training, and experience for this aircraft type.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during landing which resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: An instructor and student practicing tailwheel landings in a training aircraft overturned after the student applied brakes while lowering the tail, causing a skid off the runway. The instructor attributed the accident to teaching braking techniques for lifting the tail during landings rather than high-speed taxiing.

synopsis: An in-flight collision with a bird during the descent to land, which resulted in substantial damage to the airplane.
summary: The pilot reported a bird strike with a common loon during descent to land, approximately 10 miles from the airport between 3,500 and 3,000 feet MSL. The impact caused substantial damage to the airframe.

synopsis: The loss of engine power due to oil starvation for reasons that could not be determined based on the available evidence.
summary: During cruise, the pilot reported rough engine operation, zero oil pressure, and cockpit smoke, leading to a forced landing in a field. Post-accident examination found crankcase damage consistent with oil starvation, but the specific cause remained undetermined after the engine was disposed of.

aircraft: Divis S L/Waltrip A J RV 4
synopsis: The pilot's inadequate preflight and in-flight planning which resulted in total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine failure due to fuel exhaustion caused by increased consumption from a new propeller, altitude planning errors, and weather deviations. He executed an emergency landing at Farr Field, sustaining fuselage damage but avoiding a runway overrun into water.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: During landing, the pilot lost runway sight while flaring and, after a passenger instructed "stick forward," unknowingly moved the control stick too far forward. The aircraft nosed down on impact, sustaining damage to the propeller, cowl, landing gear, and firewall.

A Cessna 210N with a pilot and three passengers was substantially damaged during landing at Sinop Airport due to a nosegear actuator failure. The failure caused the propeller and lower fuselage to contact the runway, though no injuries occurred.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control of the helicopter due to impairment or incapacitation from a sudden, acute cardiac event.
summary: A pilot conducting an external-load practice flight in a helicopter at a nontowered airport lost control and crashed while maneuvering to land. The investigation determined the pilot likely suffered a sudden acute cardiac event due to severe coronary artery disease, which impaired his performance during the precision landing.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll. Contributing to the accident was sun glare.
summary: The pilot landing on a private grass airstrip was blinded by the setting sun upon touchdown, causing the airplane to veer right into a tree line. This resulted in substantial damage to both wings and the right main landing gear, with no pre-accident malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing roll with a crosswind, which resulted in a runway excursion and impact with terrain.
summary: During the takeoff roll, the pilot reported the aircraft encountered a dust devil that raised the right wing, causing it to skid off the runway and impact a berm. The airplane rotated 360 degrees onto a taxiway, sustaining substantial damage to the right door frame and wing spar with no mechanical anomalies reported.

synopsis: The flight instructor's overpriming of the engine during multiple unsuccessful engine start attempts on an active runway, which resulted in an engine compartment fire.
summary: A flight instructor experienced an engine quit while taxiing off the runway, followed by a fire after multiple start attempts. The fire was likely caused by overpriming due to feeling rushed, though the initial power loss cause remained undetermined.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to land as soon as possible when the master caution warning light first illuminated as prescribed and his failure to ensure the proper setting of the caution panel segment lights before the flight.
summary: The pilot ignored a master caution warning caused by dimmed panel lights and continued flight until the helicopter suffered a total engine power loss. This resulted in a forced landing into trees with substantial damage, as the pilot failed to land immediately despite the low fuel warning.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing in a gusty crosswind which resulted in a runway excursion and collision with terrain.
summary: The pilot attempted two approaches to runway 22 in gusty crosswinds, executing a go-around after the first touchdown. During the second landing, a suspected right wind gust caused the aircraft to swerve off the runway onto grass, sustaining substantial damage to the engine mount and left wing.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control and subsequent aerodynamic stall due to spatial disorientation in night instrument meteorological conditions. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's distraction due to his cell phone use while maneuvering at low-altitude.
summary: The pilot departed at night in IMC with passengers, but cell phone use likely distracted him, causing spatial disorientation and a stall-spin into terrain. The pilot lacked required currency for night and instrument flight with passengers.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain an adequate obstacle clearance altitude from phone wires while performing low-level operations.
summary: During low-level cattle herding, a helicopter pilot struck a phone line with the main rotor blades at approximately 15 feet AGL. The entanglement caused a hard impact that collapsed the skids and substantially damaged the tail and rotor blades, with no pre-impact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: During a skydiving operation, the pilot bounced the aircraft three times on landing, then departed with the landing gear extended after it failed to retract. Post-flight inspection revealed bent propeller tips and substantial firewall damage caused by the runway impact, with no pre-impact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation because of a blocked fuel line that resulted from the pilot's improper maintenance practices and the pilot's subsequent failure to maintain adequate airspeed while attempting a forced landing, which led to the airplane exceeding its critical angle-of-attack and experiencing an aerodynamic stall.
summary: The pilot of an experimental kit airplane suffered total engine power loss during climb due to RTV silicone blocking a fuel flow transducer. The pilot subsequently stalled the aircraft while attempting an off-airport landing, resulting in a collision with terrain.

synopsis: The flight crewmembers' failure to perform the flight control check before takeoff, their attempt to take off with the gust lock system engaged, and their delayed execution of a rejected takeoff after they became aware that the controls were locked. Contributing to the accident were the flight crew's habitual noncompliance with checklists, Gulfstream Aerospace Corporation's failure to ensure that the G-IV gust lock/throttle lever interlock system would prevent an attempted takeoff with the gust lock engaged, and the Federal Aviation Administration's failure to detect this inadequacy during the G-IV's certification.
summary: A Gulfstream G-IV operated by Arizin Ventures crashed after overrunning runway 11 during a rejected takeoff at Laurence G. Hanscom Field. The impact and subsequent fire killed the two pilots, flight attendant, and four passengers, destroying the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control of the airplane during landing on water due to an encounter with wind shear, which resulted in the airplane's abnormal contact with the surface.
summary: A pilot flying a float-equipped airplane encountered violent wind shear at 50 feet during a high-speed water landing approach in high winds. The aircraft struck the water on its left side, damaging the left elevator and horizontal stabilizer, before bouncing and completing the landing without further incident.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate remedial action during landing on soft terrain, which resulted in a nose-over.
summary: The pilot nosed over an airplane equipped with tundra tires while landing on a tundra site after the wheels sank into unexpectedly mushy ground at 10 mph. The pilot reported no mechanical malfunctions, but the rudder, strut, and wing rib sustained damage.

synopsis: A loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's inadequate preflight inspection.
summary: The pilot reported an engine power loss at 400 feet after takeoff, forcing a nose-first landing that sheared the nose gear. Post-accident examination found no fuel in the tanks, attributed to a pre-existing leak that a thorough preflight inspection should have detected.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control during the aerobatic flight, which resulted in the airplane exceeding its critical angle of attack and entering an accelerated stall at a low altitude.
summary: During an aerobatic airshow, a pilot intentionally entered an inverted flat spin at the apex of a loop. After recovering at low altitude, the aircraft stalled and spiraled into the ground, with no mechanical failures found.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to compensate for wind conditions during landing, which resulted in a hard landing.
summary: The pilot aborted a first landing due to turbulence and encountered a left gust during the flare of a second approach, causing the aircraft to bank right and strike the runway hard with the nose gear. This resulted in the propeller hitting the runway and substantial damage to the engine firewall, with no mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The pilot did not maintain control of the airplane while landing.
summary: During landing on runway 28, a pilot and passenger encountered a side gust that caused the aircraft to drop and turn left despite rudder inputs. The airplane departed the runway, dug in its nose wheel, and came to rest inverted with substantial damage to the left wing and vertical stabilizer.

synopsis: The improper repair of the outer combustion case, which led to its ultimate failure due to the continued progression of a fatigue crack and resulted in a partial loss of engine power during takeoff.
summary: A commercial helicopter pilot experienced engine power loss and low rotor speed warnings while hovering over an oil platform, forcing a water landing. The cause was an unauthorized brazed repair on a fatigued outer combustion case that ruptured during flight.

synopsis: The instructor pilot's failure to regain control of the airplane following the student pilot's initial loss of control of the airplane.
summary: During a student's soft field takeoff practice, the aircraft drifted and the instructor took control to gain airspeed. The left gear collapsed upon runway contact, followed by a right wing strike, causing the airplane to spin off the runway and sustain substantial aft fuselage damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during a bounced landing.
summary: The pilot landed a glider on a grass runway near parked aircraft, bounced on touchdown, and veered right despite control inputs. The glider struck a parked airplane, causing substantial damage to its right wing, with no preexisting mechanical anomalies reported.

synopsis: The pilot's improper inflight planning, which resulted in fuel starvation and a loss of engine power. A factor was the pilot's selection of a low cruise flight altitude, which provided little time for the selection of suitable terrain for the forced landing or for engine restart procedures.
summary: The pilot flying north at 200 feet AGL ran out of fuel in the left tank, causing engine power loss and a forced landing. The aircraft struck spruce trees, sustaining substantial damage to the wings and fuselage, with no pre-accident mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination of the airframe and engine did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: During a maintenance test flight, a commercial pilot reported a fuel problem before the engine lost total power, forcing a landing that resulted in a collision with a tree and a parking lot. Although silicon was found in the fuel line, the source and the cause of the engine power loss could not be determined.

The Mexican DGAC notified the NTSB of an incident involving a UPS-operated Airbus A300 on June 1, 2014. The NTSB appointed a representative to assist the DGAC investigation, which will release all information.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power for undetermined reasons, which necessitated a forced landing on unsuitable terrain, during which the airplane flipped over and became partially submerged in water.
summary: During a cross-country flight at 1,500 feet, the pilot experienced engine roughness and power loss despite applying carburetor heat and confirming fuel selector position. The pilot executed a forced landing on a lake shoreline where the aircraft flipped and sustained substantial damage, though the investigation could not definitively link unfastened fuel bladder snaps or carburetor icing to the failure.
