synopsis: The GCAA notified the NTSB of an incident involving an Emirates Airbus A330-200 on October 04, 2014. The NTSB appointed a representative to assist the GCAA investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design of the engine, with details to be released by the GCAA.
summary: The GCAA notified the NTSB of an incident involving an Emirates Airbus A330-200 on October 04, 2014. The NTSB appointed a representative to assist the GCAA investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design of the engine, with details to be released by the GCAA.

synopsis: The CIAA of Peru notified the NTSB of an incident involving a Boeing 767-322 on November 04, 2014. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the CIAA.
summary: The CIAA of Peru notified the NTSB of an incident involving a Boeing 767-322 on November 04, 2014. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the CIAA.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control while landing in variable wind conditions, resulting in a runway excursion and collision with an object.
summary: The pilot landed an aircraft during final approach when a sudden left wind shift caused the airplane to drift right of the runway centerline. The aircraft departed the runway and struck a precision approach path indicator light with the right wing, causing substantial damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The failure of the left main landing gear to extend, which resulted in a gear-up landing. The reason for the left main landing gear's failure to operate normally could not be determined because postincident examination of the landing gear system did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: The pilot reported a left main landing gear failure to retract after takeoff, confirmed by a helicopter pilot observing the gear extended while the right gear was down. After unsuccessful troubleshooting and fuel burn, the pilot executed an uneventful gear-up landing, though the cause remained undetermined post-incident.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airspeed while maneuvering in gusting wind conditions, which resulted in the airplane exceeding its critical angle of attack and experiencing an aerodynamic stall.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a light sport airplane without a stall warning system or flaps entered a steep bank and impacted terrain while landing on a private grass airstrip. The reporter attributes the accident to a sudden gust or windshear causing an aerodynamic stall at low altitude, leaving insufficient time for recovery.

synopsis: The failure of the landing gear actuator housing during landing for reasons that could not be determined based on the available evidence.
summary: After takeoff, a pilot experienced landing gear and flap failure due to a split actuator housing causing hydraulic pressure loss. The gear collapsed during landing, resulting in a belly landing, left-side tip-over, and damage to the horizontal stabilizer.

synopsis: On October 14, 2014, the sole pilot of an amateur-built Vans RV-6A, VH-JON, collided with terrain near Moorabbin, Australia. The aircraft was substantially damaged and the pilot was fatally injured.
summary: On October 14, 2014, the sole pilot of an amateur-built Vans RV-6A, VH-JON, collided with terrain near Moorabbin, Australia. The aircraft was substantially damaged and the pilot was fatally injured.

synopsis: The airplane's encounter with supercooled large droplet (SLD) icing, which resulted in a loss of lift and a subsequent uncontrolled descent into terrain. Also causal was the pilot's preflight and in-flight decision to fly in known icing conditions in an airplane that was not certified to do so.
summary: A private pilot and two passengers flew a non-icing-certified single-engine airplane into supercooled large droplet icing during descent. Rapid ice accumulation caused an uncontrolled descent to ground contact, and while the CAPS rocket motor was expended, the parachute remained packed.

synopsis: An inflight collision with a goose while descending to land at the destination airport.
summary: A pilot and four passengers experienced a bird strike during descent when a goose impacted the radome and bulkhead. The pilot landed normally, but the collision caused substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The flight instructor's decision to conduct a night training flight in mountainous terrain without conducting or allowing the student to conduct appropriate preflight planning and his lack of situational awareness of the surrounding terrain altitude, which resulted in controlled flight into terrain.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot flew a Cessna into a mountain at night after the instructor changed the destination without planning or charts. The accident resulted from controlled flight into terrain because the crew was unaware of the 3,700-foot mountain elevation while flying at 3,000 feet.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from power lines while flying at a low altitude. Contributing to the accident was the obscuration of the pilot's visibility due to sun glare.
summary: An airline transport pilot and passenger crashed a single-engine airplane into unmarked overhead power lines while flying at low altitude in a valley. The accident was likely caused by sun glare preventing the pilot from seeing the lines, as no mechanical failures were found.

synopsis: A Diamond DA20-C1 (TF-FGC) carrying two pilots on an instructional flight suffered a loss of power 11 minutes after takeoff, forcing a landing near Hveragerdi, Iceland. The aircraft was substantially damaged, but there were no injuries.
summary: A Diamond DA20-C1 (TF-FGC) carrying two pilots on an instructional flight suffered a loss of power 11 minutes after takeoff, forcing a landing near Hveragerdi, Iceland. The aircraft was substantially damaged, but there were no injuries.

synopsis: The pilot's improper preflight planning, which resulted in a loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot experienced a total engine power loss enroute due to incorrect fuel calculations causing fuel exhaustion. He declared an emergency and performed a forced landing on a dirt road, resulting in substantial damage to the engine firewall.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airspeed while maneuvering, which resulted in the airplane exceeding its critical angle-of-attack and experiencing an aerodynamic stall. Contributing to the accident were abnormal engine operation due to improper magneto-to-engine ignition timing and the pilot's failure to have the airplane inspected before the flight as required by the special flight permit.
summary: A private pilot flew a newly purchased aircraft without the required pre-flight mechanic inspection. Post-accident examination found incorrect ignition timing likely causing abnormal engine operation, while witness accounts suggest the pilot may have stalled the airplane due to inadequate airspeed during the climb.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate clearance from trees during a precautionary landing. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's inadequate preflight inspection during which he failed to detect a loose drive belt, which resulted in an in-flight shudder.
summary: The pilot executed an autorotation after a helicopter shuddered during a crosswind turn due to a loose secondary drive reduction belt caused by pulley wear. During the flare, the tail rotor struck a tree, resulting in a loss of directional control.

synopsis: The noninstrument-rated pilot's decision to initiate the flight into known deteriorating weather conditions and his continued visual flight into instrument meteorological conditions, which ultimately resulted in a loss of airplane control. Contributing to the accident was the air traffic controller's failure to provide additional assistance to the pilot when it was apparent the pilot was having difficulties.
summary: A noninstrument-rated pilot departed into deteriorating IFR conditions with active icing and mountain obscuration AIRMETs, eventually losing control and impacting terrain while flying westbound. The accident resulted from the pilot's decision to continue into worsening weather despite ice accumulation and low clouds, compounded by the controller's failure to obtain or provide critical weather information.

synopsis: The flight instructor's delayed reaction in taking control of the helicopter during a student pilot's loss of control while landing.
summary: During an instructional "hydraulic off" landing, a student pilot lost control of the helicopter's yaw and pitch. The flight instructor took control but could not prevent the aircraft from rotating and striking the ground, causing substantial damage to the tail boom and main rotor blades.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during takeoff roll.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane inadvertently actuated the left brake during takeoff roll when his foot entangled in the rudder pedal cable. This caused a loss of control and groundloop, resulting in fuselage structural damage with no preimpact mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: A loss of directional control during landing for reasons that could not be determined based on the available information.
summary: A private pilot lost directional control while landing an experimental tailwheel airplane on a turf runway, causing a ground loop and inverted crash. The pilot reported a left main wheel axle separation, but the cause remained undetermined as the aircraft was not examined.

synopsis: The airplane's collision with water for reasons that could not be determined because the wreckage was not located.
summary: A flight instructor and commercial pilot departed for a local night instructional flight but requested to return without specifying a reason before losing contact. Their bodies were found in a lake days later, but the aircraft was not located and the cause of the collision with water remains undetermined.

synopsis: Engine power surges during takeoff for reasons that could not be determined during postaccident testing of the engine and the engine control unit.
summary: A helicopter pilot experienced compressor stalls and engine surges shortly after takeoff from an offshore platform, forcing a water landing. Post-flight testing of the engine and ECU found no definitive cause for the surges, though recorded data confirmed the surge condition occurred.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during the landing roll for reasons that could not be determined, because postaccident examination of the nosewheel assembly revealed no anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: A private pilot lost directional control during landing due to a deflated nosewheel oleo strut, causing the aircraft to veer left and exit the runway with right wing contact. Although the strut was found deflated, the investigation could not determine if it failed before or during the accident, leaving the exact cause of the loss of control undetermined.

synopsis: The certified flight instructor's failure to maintain helicopter control during the autorotation which resulted in a hard landing and subsequent roll over.
summary: During an instructional helicopter autorotation, a certified flight instructor and student attempted a 180-degree turn from 800 feet AGL. The instructor applied down collective as rotor RPM decayed, but the helicopter impacted the ground hard and rolled onto its left side, sustaining substantial damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The partial loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination of the engine revealed no evidence of any preimpact mechanical anomalies.
summary: The pilot reported an engine power loss at 35 feet after takeoff, forcing a landing in trees that caused substantial damage to the wings and fuselage. Postaccident examination found no preimpact mechanical anomalies, and the engine subsequently operated normally with full factory-specified rpm.

synopsis: A Russian pilot flying a Robinson R44 from Bugulma to Kazan suffered serious injuries when the aircraft was destroyed during a forced landing. The accident occurred near Novosheshminsk following an engine failure in the vicinity of a thunderstorm.
summary: A Russian pilot flying a Robinson R44 from Bugulma to Kazan suffered serious injuries when the aircraft was destroyed during a forced landing. The accident occurred near Novosheshminsk following an engine failure in the vicinity of a thunderstorm.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airspeed while maneuvering, which led to the airplane exceeding its critical angle-of-attack and experiencing an aerodynamic stall at an insufficient altitude to fully recover before collision with obstacles and terrain.
summary: The pilot reported that the aircraft entered a nose-down descent likely due to low airspeed and exceeding the critical angle of attack. Although the pilot recovered control at low altitude, the airplane subsequently collided with a flagpole, a restaurant, and terrain.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate fuel planning and improper fuel management, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to follow proper procedures in response to the loss of engine power.
summary: A commercial pilot experienced engine power loss and crashed a single-engine airplane into trees due to fuel starvation. The accident resulted from inadequate preflight fuel planning and failure to initialize the fuel-flow indicator, causing the pilot to misjudge remaining fuel and run the engine dry.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to ensure that the landing gear was fully extended in the down and locked position prior to touchdown, which resulted in the left main landing gear collapse, runway excursion, and impact with a runway exit sign.
summary: The pilot of a retractable gear airplane reported the left main gear retracted after touchdown, causing a runway excursion and empennage damage. Post-accident inspection revealed a broken gear actuator tooth, though the manufacturer stated the gear should not unseat under weight without positive pilot action.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the balloon when the wind unexpectedly increased which resulted in a collision with trees during the landing.
summary: The pilot of a hot-air balloon carrying 11 passengers encountered increasing winds of 15 to 20 mph during landing. An attempt to activate the rapid deflation valve was slower than expected, causing the balloon to collide with a tree and sustain substantial basket damage.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control after the weight-shift-control aircraft encountered low-level wind shear shortly before touchdown. Also causal to the accident was the pilot's inadequate preflight weather assessment that failed to correctly determine the actual location and speed of the approaching line of thunderstorms.
summary: The pilot of a weight-shift-control aircraft encountered low-level wind shear from an approaching thunderstorm squall line while attempting an off-field landing in a pasture. The aircraft lost altitude and impacted the ground with substantial damage due to the pilot's failure to correctly identify the storm's location and speed.

synopsis: A failure of the right engine magneto distributor drive gears, which resulted in a total loss of engine power during takeoff. Contributing to the accident was the operator's failure to inspect and maintain the magnetos in accordance with the engine manufacturer's specifications.
summary: A private pilot aborted takeoff in a multi-engine airplane after the right engine lost power due to failed magneto distributor gears. The aircraft exited the runway and impacted rough terrain; investigation revealed the gears had missing teeth and discoloration from exceeding maintenance intervals.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airspeed while attempting to return to the airport after a reported engine problem, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall/spin.
summary: A commercial pilot conducting an on-demand cargo charter flight reported left engine trouble shortly after takeoff and attempted a return landing. The pilot failed to maintain adequate airspeed during a turn, resulting in an aerodynamic stall/spin and crash, though no mechanical failure was found.

synopsis: Loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion. Contributing to the accident was an incorrectly calibrated fuel totalizer.
summary: A sport pilot experienced an engine power loss during a straight-in final approach while refueling, resulting in an emergency landing where the aircraft struck a fence and sustained substantial damage. The pilot attributed the incident to an inaccurate fuel totalizer calibration that falsely indicated 3.6 gallons of fuel in an empty tank.

synopsis: An undetermined pilot's failure to maintain clearance from an electrical transmission tower resulting in substantial damage to a main rotor blade. Postaccident investigation could not determine which of two pilots was flying the helicopter at the time the damage occurred.
summary: Two pilots operated a helicopter equipped with an aerial platform for powerline work. Substantial main rotor blade damage was discovered postflight, but the investigation could not determine which flight caused the damage or identify any mechanical failures or abnormal flight characteristics.

synopsis: The noninstrument-rated pilot's improper decision to fly to the destination airport and into known instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in his controlled flight into mountainous terrain during a snow storm.
summary: A noninstrument-rated pilot flying a Mooney into known heavy snow and poor visibility ignored FBO warnings and lost contact while circling below 1,000 feet. The aircraft crashed into mountainous terrain due to the pilot's improper decision to continue the flight into adverse weather.

synopsis: The flight crew of a BAE Jetstream 41 operating from Medellin to Quibdó declared an emergency after the No. 1 engine stopped during cruise. They returned for a single-engine landing, and a post-flight inspection revealed a hole in the engine gearbox.
summary: The flight crew of a BAE Jetstream 41 operating from Medellin to Quibdó declared an emergency after the No. 1 engine stopped during cruise. They returned for a single-engine landing, and a post-flight inspection revealed a hole in the engine gearbox.

synopsis: On November 11, 2014, a Cessna 150M (C-GJAO) operated by Flyblocktime Inc. impacted terrain near Whitney, Ontario, while en route from Ottawa to Toronto. The pilot and one passenger were fatally injured, and the aircraft was substantially damaged.
summary: On November 11, 2014, a Cessna 150M (C-GJAO) operated by Flyblocktime Inc. impacted terrain near Whitney, Ontario, while en route from Ottawa to Toronto. The pilot and one passenger were fatally injured, and the aircraft was substantially damaged.

synopsis: The pilot's improper decision to land long (past the midpoint) on a wet runway and his failure to conduct a go-around when the airplane did not touch down at the approach end of the runway, which resulted in an overrun.
summary: The pilot landed a rain-soaked aircraft on runway 14, ran off the end, and struck a fence, crushing the left wing and collapsing the nose gear. Although the pilot reported brake failure, tests showed normal operation, and the accident was attributed to hydroplaning and a late touchdown.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain airplane control during the initial climb, resulting in a runway excursion and substantial damage to the engine firewall. The student pilot's lack of overall flying experience was a factor.
summary: A student pilot with 45 hours experienced a violent 90-degree left veer during takeoff, causing the aircraft to depart the runway and cross an intersecting runway. The excursion resulted in a buckled engine firewall, with no reported mechanical issues or wind gusts identified as the cause.

synopsis: A Piper PA-31, XB-ZAX, impacted terrain near Ciudad Victoria, Mexico, while en route to Torreon, killing the pilot and five passengers. The aircraft sustained substantial damage, and the investigation is under the jurisdiction of the Dirección General de Aeronáutica Civil.
summary: A Piper PA-31, XB-ZAX, impacted terrain near Ciudad Victoria, Mexico, while en route to Torreon, killing the pilot and five passengers. The aircraft sustained substantial damage, and the investigation is under the jurisdiction of the Dirección General de Aeronáutica Civil.

synopsis: N263WN captain's failure to maintain a safe clearance from the parked N8314L resulting in a ground collision. N263WN captain's failure to maintain a safe clearance from the parked N8314L resulting in a ground collision.
summary: Southwest Airlines flight 8751, a Boeing 737-700 functional check flight, collided with parked flight 301, a Boeing 737-800, while taxiing on taxiway B. The captain's left wingtip struck the parked aircraft's right horizontal stabilizer due to over-correction, causing minor and substantial damage respectively with no injuries.

synopsis: A loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined due to extensive damage sustained during the collision and postaccident water immersion.
summary: A private pilot flying a routine cross-country approach likely experienced engine power loss after the fuel mixture cable disconnected from the carburetor. The aircraft impacted a tree 2,260 feet short of the runway and came to rest in a river, though investigators could not definitively confirm the cable failure caused the accident.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to properly set the throttle prior to engine start, which resulted in a loss of control and collision with a hangar.
summary: A pilot conducting a solo local departure primed the engine with the throttle fully open instead of retarded. The aircraft accelerated upon start, striking a hangar and parked airplane, causing substantial left wing damage due to the throttle error.

synopsis: The exhaustion of the fuel supply resulting in a complete loss of engine power.
summary: A pilot and flight instructor experienced intermittent electrical issues and fuel exhaustion during a night VFR flight, leading to a forced landing where the aircraft struck wires and impacted the ground. The accident likely resulted from fuel depletion, potentially exacerbated by inaccurate fuel gauge readings caused by the electrical problems.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed and his exceedance of the airplane's critical angle-of-attack for reasons that could not be determined based on the available evidence, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall/spin. Contributing to the accident was the improperly installed oil gauge housing extension, which resulted in a loss of oil quantity and right engine power.
summary: An airline transport pilot flying a twin-engine aircraft en route lost the right engine due to an improperly secured oil gauge housing, causing oil loss. The pilot failed to maintain airspeed while the autopilot was active, resulting in an aerodynamic stall/spin and a near-vertical impact.

synopsis: The failure of the gust lock actuator solenoid for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination of the rudder gust lock system revealed no mechanical malfunctions or failures that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: An airline transport pilot experienced uncoordinated flight and right yaw during takeoff and climb due to a rudder gust lock actuator solenoid failure that left the rudder locked. The pilot returned for a landing with minor wing tip damage after the gust lock pin engaged the ball nut while the bellcrank remained connected to the rudder quadrant.

synopsis: The pilot's engagement of the emergency parking brake during the landing roll, which decreased the airplane's braking performance and prevented it from stopping on the available runway. Contributing to the pilot's decision to engage the emergency parking brake was the expectation of a faster rate of deceleration and considerably shorter wet runway landing distance provided by the airplane flight manual than that experienced by the crew upon touchdown and an actual wet runway friction level lower than the assumed runway fiction level used in the calculation of the stopping distances published in the airplane flight manual.
summary: Pilots of a very light jet conducting an ILS approach in IMC landed with excessive speed and a tailwind. The pilot applied the emergency parking brake when deceleration was insufficient, causing skidding and hydroplaning that led to a runway excursion into a drainage ditch.

synopsis: The pilot inadvertently applied the left brake during the landing roll which resulted in a loss of directional control and subsequent impact with terrain.
summary: During the landing roll, the pilot's foot slipped off the rudder pedal, causing an inadvertent left brake application that veered the airplane off the runway left side. Despite adding power to avoid a ditch, the aircraft contacted the ditch and nosed over, sustaining substantial damage with no reported mechanical failures.

aircraft: Ross H/Herriott M VANS AIRCRAFT RV 3
synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control, which resulted in a stall/spin. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to obtain adequate familiarization in the accident airplane type before the accident.
summary: A pilot with only 4 hours of experience in the aircraft lost control during traffic pattern turns shortly after takeoff, resulting in a stall/spin and crash. The accident was likely caused by the pilot's lack of experience with the specific airplane type, while toxicology results indicated marijuana presence unlikely to have impaired performance.

synopsis: The collapse of the left main landing gear for reasons that could not be determined during postaccident examination.
summary: During landing after a personal flight, the pilot reported the left main landing gear collapsed despite the green indicator light being on and no warning horn sounding. Post-accident testing found no mechanical faults, and the specific cause of the collapse could not be determined.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control during the landing flare with a crosswind.
summary: The pilot of an airplane landing at a mountain dirt airstrip encountered a sudden right crosswind during the flare, causing the right wing to lift. Unable to maintain the runway centerline, the aircraft descended into an adjacent creek, sustaining substantial damage to the firewall and forward fuselage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: On November 17, 2014, a Piper PA-25-235 (PR-WIZ) impacted a sugar cane field in Cidade Gaúcha, Brazil, destroying the aircraft and fatally injuring the pilot. The flight was conducted under Brazilian regulations, and the investigation is under the jurisdiction of CENIPA.
summary: On November 17, 2014, a Piper PA-25-235 (PR-WIZ) impacted a sugar cane field in Cidade Gaúcha, Brazil, destroying the aircraft and fatally injuring the pilot. The flight was conducted under Brazilian regulations, and the investigation is under the jurisdiction of CENIPA.

synopsis: A loss of tail rotor effectiveness while hovering in gusting crosswind conditions resulting in the student pilot's loss of control of the helicopter. Contributing was the delayed remedial action of the flight instructor.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor experienced an uncontrollable right yaw during a hover in 15-knot winds, requiring an autorotation. The helicopter's tail rotor struck a ground handling dolly upon landing, causing substantial damage, with no pre-impact mechanical failure reported.

synopsis: A hard landing for reasons that could not be determined based on the available evidence.
summary: The helicopter owner-pilot discovered a cracked left skid and hard landing damage after a local flight, though she and a passenger denied a hard landing occurred. Investigators could not determine when the damage happened or who was flying, as prior flights by an instructor and repositioning showed no observed damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed during a forced landing following a total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation, which resulted in the airplane exceeding its critical angle of attack, and an aerodynamic stall at a low altitude. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's improper fuel management.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a cross-country flight diverted due to weather but suffered engine power loss in the traffic pattern after extending landing gear. The accident resulted from fuel starvation caused by the fuel selector being set to an empty tank, leading to an aerodynamic stall and terrain impact.

synopsis: A loss of airplane control for reasons that could not be determined based on available evidence.
summary: A commercial pilot lost control and crashed during a water calibration flight after agricultural spraying. No pre-impact mechanical failures were found, and the specific cause of the loss of control remains undetermined.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airplane control while maneuvering, which resulted in a collision with mountainous terrain.
summary: A private pilot flying a local area flight collided with mountain terrain in a vertical nose-down attitude. The investigation concluded the pilot likely lost control while maneuvering at low altitudes, leaving insufficient height to recover before impact.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate altitude while landing in gusty wind conditions, which resulted in a collision with power lines while on final approach.
summary: During final approach to a turf runway, the pilot added power as the airplane sank in gusty winds, but the engine hesitated. The right main gear struck power lines, causing the aircraft to pitch down and impact the runway with substantial fuselage damage.

synopsis: The loss of airplane control after encountering windshear.
summary: A sport pilot performing touch-and-go landings on runway 17R encountered a wind gust and low-level windshear, causing the aircraft to drift left unresponsive to rudder. During the go-around, the airplane clipped an airport sign and landed on adjacent grass, sustaining substantial firewall damage.

synopsis: The pilot's improper decision to descend the airplane at an airspeed greater than the published best glide speed following an erroneous oil pressure indication, which resulted in an off-airport landing. Contributing to the erroneous oil pressure indication was the faulty oil pressure transducer. Contributing to the severity of the accident was the pilot's late deployment of the ballistic parachute system.
summary: A private pilot flying a personal cross-country flight diverted after a faulty oil pressure transducer caused erroneous warnings and the pilot reduced engine power. The aircraft crashed into trees after the pilot descended too fast and deployed the ballistic parachute at 453 feet MSL, which was too low for full deceleration.

synopsis: The partial loss of engine power during climb after takeoff for a reasons that could not be determined because postaccident engine examination revealed no evidence of mechanical malfunctions or failures.
summary: A private pilot experienced rough running and power loss during climb after takeoff. Despite applying carburetor heat, he performed a forced landing that resulted in the aircraft impacting a chain link fence, though post-accident examination found no mechanical anomalies.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate fuel planning, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot circled the destination due to weather, depleting fuel reserves calculated for 90 minutes. Approximately 4 miles from the runway, the aircraft suffered a total engine power loss from fuel exhaustion, resulting in a forced landing that impacted trees and terrain.

synopsis: The pilot's inadvertent selection of an incorrect frequency, which resulted in his inability to activate the airport lighting, and his subsequent decision to continue the approach in dark night conditions despite having not positively identified the runway environment.
summary: During a night instrument approach, the pilot failed to activate runway lights due to incorrectly tuning the CTAF frequency. Consequently, he landed on a taxiway instead of the runway, overran the end, and struck a sign, causing substantial damage to the right wing.

synopsis: A loss of engine power during takeoff due to excessive debris in the fuel system.
summary: A noncertificated pilot lost engine power during takeoff due to fuel flow restriction from debris in the gascolator. The aircraft struck a vehicle and terrain after the canopy opened, resulting in an inverted crash with no postimpact fire.

synopsis: The noninstrument-rated pilot's improper decision to attempt visual flight in instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in an in-flight loss of airplane control due to spatial disorientation. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's impaired decision-making due to the effects of ethanol and chlordiazepoxide.
summary: A noninstrument-rated private pilot departed at night in instrument meteorological conditions and crashed into a wooded area due to spatial disorientation. The accident was likely caused by impaired judgment from ingested ethanol and chlordiazepoxide, leading to a flight beyond the pilot's capabilities.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-31-350 operating Southern Air Flight 302 lost right engine power while maneuvering for a second landing attempt at Nassau due to reported landing gear problems. The aircraft was forced to ditch in the ocean six miles from shore, resulting in the death of one passenger from a medical emergency.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-31-350 operating Southern Air Flight 302 lost right engine power while maneuvering for a second landing attempt at Nassau due to reported landing gear problems. The aircraft was forced to ditch in the ocean six miles from shore, resulting in the death of one passenger from a medical emergency.

synopsis: A pilot and two passengers were fatally injured when a Beech A36, PT-WVM, impacted terrain in Macarani, Brazil, after an inflight loss of control. The personal flight was en route from Salvador to Belo Horizonte when the accident occurred.
summary: A pilot and two passengers were fatally injured when a Beech A36, PT-WVM, impacted terrain in Macarani, Brazil, after an inflight loss of control. The personal flight was en route from Salvador to Belo Horizonte when the accident occurred.

synopsis: The pilot/mechanic's failure to properly secure the pitch link hardware of one main rotor blade to the rotating swash plate, which resulted in the pitch link separating in flight and a subsequent loss of control.
summary: A commercial helicopter pilot-mechanic crashed the aircraft during a test flight after a main rotor blade separated due to an improperly torqued pitch change link attachment bolt. The loose fastener allowed the locknut to fail, causing the blade to strike the tail and resulting in an uncontrollable descent and impact.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing with a gusting crosswind, which resulted in a hard landing adjacent to the runway.
summary: A private pilot experienced smoke from an oil leak onto the exhaust during cruise and a hard landing with wing and fuselage damage caused by a gusting crosswind. The pilot attributed the landing incident to a failure to maintain control in 19-knot gusts, while the smoke was cleared by opening a vent window.

synopsis: The Afghanistan Civil Aviation Authority notified the NTSB of a Boeing 737-400 accident on November 7, 2014. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the ACAA investigation, which will release all information.
summary: The Afghanistan Civil Aviation Authority notified the NTSB of a Boeing 737-400 accident on November 7, 2014. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the ACAA investigation, which will release all information.

synopsis: The total loss of engine power during takeoff following a touch-and-go landing for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination of the engine did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: An airline transport pilot experienced an engine failure at 100 feet during a touch-and-go takeoff, forcing a hard landing that resulted in the aircraft impacting a trailer and pole, inverting, and separating the right wing. Post-accident examination found no mechanical anomalies to explain the engine silence.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control when executing a landing with a tailwind, resulting in impact with a retaining wall.
summary: A sport pilot flying an experimental light sport powered parachute lost control during a tailwind approach to an off-airfield landing. The pilot attempted to abort but could not establish a climb, resulting in a collision with a retaining wall and substantial airframe damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll, which resulted in a runway excursion and encounter with terrain.
summary: The pilot reported that after landing on the centerline, the airplane pulled left, exited the runway, and nosed over in a swampy area. This resulted in substantial damage to the left wing strut and wing, with no preimpact mechanical malfunctions reported.

synopsis: The pilot's improper recovery from a bounced landing during gusty crosswind conditions.
summary: The pilot landed a single-engine airplane in 10 to 15-knot crosswinds, but the aircraft bounced and weather-vaned before the propeller struck the runway. This caused the airplane to veer off the right side, collapsing the nose gear and breaking the engine mounts.

synopsis: An ATR72-212A experienced excessive vibration during approach to Visby Airport, leading to a right engine shutdown and single-engine landing. Post-incident inspection revealed damage to the right propeller hub, prompting an investigation by the Swedish Accident Investigation Authority.
summary: An ATR72-212A experienced excessive vibration during approach to Visby Airport, leading to a right engine shutdown and single-engine landing. Post-incident inspection revealed damage to the right propeller hub, prompting an investigation by the Swedish Accident Investigation Authority.

synopsis: The pilot's inability to identify the power line during the initial approach in night visual meteorological conditions and his subsequent failure to avoid the power line once he identified it on final approach.
summary: During a night off-airport landing, a helicopter pilot struck power lines at 20 feet AGL while attempting to avoid them after failing to identify them during initial orbits. The pilot maintained control and landed safely, though the main rotor sustained substantial damage to three blades and minor damage to two.

synopsis: The loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion, which resulted from the non-certificated pilot's inadequate preflight planning and inflight decision making.
summary: A non-certificated pilot and passengers experienced an engine power loss during a local flight, forcing a landing 10 miles from the airport. The accident caused substantial damage to the wings, fuselage, and landing gear, with investigation revealing empty but unbreached wing fuel tanks.

synopsis: Two pilots operating a Cessna 152 for the Madhya Pradesh Flying Club were fatally injured when the aircraft collided with the ground shortly after takeoff from Indore Airport. The airplane was substantially damaged, and the investigation remains under the jurisdiction of the Government of India.
summary: Two pilots operating a Cessna 152 for the Madhya Pradesh Flying Club were fatally injured when the aircraft collided with the ground shortly after takeoff from Indore Airport. The airplane was substantially damaged, and the investigation remains under the jurisdiction of the Government of India.

synopsis: Maintenance personnel's inadequate inspection of the No. 2 cylinder valve area during the most recent annual inspection, which resulted in the in-flight failure of the intake valve springs due to rust on the spring surfaces and subsequent fatigue cracking.
summary: The pilot of a skydiving aircraft executed a forced landing after an in-flight engine failure caused by fractured No. 2 cylinder intake valve springs. The accident resulted from rust-induced fatigue fractures that likely went undetected during an inadequate annual inspection of the valve area.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power to both engines during descent due to fuel starvation as a result of an interruption of the fuel flow, which resulted in a forced landing to a short strip and a subsequent overrun.
summary: A commercial pilot flying an experimental airplane experienced dual engine flameouts during descent, likely due to fuel starvation from a blocked fuel filter. The pilot attempted a forced landing on a short strip but overran into rough terrain, causing substantial damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll resulting in a runway excursion and collision with hangars.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel-equipped airplane reported that after a normal touchdown, the aircraft veered left off the runway and struck two hangars with both wings. No preimpact mechanical malfunction was reported, but both wings sustained substantial damage.

synopsis: The total loss of engine power due to carburetor icing, which resulted from the pilot's failure to use carburetor heat while operating at low-power settings in an area conducive to carburetor icing.
summary: The pilot lost engine power on short final after cycling carburetor heat, causing a collision with rising terrain. The accident likely resulted from carburetor ice forming during power reduction, as confirmed by atmospheric conditions and a witness report.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to comprehend the significance of the wake turbulence that a preceding helicopter would generate during departure, which resulted in a loss of airplane control during landing. Contributing to the accident was the lack of Federal Aviation Administration wake turbulence separation criteria for a small airplane following a helicopter.
summary: A student pilot flying a Cirrus SR20 solo at an uncontrolled airport encountered wake turbulence from a departing Sikorsky UH-60 helicopter while attempting to land. The resulting uncommanded left bank caused a loss of control, leading to the aircraft impacting left of the runway and cartwheeling.

synopsis: the pilot's conduct of an approach in structural icing conditions without turning on the airplane's wing and horizontal stabilizer deice system, leading to ice accumulation on those surfaces, and without using the appropriate landing performance speeds for the weather conditions and airplane weight, as indicated in the airplane's standard operating procedures, which together resulted in an aerodynamic stall at an altitude at which a recovery was not possible.
summary: The pilot of an Embraer Phenom 100 crashed into three houses and the ground while on IFR approach to runway 14 at Montgomery County Airpark in visual conditions. The impact and subsequent fire killed the pilot, two passengers, and three house occupants, destroying the aircraft.

synopsis: A Schweizer 269C-1 helicopter (CS-HFD) impacted terrain near Ponte de Sôr, Portugal, during an instructional flight. The instructor and student pilots were fatally injured and the helicopter was destroyed under unknown circumstances in visual meteorological conditions.
summary: A Schweizer 269C-1 helicopter (CS-HFD) impacted terrain near Ponte de Sôr, Portugal, during an instructional flight. The instructor and student pilots were fatally injured and the helicopter was destroyed under unknown circumstances in visual meteorological conditions.

synopsis: The pilot did not maintain directional control of the airplane during the landing flare when a sudden wind shift occurred.
summary: The pilot of a ski-equipped aircraft attempted a three-point landing on runway 18 in gusting crosswinds but drifted right despite control inputs. During the go-around, the right main gear collapsed under side load, causing the aircraft to cartwheel and sustain substantial wing and firewall damage.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane while braking during landing rollout.
summary: The pilot reported that a tail wheel-equipped airplane nosed over during landing rollout on a grass runway with variable wet and dry surfaces. The pilot attributed the accident to variable braking action and noted that more careful brake application might have prevented it, with no mechanical failures involved.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a wire during an off-airport landing following a partial loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined during postaccident examination.
summary: A student pilot experienced a partial power loss during a solo cross-country return flight, leading to an emergency landing in a field where the aircraft struck a wire and sustained substantial damage. While the left magneto showed wear, investigators could not determine if carburetor icing caused the power loss, as no definitive engine anomaly was found.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airspeed during the final approach, which resulted in a stall/mush. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to obtain training in the pusher-type airplane.
summary: The pilot, flying a new pusher-type airplane for the first time, reduced power on final approach at 100 feet and the aircraft suddenly dropped. The plane impacted the ground in a flat attitude, causing substantial fuselage damage, though the engine was reported running normally.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate approach and excessive airspeed, which resulted in a long landing, the subsequent runway overrun, and impact with terrain. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's delay in aborting the landing.
summary: The pilot reported that during final approach, excessive airspeed caused a long landing, and a subsequent go-around attempt failed to achieve flying speed before the aircraft overran the runway. The airplane impacted terrain, sustaining substantial damage to the wings, fuselage, and engine compartment with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the airplane during landing in gusty wind conditions.
summary: The pilot lost control during landing due to gusty winds while repositioning the aircraft, impacting terrain adjacent to the runway. This resulted in substantial damage to the right wing spar, with the owner reporting no pre-accident mechanical anomalies.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control during the landing and his poor decision not to abort the landing before the airplane traveled off the end of the airstrip.
summary: The pilot landed on a 1,944-foot grass airstrip, overran the end, crossed a paved runway, and nosed over into an embankment, damaging the firewall. The pilot attributed the loss of directional control to a wind gust, though nearby winds were only 6 knots, and it remained undetermined if high airspeed or a long landing contributed.

synopsis: The student pilot's failure to maintain directional control and the flight instructor's delayed remedial action during landing. Contributing was the snow on the runway surface.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot veered off the runway during landing when the left main gear contacted snow, causing the aircraft to enter a snowbank and impact the ground with the right wing. The instructor reported no mechanical failure, but the airplane sustained substantial damage.

synopsis: A Beech 76 pilot and passenger sustained no injuries after the aircraft was substantially damaged during an emergency landing at Cambridge International Airport. The incident occurred following a mechanical failure of the nose landing gear extension system.
summary: A Beech 76 pilot and passenger sustained no injuries after the aircraft was substantially damaged during an emergency landing at Cambridge International Airport. The incident occurred following a mechanical failure of the nose landing gear extension system.

synopsis: The improper installation of a doubler patch, which prevented the right flap from actuating and moving properly and led to the subsequent interference with the aileron.
summary: During a proficiency flight, a pilot experienced uncommanded right yoke movement and a loud pop while retracting flaps, causing the right flap to buckle. Post-accident examination revealed an improperly installed doubler patch altered skin curvature, fracturing brackets and allowing the flap to contact the aileron.

synopsis: A loss of engine power while maneuvering at low altitude for reasons that could not be determined during postaccident examination.
summary: The pilot, flying an aircraft he had not operated recently, experienced engine power loss at 1,200 feet AGL and forced landed, striking an irrigation pipe and fence post. He attributed the failure to a broken cowl flap cable causing overheating, though post-accident examination found no definitive mechanical malfunction.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, resulting in a hard landing.
summary: The pilot experienced a nose gear collapse during landing after a local flight when the gear struck the runway first following a bounce. Post-accident examination found no pre-impact mechanical failures, but the gear separated and damaged the fuselage as the aircraft stopped 300 feet down the runway.

synopsis: an inadvertent encounter with clear air turbulence while the flight attendants were returning to their seats.
summary: During cruise at FL340, the crew encountered severe turbulence causing ±300 feet altitude fluctuation while flight attendants were stowing carts. This resulted in minor injuries to passengers and crew, including one flight attendant who later sustained a fractured lumbar vertebra.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain situational awareness during a turn which resulted in a loss of airplane control.
summary: During a night touch-and-go, the pilot initiated a left climbing turn and looked outside to orient, inadvertently entering a steep left bank from which recovery was impossible. The aircraft impacted terrain with substantial damage to the fuselage and wings, with the pilot reporting no pre-accident mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to fly the airplane with known engine deficiencies and his subsequent exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack following a loss of engine power, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and loss of control after takeoff.
summary: A private pilot departed an experimental amateur-built airplane with known brake and engine issues despite warnings. The aircraft lost engine power, entered a stall, and impacted the ground due to a loss of control, though the specific cause of the power loss remained undetermined.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain airspeed while maneuvering at a low altitude, which resulted in the airplane exceeding its critical angle-of-attack and experiencing an aerodynamic stall.
summary: A sport pilot flying a local flight in an accident airplane experienced an engine "missing" sound followed by a vertical descent into trees after three turns. The probable cause was the pilot's failure to maintain airspeed during maneuvers, resulting in an aerodynamic stall, while no pre-impact engine failure was found.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to descend below the recommended altitude during approach for landing in night visual meteorological conditions, and his failure to see and avoid a lighted tower, which resulted in collision with the tower and a subsequent total loss of engine power.
summary: A private pilot flying a night instrument approach struck a 367-ft cellular tower at 275 ft above airport elevation after cancelling the flight plan. The aircraft suffered total engine power loss and impacted terrain, with no mechanical failures found, violating FAA altitude guidance over congested areas.

synopsis: The failure of the uncertified engine's front connecting rod needle bearing, which resulted in damage to the front piston and a subsequent loss of engine power. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision to operate the airplane with the uncertified engine over a town that had no suitable area to land.
summary: The pilot reported total engine power loss during cruise over a town due to a failed front connecting rod needle bearing in an uncertified engine. The aircraft struck a tree and tombstone during a forced landing to a cemetery, an outcome exacerbated by operating the uncertified engine over an area with no suitable landing sites.

synopsis: The nose landing gear collapse as a result of the fracture of the engine mount at the nose gear actuator attachment point in an area that a service bulletin (SB) recommended for inspection. Contributing to the accident was maintenance personnel's inadequate compliance with the SB.
summary: The pilot reported a sharp left veer and nose gear collapse immediately after landing, caused by a fractured engine mount. Maintenance records indicated the required inspection for this crack was likely missed or failed during the most recent annual check.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from terrain while performing an intentional, abrupt low-level maneuver.
summary: A commercial pilot conducting a personal flight with a passenger struck a hillside while performing a low-level wingover maneuver. The pilot pulled up too late to clear the terrain, resulting in a left-bank impact on a steep slope with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to prevent the helicopter from settling with power while maneuvering at a low altitude, which resulted in a loss of control and subsequent hard landing.
summary: During a low-altitude herding operation for a DNR pronghorn capture project, the pilot maneuvered a helicopter backward when animals ran underneath. The aircraft experienced a settling with power condition, resulting in a hard landing that caused structural damage to the tail boom and bulkhead.

synopsis: The mechanic's improper installation of the elevator trim actuator, which resulted in reversed elevator trim control, and his subsequent failure to detect the misrigging of the elevator cables during the postmaintenance inspection.
summary: A pilot experienced a severe nose-down pitch during a post-maintenance test flight due to a mechanic misrigging elevator control cables after replacing the trim actuator. The pilot identified the control reversal, applied opposite trim, and landed safely after the mechanic failed to verify correct tab movement per the manual.

synopsis: an inadvertent encounter with birds during approach to land that resulted in substantial damage.
summary: Southwest Airlines Flight 3118, a Boeing 737-76N, struck multiple birds while descending through 2,500 feet on approach to Baltimore/Washington International Airport. The event caused substantial damage to the forward pressure bulkhead and left wing, though no passengers or crew were injured.

synopsis: A Liberty Aerospace XL2 operated by the Lombok Institute of Flight Technology was reported missing on October 30, 2014, and later found substantially damaged south of Moyo Island. The certified flight instructor and student pilot were fatally injured, with the investigation remaining under Indonesian jurisdiction.
summary: A Liberty Aerospace XL2 operated by the Lombok Institute of Flight Technology was reported missing on October 30, 2014, and later found substantially damaged south of Moyo Island. The certified flight instructor and student pilot were fatally injured, with the investigation remaining under Indonesian jurisdiction.

synopsis: On December 2, 2014, an Ayres Trush S2R-T34 operated by PT. Elang Nunsantara Air ditched in the sea near Manado, Indonesia, under unknown circumstances. The aircraft was destroyed, and the pilot and engineer are presumed fatally injured.
summary: On December 2, 2014, an Ayres Trush S2R-T34 operated by PT. Elang Nunsantara Air ditched in the sea near Manado, Indonesia, under unknown circumstances. The aircraft was destroyed, and the pilot and engineer are presumed fatally injured.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control and subsequent impact with terrain in instrument meteorological conditions.
summary: The pilot attempted six unsuccessful instrument approaches in IMC, declining controller suggestions to divert due to low fuel and fatigue. The aircraft impacted terrain after a rapid descent, likely caused by spatial disorientation or descending below minimums, compounded by poor judgment and potential medical impairment.

synopsis: The CIAIAC notified the NTSB of a June 23, 2014 accident involving a Boeing 737-8AS. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation as the State of Manufacturer, with all information to be released by the CIAIAC.
summary: The CIAIAC notified the NTSB of a June 23, 2014 accident involving a Boeing 737-8AS. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation as the State of Manufacturer, with all information to be released by the CIAIAC.

synopsis: On December 6, 2014, a Yakutia Airlines Boeing 757-236PCF (VQ-BPY) experienced decompression and a cargo door opening four minutes after takeoff from Magadan. The Federal Air Transport Agency is investigating the incident with an NTSB representative appointed as the manufacturer's accredited observer.
summary: On December 6, 2014, a Yakutia Airlines Boeing 757-236PCF (VQ-BPY) experienced decompression and a cargo door opening four minutes after takeoff from Magadan. The Federal Air Transport Agency is investigating the incident with an NTSB representative appointed as the manufacturer's accredited observer.

synopsis: The pilot's delayed decision to abort the takeoff. Contributing to the accident are an inadequate modification to the seat position, and the pilot's failure to check flight controls for freedom and correct movement.
summary: The pilot of an experimental airplane moved the seat forward without checking for flight control stick restriction. During takeoff, the restricted stick prevented rotation, leading to an aborted takeoff, runway excursion, and substantial damage after impacting trees.

synopsis: The partial loss of engine power during takeoff due to an improperly configured carburetor and fuel supply system. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's loss of airplane control during the off-field landing, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
summary: The private pilot-owner of an experimental light sport airplane experienced partial engine power loss during a crosswind turn after takeoff. Postaccident examination found carburetor and fuel system installation discrepancies not meeting manufacturer manuals, causing the power loss, subsequent stall, and terrain impact.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed while maneuvering at an excessive bank angle at a low altitude, which resulted in an accelerated stall and spin with insufficient altitude for a recovery.
summary: During an aerial survey flight, the pilot likely entered an excessive bank to inspect a water leak, causing an accelerated stall with insufficient altitude for recovery. The aircraft impacted the ground and burned, with no mechanical failures found.

synopsis: The student pilot's improper flare which resulted in a hard landing and subsequent nose gear collapse.
summary: A student pilot conducting solo takeoff and landings experienced a hard landing and bounce on the second approach, causing the nose gear to collapse into the firewall. The pilot reported no preexisting mechanical failures, attributing the incident to the landing technique.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control while landing, which resulted in a collision with a snow bank. Contributing to the accident was ice that covered the landing surface.
summary: A pilot with 635 total hours landed a helicopter at a private heliport in -1°C conditions. The aircraft spun on black ice after touchdown, causing the tail rotor to strike a snow bank and sustain substantial damage, with no mechanical failures reported.

synopsis: The loss of engine power during cruise flight for reasons that could not be determined based on the available information.
summary: A student pilot flying a helicopter solo experienced total engine power loss during cruise, forcing an autorotation to a field. The tail struck the ground during flare, severing the tail rotor and causing substantial fuselage damage, though a subsequent engine test showed no anomalies.

synopsis: A short in the trim system's wires and connector, which resulted in the elevator trim being in a full nose-down position.
summary: During a visual approach, the copilot applied excessive aft pressure to counteract a full nose-down elevator trim caused by a shorted wire and connector. The crew landed safely, then used emergency trim to reset the system after replacing the faulty electrical components.

synopsis: The Japan Transport Safety Board notified the NTSB of a December 16, 2014, accident involving a Boeing 777-200. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the JTSB investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design.
summary: The Japan Transport Safety Board notified the NTSB of a December 16, 2014, accident involving a Boeing 777-200. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the JTSB investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design.

synopsis: Unintentional collision with a deer at night.
summary: During a night landing in visual meteorological conditions, the pilot struck a deer that ran across the runway during rollout. The impact caused substantial damage to the aircraft's right wing spar.

synopsis: The student pilot's loss of airplane control during the landing flare in gusting wind conditions.
summary: A student pilot flying a solo cross-country flight encountered a wind gust during the flare of a cleared stop-and-go landing. She applied forward elevator, causing a hard nosewheel strike and a subsequent go-around attempt that resulted in the aircraft departing the runway and sustaining substantial damage to the nose gear and fuselage.

synopsis: CENIPA notified the NTSB of a September 25, 2014 accident involving a Boeing 737-700. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the CENIPA investigation, which will release all information.
summary: CENIPA notified the NTSB of a September 25, 2014 accident involving a Boeing 737-700. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the CENIPA investigation, which will release all information.

synopsis: The DGCA of Turkey notified the NTSB of an incident involving a Boeing 737-800 on September 29, 2014. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the DGCA investigation, which will release all information.
summary: The DGCA of Turkey notified the NTSB of an incident involving a Boeing 737-800 on September 29, 2014. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the DGCA investigation, which will release all information.

synopsis: The pilot's misjudgment of his helicopter's position relative to a parked helicopter during a pedal turn.
summary: During a hover-taxi and pedal turn in a parking area, the pilot's helicopter tail rotor blade struck a main rotor blade tip of a parked helicopter. The incident caused substantial damage to the tail rotor blade, though the pilot completed the maneuver and landed without further incident or reported mechanical anomalies.

synopsis: The AAIB notified the NTSB of a December 17, 2014, accident involving a Boeing 737-800. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the AAIB investigation, which will release all information.
summary: The AAIB notified the NTSB of a December 17, 2014, accident involving a Boeing 737-800. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the AAIB investigation, which will release all information.

synopsis: The noninstrument-rated pilot's encounter with instrument meteorological conditions (IMC) while maneuvering, which resulted in a loss of airplane control due to spatial disorientation. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's decision to attempt to descend into an area of widespread IMC.
summary: A noninstrument-rated private pilot flying a personal cross-country flight entered instrument meteorological conditions without a weather briefing. The pilot likely became spatially disoriented while maneuvering to locate the airport, lost control, and impacted a hill.

synopsis: The pilot's improper flare during a water landing.
summary: The pilot and passenger conducted a local seaplane flight involving water takeoffs and landings. During the landing approach, the pilot misjudged flare height due to a lack of visual reference on the water, resulting in a hard landing that damaged the left forward float strut and lower frame tube.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to continue flight below the minimum descent altitude without visually acquiring the runway and his delayed and improperly executed missed approach procedure in instrument meteorological conditions.
summary: A private pilot conducting a business flight continued an unstabilized approach in instrument meteorological conditions below minimums. The aircraft impacted a wooded area after the pilot likely descended below minimum descent altitude without visual reference and failed to execute a timely missed approach.

synopsis: A commercial pilot and six passengers died when a Cessna T207A, operated by Aerolineas Alas De Colombia, collided with mountainous terrain during a VFR flight from Palonegro to Malaga. The aircraft was destroyed by impact forces with no postcrash fire, and the investigation remains under Colombian jurisdiction.
summary: A commercial pilot and six passengers died when a Cessna T207A, operated by Aerolineas Alas De Colombia, collided with mountainous terrain during a VFR flight from Palonegro to Malaga. The aircraft was destroyed by impact forces with no postcrash fire, and the investigation remains under Colombian jurisdiction.

synopsis: The pilot's inadequate control of the airplane during the landing roll, which resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot reported that during the landing roll at the original departure airport, the airplane veered left after braking, departed the runway, and nosed over inverted. Post-accident examination found no mechanical failures, and the pilot attributed the incident to a need for better braking control.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to see and avoid the other airplane, which resulted in a midair collision while both airplanes were on final approach to land. The other pilot's failure to see and avoid the airplane, which resulted in a midair collision while both airplanes were on final approach to land.
summary: A Piper PA-28-140 and a Pitts Special S-1S collided midair on short final approach while both were on visual approaches to the same runway. The Pitts, which lacked a radio, struck the Piper from behind and above, causing the Pitts to crash and the Piper to land with substantial damage.

synopsis: A main rotor stall due to low rotor rpm, which resulted in an uncontrolled descent into terrain. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's delayed remedial action.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot were killed and injured when their helicopter impacted terrain during a practice autorotation. The accident likely resulted from a main rotor stall caused by premature collective application, compounded by a non-standard procedure of reducing throttle to idle.

synopsis: The State Commission on Aircraft Accident Investigation of Poland notified the NTSB of an incident involving a Boeing 757-236 on December 17, 2014. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the Polish commission.
summary: The State Commission on Aircraft Accident Investigation of Poland notified the NTSB of an incident involving a Boeing 757-236 on December 17, 2014. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation, with all information to be released by the Polish commission.

synopsis: The Indonesian National Transportation Safety Committee notified the NTSB of an accident involving an Airbus A320-216 on December 28, 2014. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design for the aircraft engines.
summary: The Indonesian National Transportation Safety Committee notified the NTSB of an accident involving an Airbus A320-216 on December 28, 2014. The NTSB appointed a U.S. Accredited Representative to assist the investigation as the State of Manufacturer and Design for the aircraft engines.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of control following a loss of left engine power for reasons that could not be determined because an examination of the airframe and engine did not reveal any preimpact abnormalities.
summary: A pilot departing a twin-engine airplane experienced a left engine power loss, likely due to carburetor water or ice, causing a loss of control and terrain impact. Investigators could not definitively rule out firefighter water as the source, though weather conditions supported carburetor ice risk.

synopsis: The retraction of the left main landing gear after landing for reasons that could not be determined during postaccident examinations.
summary: The pilot reported a landing gear malfunction after departure where the gear failed to extend despite troubleshooting. Although cleared to land with gear visually confirmed down, the left gear retracted during the landing roll, causing substantial wing spar damage due to an undetermined cause linked to a dirty gear compartment.

synopsis: The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing and collapse of the left main landing gear.
summary: The pilot landed hard at night in visual conditions, causing the left main gear to collapse and substantial fuselage damage. The pilot reported no mechanical issues but noted the airport had non-standard runway lighting, despite his experience with glidepath guidance.

synopsis: The disengagement and subsequent binding of the right tailwheel steering cable, which disabled the rudder system.
summary: Shortly after takeoff, the pilot experienced an uncommanded right turn caused by a bound tailwheel steering cable that disabled the rudder system. The pilot executed an emergency landing, veered off the runway, and impacted a snow berm, resulting in minor landing gear damage.

synopsis: The loss of power to the right engine for reasons that could not be determined during postaccident examination and teardown and the pilot's failure to properly configure the airplane for single-engine flight.
summary: The pilot of a cargo airplane lost engine power shortly after takeoff in snowy conditions and crashed into a residential area. Investigators found no mechanical failures but could not determine if ice ingestion caused the power loss or why the pilot failed to feather the propeller as required.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed to compensate for icing on the airplane's wings and control surfaces during a circling approach, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and impact with terrain.
summary: An airline transport pilot flying a single-engine turboprop cargo flight encountered icing and solid IMC, preventing a climb above 8,500 ft. The aircraft stalled and rolled left during a no-flap circling approach due to inadequate airspeed and ice accumulation, causing the left wing to impact terrain.

aircraft: Mds Fying Llc ZENITH ZODIAC CH 650
synopsis: The inadequate modification of the airplane's canopy latching mechanism, which resulted in the inadvertent opening of the canopy while on final approach to land and a subsequent loss of pitch control.
summary: A private pilot flying an experimental amateur-built airplane experienced an unexpected canopy opening on short final approach due to an inadequate modification of the locking system. The resulting pitch-down rendered the aircraft uncontrollable, causing it to impact the ground in a nose-down attitude.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power during cruise flight for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination and testing did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a helicopter during a local public flight experienced unexplained engine and rotor RPM loss while orbiting. The pilot executed an emergency autorotation landing, resulting in a hard impact that separated the tail, though post-accident examinations found no mechanical anomalies or fuel issues.

synopsis: The noninstrument-rated pilot's continued flight into night instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in his failure to maintain clearance from terrain.
summary: A noninstrument-rated pilot departed a cross-country flight in instrument meteorological conditions and night, later impacting rising terrain while likely attempting to fly under clouds. The accident involved poor decision-making and a positive THC test, though impairment could not be confirmed.

synopsis: The pilot's continued visual flight into instrument meteorological conditions which resulted in an inflight collision with terrain. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's inadequate preflight planning, during which he failed to identify forecasted deteriorating weather conditions along the route of flight.
summary: A pilot conducting a VFR repositioning flight encountered instrument meteorological conditions with low ceilings and visibility, leading to a collision with terrain. The accident resulted from the pilot's failure to identify deteriorating weather during preflight planning before attempting the flight.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to compensate for crosswind conditions during takeoff, which resulted in the loss of directional control and collision with terrain.
summary: The pilot departed a private airstrip in a 15 mph left crosswind, causing the aircraft to drift right and sink after losing ground effect. The tail wheel struck the ground, followed by main gear impact on an irrigation pipe, flipping the airplane inverted and sustaining substantial wing damage.

synopsis: The accidental application of the brakes by the passenger during landing roll which resulted in the airplane nosing over.
summary: During the landing roll of a tailwheel-equipped airplane, the aircraft nosed over and sustained substantial damage to the aft fuselage and tail section. The passenger reported accidentally applying the brakes, while the pilot noted no preimpact mechanical malfunctions.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to properly set the left engine fuel selector before takeoff and to recognize the incorrect setting during the flight, which resulted in fuel starvation and a loss of engine power on both engines.
summary: A commercial pilot flying a twin-engine aircraft at night experienced dual engine failure due to fuel starvation caused by leaving the left fuel selector in the crossfeed position. The pilot likely failed to reset the valve during a rushed preflight, resulting in both engines drawing from the right tank until exhaustion, leading to a crash short of the airport.

synopsis: The pilot's failure to maintain control of the helicopter while landing which resulted in a tailrotor ground strike and collision with terrain.
summary: A pilot flying a rented helicopter with two passengers rolled the aircraft onto its left side while attempting to land on a mountain ridge dirt road. The accident occurred when the helicopter pitched aft, spun uncontrollably despite full left pedal, and lost power, resulting in substantial damage to the tail rotor and boom.

synopsis: The helicopter's contact with the landing pad during a rejected landing.
summary: The pilot attempted to land a helicopter on a landing cart in variable winds with a developing tailwind. The aircraft slid, struck the cart with its tail boom stinger, and nosed over onto its side, causing substantial damage to the tail boom, fuselage, and rotor system.

synopsis: On December 29, 2014, a Cessna 172S (VH-PFT) carrying a pilot and passenger collided with water near Port Arthur, Australia, during an aerial photography flight. The aircraft was substantially damaged, and both occupants were fatally injured.
summary: On December 29, 2014, a Cessna 172S (VH-PFT) carrying a pilot and passenger collided with water near Port Arthur, Australia, during an aerial photography flight. The aircraft was substantially damaged, and both occupants were fatally injured.

synopsis: The pilot's improper approach to landing and his failure to perform a go-around, which resulted in a runway overshoot, and collision with a fence.
summary: The pilot overshot the approach during arrival in light, variable winds and failed to initiate a go-around. The aircraft landed left of the runway, struck a perimeter fence, and sustained substantial wing damage with no reported mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's improper fuel planning, which resulted in a loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: The pilot reported an engine power loss 3 miles from the destination, causing a forced landing where the aircraft struck power lines and sustained substantial damage. Fuel gauges indicated low fuel, but post-accident examination found no fuel in the system and no engine mechanical failures.

synopsis: The pilot's loss of directional control during the landing roll.
summary: A pilot flying a personal cross-country flight landed southbound on a sloped runway to follow prevailing traffic. While braking, the left wheel struck unidentified debris, causing a loss of directional control that veered the aircraft off the runway and damaged the left wing.

synopsis: The pilot's decision to maneuver the airplane at low altitude resulting in the airplane impacting power lines.
summary: The pilot departed for a local flight and struck power lines while maneuvering at low altitude to overfly people on the ground. The impact separated both ailerons and wing portions, causing the aircraft to roll and crash near the runway upon landing due to the pilot's inability to see the wires because of sun glare.

synopsis: A total loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined during postaccident examinations and testing.
